Affliction league was a challenge league. It launched on December 8, 2023 as part of Path of Exile: Affliction in version 3.23.0. It ended on March 26, 2024.

== League mechanic ==
Players explore the Viridian Wildwood and use the power of sacred wisps to burn away and discover the secrets of the Affliction shrouding the forest in darkness. Train alongside powerful Azmeri and unlock the power of Wildwood ascendancy classes.
Freeing wisps trapped in the Wildwood will cause them to escape into the overworld, empowering monsters and improving their rewards.

== Ladders ==
In Affliction league, players could choose to enable any of these optional game modes:

Hardcore (HC)
Solo Self-Found (SSF)
Ruthless (R)
This means that there were eight distinct ladders for Affliction league:

Affliction league
HC Affliction league
SSF Affliction league
HC SSF Affliction league
R Affliction league
HC R Affliction league
SSF R Affliction league
HC SSF R Affliction  league

== Items ==
Central to the Affliction league content were new types of items, each associated with a different Wildwood ascendancy class:
title: Affliction league

text:
Charms functioned like very powerful jewels that could be used by the Wildwood Primalist. They were removed from the game at the end of the league.
Tinctures, utilised by the Warden of the Maji, could be equipped in flask slots. One tincture could be activated at a time to grant bonuses to the character's weapons. These were also removed from the game at the end of the league, but later reworked and added to the core game
Corpse items produced special monster corpses, which synergised in various ways with the Warlock of the Mists. These were later added to Ritual rewards in version 3.25.
Omens, first featured in Ancestor league, made a return in Affliction league with new 2D artwork. These could drop from Omen Cairns in the Viridian Wildwood. At the end of the league, omens were incorporated into the favours offered by Ritual encounters.

text:
Ailments are a type of debuff associated and applied by one or more damage types. Ailments normally distinguish themselves from other debuffs by being applied by hits, which allows them to check conditions on the enemy, and vary their effect or duration based on damage instead of having a predetermined value from a skill or modifier.
Frozen, ignited, and shocked are the default ailments of cold, fire, and lightning damage respectively. Critical strikes with those elements have a 100% chance to deal their respective ailments. Brittle, scorched, and sapped are the respective alternate ailments.

== List of ailments ==
Ignite, chill, freeze, shock, scorch, brittle, and sap are referred to as elemental ailments because they are associated with elemental damage types. Bleeding and poison are non-elemental ailments.

=== Damaging ailments ===
Damaging ailments are those that deal damage over time. Bleeding, poison and ignite are damaging ailments. The remaining ailments—chill, freeze, shock, scorch, brittle and sap—are non-damaging ailments.

=== Application by damaging hits ===
Ailments are typically applied by hits comprised of their associated damage types.
Each ailment is associated with one or more damage types. A damaging hit can inflict any ailments associated with the types of damage dealt. For example, a hit of physical and fire damage can inflict bleed, poison and ignite. (However, each ailment's damage/non-damaging effect magnitude is based on only the damage value of the damage types that inflicted it.) Bleed has an additional restriction: it can only be applied by attacks.
The damage type associations for ailments may be changed by specific effects, for example:

text:
=== Non-damaging ailments and ailment threshold ===
Non-damaging ailments have the magnitude of their effect (or their duration, in the case of freeze) calculated based on the hit's damage divided by the enemy's ailment threshold. The exact formula depends on the ailment type.
Each non-damaging ailment type also has a minimum and maximum effect: an ailment that would fall below the minimum effect is discarded and not applied, while an ailment that would exceed the maximum effect is capped at that value.
In the great majority of cases, the ailment threshold is the same as the monster's maximum life. It primarily differs for endgame bosses (such as the Shaper) and other high-life monsters, where the threshold is reduced to allow ailments to be applied with hits that wouldn't ordinarily reach the required life thresholds. Ailment threshold has a maximum of approximately 800 million.
The magnitude (or effect) of a non-damaging ailment is dependent on the damage the enemy takes from the hit, not the base damage of the hit. Sources of increased non-damaging ailment effect lower the damage required to apply a certain magnitude of an ailment, but cannot cause an effect to exceed its cap.
Non-damaging ailments that are applied by non-damaging means will use these default magnitudes unless otherwise stated (this can be verified by viewing the detailed modifier tooltip):

Chill - 10% reduced action speed
Shock - 15% increased damage taken
Scorch - -10% to elemental resistances
Brittle - +2% to critical strike chance against afflicted target
Sap - 6% less damage dealt
title: Ailment

text:
=== Damage with ailments ===
Ignite, bleed and poison are damaging ailments. A damaging ailment deals damage over time based on the flat damage (base and added damage, plus conversion) of the hit that inflicts the ailment, modified by modifiers for damage over time. This calculation is not based on final hit damage, so that stats like #% increased fire damage or enemy resistance do not modify ailment damage twice. 
Only damage types capable of inflicting a damaging ailment contribute to the damage-per-second value for that ailment. From a previous example, a hit of physical and fire damage can potentially inflict bleed, poison and ignite. In this example, only the fire portion of the base damage is considered for ignite.

However, inflicting damaging ailments with base damage of a different type is treated similar to converting damage. For example, ignite damage contributed by fire damage converted from physical damage will remember to include #% increased/more Physical Damage modifiers in its calculation. However, the ignite itself is always considered fire damage over time, and will not scale with physical damage over time modifiers, or the enemy's modifiers for physical damage taken.
Damage with hits and damage with ailments are calculated separately and have different modifiers:
title: Ailment

text:
Modifiers to damage with ailments do not contribute to the damage of attacks or spells. Similarly, modifiers to attack damage and spell damage do not affect damage with ailments.
Modifiers to damage with weapons, melee damage, projectile damage and area damage do not apply to ailments under any circumstances.
Modifiers to damage with ailments, damage over time modifiers, and generic damage modifiers all apply to damaging ailments.
Modifiers to damage with specific ailments apply only to those ailments. Damage type modifiers apply to ailments that deal those types of damage.
Additionally, burning damage modifiers apply to ignite, since 'burning damage' simply means fire damage over time.
Resistances and non-armour sources of damage reduction apply to damage of the corresponding types dealt by ailments.
The defender's damage mitigation does not interact with the attacker's damage conversion or X can inflict Y. For example, an ignite that was inflicted with cold damage converted to fire damage, or Your Cold Damage can Ignite, is mitigated by the defender's fire resistance but not their cold resistance.

==== Critical strikes ====
Damaging ailments from critical strikes gain a bonus +50% damage over time multiplier, which stacks additively with other sources of damage over time multiplier. Critical strikes do not directly affect ailment damage otherwise, though it's possible for mechanics to change this:

title: All Hands

text:
== Mechanics ==
All Hands adds a 40% chance to encounter a random master when a master mission is not selected on the map device, increasing it to 50% chance to encounter a random master. This 50% value is split evenly between the four masters by default using a weighting system of 1:1:1:1 for Einhar/Niko/Alva/Jun respectively, and can be modified by the notables that affect randomly encountered Masters in your Maps have #% increased chance to be a specific Master (Hunting Season, Mining Partnership, Archaeology Tour, and Covert Stakeouts), skewing a 12.5% chance to encounter a specific master to 20%. 
It also disables the ability to gain a master mission on completing a map. Note that while this disables the gaining of Kirac missions, it does not enable Kirac to be encountered in a map.
Modifiers to chance to grant an additional Master Mission on Map Completion instead apply to chance for that Master to be randomly encountered in your Maps at 150% of their value causes passives that read Your Maps have #% chance to grant an additional (Einhar/Niko/Alva/Jun) Mission on Completion to apply a flat chance instead to encounter that master. This means that 10% to gain a specific master's mission is translated into 15% chance for that specific master to be randomly encountered, stacking additively with the 50% above. Each master can gain up to 10% mission chance on the tree (12% with Wandering Path), or 15% (18%) chance to encounter a master in a map. By investing into multiple masters to get a total of  ≥34% mission chance across the four masters, it is possible to encounter ran
title: All Hands

15% (18%) chance to encounter a master in a map. By investing into multiple masters to get a total of  ≥34% mission chance across the four masters, it is possible to encounter random masters in every map.

text:
== Mechanics ==
Outcomes are determined using a weight system, where all item outcomes of the same tier have the same weight.
Ancient Orbs can only roll unique items into a different unique item in the core drop pool (e.g. not drop-restricted).
Ancient Orbs cannot be used on unique non-equipment items (Strongboxes, Vaal side areas).
The resulting item will always be different than the original item.

=== Item level mechanics ===
Unlike the Orb of ChanceOrb of ChanceStack Size: 20Upgrades a normal item to a random rarityRight click this item then left click a normal item to apply it., Ancient Orbs are influenced by the base item's item level to determine the possible outcomes. In general, the item level must be equal to or higher than the drop level of the unique item; if no drop level is specified, this typically matches the unique's level requirement. Base items under ilvl 40 are treated as if the item is ilvl 40; this means that obtaining an item level 2 base item can roll any uniques for that item category and size that has a drop level of 40 or under. Arbitrary Tenets is an Atlas passive skill and Atlas keystone, specifically for the Ritual league encounter.

== Mechanics ==
Arbitrary Tenets causes Favours at Ritual Altars in your maps to randomly cost between 90% less and 80% more. These cost alterations are retained on deferred Rewards.
As an example, something which costed 1000 Tribute before now has a range of 100 to 1800 Tribute with this Atlas keystone allocated.
This averages out to 95% (950 in this case) of the Tribute costs, technically a net benefit overall as long as the player has sufficient tribute to account for the higher variability.

== Location ==
As of version 3.22.0, it is located near the center-left of the Atlas passive skill tree inside the Ritual cluster containing Profitable Prayers and Flexible Dogma.

Area of effect (often referred to as AoE) refers to mechanics (such as skills, auras, and monster abilities) that apply to an area of the ground (rather than targeting a particular character, monster, etc.).
Many AoE mechanics deal damage, but AoE mechanics can have other effects. == How modifiers to AoE sizes work ==
Support gems and other mechanics can increase or decrease the size of an area of effect, almost always by a percentage, e.g. 30% increased Area of Effect. These percentages refer to the total amount of ground covered by the area of effect, not to the area of effect's radius, diameter, or other dimensions. For example, a 100% increased Area of Effect modifier applied to Shock NovaShock NovaSpell, AoE, Lightning, NovaLevel: (1-20)Cost: (12-23) ManaCast Time: 0.70 secCritical Strike Chance: 6.00%Effectiveness of Added Damage: (140-190)%AoE Radius: 26 / 14Requires Level 28Casts a ring of Lightning around you, followed by a larger Lightning nova. Each effect hits enemies caught in their area with Lightning Damage.Deals (34-537) to (101-1610) Lightning Damage+10% to Maximum Effect of ShockRing always Shocks  Additional Effects From 1-20% Quality:  +(0.5-10)% to Maximum Effect of ShockPlace into an item socket of the right colour to gain this skill. Right click to remove from a socket.'s circular area of effect will double the area of ground covered by the circle. The mathematics of that mean that the circle's radius and diameter will increase by around 40%.
If multiple percentage-based modifiers apply to the same area of effect, they add together. For example, if 40% increased Area of Effect, 20% increased Area of Effect, and 30% decreased Area of Effect modifiers all apply to the same area of effect, the area of effect's size will increase by 30% (40+20-30).

text:
== Mechanics ==
Armour grants physical damage reduction against hits, with the exact amount of damage reduction depending on the relative magnitude of the character's armour value and the physical damage of the hit. If the armour value is significantly larger than the damage, most of that damage is prevented. If the armour value is similar to or less than the incoming damage, only a small percentage of that damage will be prevented. For some numeric examples of how damage reduction changes based on armour, see the rule of thumb section later on this page.
As a result armour is more effective against many smaller hits than fewer larger hits, even if both scenarios represent the same total damage in the same amount of time. For a character with extreme investment in armour, what is considered a 'smaller hit' (receiving 75% damage reduction) can be 5000 damage or more. A character with only a minor investment in armour will encounter the limiting case where the damage reduction is very low (less than 5%) and the maximum damage that armour can prevent per hit is only one fifth of the armour value.
Armour never mitigates damage over time, as armour only applies to hits. Bleed is an ailment that deals physical damage over time that is based on the initial physical damage of an attack or spell; armour will reduce the initial hit but not the damage over time. However, both the initial hit and the damage over time can be mitigated with sources of #% additional Physical Damage Reduction, such as endurance charges or the suffix of Numbingof NumbingSuffix(3-4)% additional Physical Dama
title: Armour

text:
ver time can be mitigated with sources of #% additional Physical Damage Reduction, such as endurance charges or the suffix of Numbingof NumbingSuffix(3-4)% additional Physical Damage Reduction found on some body armours that require strength to equip. Physical damage reduction is capped at 90%. The statsheet physical damage reduction combines Armour and Physical Damage Reduction values, making it unreliable for calculating effective damage reduction.
Normally, armour will only grant damage reduction against physical hits, not elemental or chaos damage. However, with the Transcendence keystone or other items (e.g Doryani's PrototypeDoryani's PrototypeSaint's HauberkArmour: (1107-1488)Energy Shield: (190-255)Movement Speed: -5%Requires Level 67, 109 Str, 94 Int(150-200)% increased Armour and Energy Shield+(60-90) to maximum LifeDeal no Non-Lightning DamageArmour also applies to Lightning Damage taken from HitsLightning Resistance does not affect Lightning Damage takenNearby Enemies have Lightning Resistance equal to yours"This was the first step in some grand design,lost to the ages, now ours to decipher."- Dominus, High Templar) or passives (e.g. Juggernaut), armour can apply to non-physical hits. In cases where armour mitigates multiple types of damage, it does so separately for each type it mitigates. If you make armour apply to lightning damage as well as physical damage, then take a hit containing both physical and lightning damage, then armour will calculate Physical Damage Reduction based on comparing the physical damage to armour, and apply that only to the physical d

ing both physical and lightning damage, then armour will calculate Physical Damage Reduction based on comparing the physical damage to armour, and apply that only to the physical damage, and will calculate Lightning Damage Reduction based on comparing the lightning damage to armour, and apply that only to the lightning damage.
In the order of damage mitigation, damage reduction from armour is calculated after damage shifts and resistances (if applicable), but before modifiers to damage taken and spell suppression.

text:
=== Rule of thumb ===
To prevent one third of damage (33%), you need armour 2.5 times the damage (e.g. 250 armour for 100 damage)
To prevent half of damage (50%), you need armour 5 times the damage (e.g. 500 armour for 100 damage)
To prevent two thirds of damage (66%), you need armour 10 times the damage (e.g. 1000 armour for 100 damage)
To prevent three quarters of damage (75%), you need armour 15 times the damage (e.g. 1500 armour for 100 damage)
To prevent 90% of damage, you need armour 45 times the damage (e.g. 4500 armour for 100 damage)
When the damage of a hit significantly exceeds Armour, it will never prevent more damage than its value divided by 5 (e.g. 1000 armour will never prevent more than 200 damage at its minimum percentage prevention).

=== Armour on monsters ===
Monsters also have armour values. The general amount of armour on monsters will increase as monster level increases, with monster types like stone golems and zombies having relatively high amounts of armour compared to hellions or sea witches. Boss monsters similarly increase in armour rating throughout the campaign. For example, Malachai, The Nightmare has 783 armour, while early map bosses such as Piety the Empyrean can have around 7000 armour depending on map level. Endgame bosses such as The Elder or Sirus, Awakener of Worlds have over 20000 and 32000 armour respectively.

== Formulas ==

The amount of physical damage reduction is a function of armour rating and the physical damage taken.

Armour Recombinator is a recombinator currency item that was introduced in the Sentinel League. They can be used to combine two armour items, merging the modifiers into a single item, inheriting one of the item bases at random. They were occasionally available as a random drop from Sentinel reward types.
Recombinators can be used to create many otherwise impossible items by the merging of modifiers. Fractured and Crafted modifiers are able to be moved and retain their status, allowing multiple of them to exist on an item simultaneously. Additionally, Armour Recombinators can occasionally add special modifiers.

text:
Ascendancy classes are subclasses for each character class that grant access more powerful and specialized passive skills. Upon completing the Labyrinth for the first time, the player can choose an Ascendancy class for their character, granting them access to the Ascendancy class' passive tree. Ascendancy passives require Ascendancy skill points to allocate, which are earned by completing the Labyrinth in various difficulties.

== Overview ==
Choosing an Ascendancy class after completing the Labyrinth for the first time allows the player to access a new Ascendancy skill tree specific to the class chosen. Each character class comes with three associated Ascendancy classes (except for Scion, who only has two) for a total of 20 Ascendancy classes. 
The first time the player completes a version of the Labyrinth, the player will receive two Ascendancy skill points to allocate in the ascendancy skill tree. The first three Labyrinths can be unlocked via playing through the Acts, resulting in six Ascendancy skill points. Two more skill points are unlocked when the Eternal Labyrinth, which requires an Offering to the GoddessOffering to the GoddessIt is time for the Goddess to give her final verdict.Your fate rests in her even hands.Travel to the Aspirants' Plaza and spend this item to open the Eternal Labyrinth. to access (note that the Eternal Labyrinth does not have any Trials of Ascendancy as prerequisites), is completed, which means players can spend a total of eight Ascendancy skill points.

== Ascendancy skill tree ==
title: Ascendancy class

text:
The Ascendancy skill tree is a small skill tree that a character has access to when the Labyrinth has been completed. Each Ascendancy class has its own tree. It functions similarly to the larger passive skill tree; the player earns Ascendancy skill points, which can be spent on allocating nodes granting passive bonuses. The Ascendancy skill tree is shown on the regular passive skill tree in a tab near the character's starting location.

=== Layout ===
Ascendancy passive skills are significantly more powerful than regular passive skills and will heavily impact the way a character is played. A character can only spend a maximum of eight points on the tree; however, the last two points are not available until significantly later when end-game maps can be cleared. Aside from the Ascendant's, the skill trees also follow a certain format. Most classes have 12 to 16 passive skills in each tree, and each potent "notable" skill is gated by a generic, lesser node, so it takes two points to reach them. Certain notables require the player to allocate another notable first, so they take up four points. A character will only be able to have one four-pointer skill until the Eternal Labyrinth is cleared.
title: Ascendancy class

text:
==== Scion ====
The Scion's Ascendancy classes follow a different format: some notables on the Ascendant and the Reliquarian have two minor passive requisites, resulting in the class having up to three notables with all 8 Ascendancy passive points. In a typical setup, the Ascendant will have up to two class notables and one notable that grants them a second starting point, and the Reliquarian can have one armour notable, one weapon notable, and one jewelry notable. Due to the tree layout, the Scion won't have an Ascendancy notable until Cruel Labyrinth. and the Ascendant won't be able to gain a second starting point until Merciless Labyrinth.

=== Refunding ===
Refunding one Ascendancy skill point requires five regular refund points, or 5 times as much gold if using Respcialisation. When all points are refunded, use the Altar of Ascendancy in the Labyrinth treasure room in any difficulty to select a new Ascendancy class.
Some notable passives such as the Scion notables have multiple attached choices for that passive, which you can select only one of. You can refund these passives and choose a different option without having to refund the passives connected to the main passive.

== Bloodline Ascendancy classes ==
title: Ascendancy class

text:
Bloodline Ascendancy classes are secondary Ascendancy classes that are unlocked by completing certain endgame bosses or encounters. 
They are not specific to any character class and do not affect your character's usual Ascendancy class. Bloodline Ascendancy passives also require Ascendancy skill points to allocate, sharing these points between the regular and Bloodline Ascendancy class. Bloodline Ascendancy classes offer a smaller amount of passives than regular Ascendancy classes, preventing a character from completely specializing into one.
When switching to a different Bloodline Ascendancy, all points on your current Bloodline passive tree will be refunded for free.

text:
The Atlas of Worlds is Path of Exile's end-game content system. The Atlas is a series of linked areas that players can progress through after completing the quest A Call to Arms for Commander Kirac. The Atlas is revealed and explored by running map items within a Map Device.
The Atlas of Worlds represents a visualisation of potential realities (referred to as "dreams") visited by opening map items. The Atlas is comprised 100 different standard maps split among four quadrants, with each map being connected to each other by paths, as well as dozens of additional areas accessed via unique maps, map fragments or miscellaneous map items.

== Overview ==
title: Atlas of Worlds

text:
=== Running Maps ===
As part of the quest A Call to Arms given by Commander Kirac, the player is given a Map (Tier 1)Map (Tier 1)Monster Level: 68Travel to a Map by using this in a personal Map Device. Maps can only be used once. of Magic quality. After acquiring this map item, the player can use it in a map device to open a map area. Clicking the map device will open the Atlas Screen. Initially, only the centre of the Atlas, with the beginning paths of the four quadrants, are shown. The four visible areas connected to the center of the Atlas are all accessible via this tier 1 map, as all four of those areas are Tier 1 by default. Selecting one of the four areas will open the interface and allow you to place the map item inside (there are also spaces for map enhancers, discussed in more detail on that page). After placing a map of at least that area's tier inside and selecting "Activate", portals will open leading to the area. Your character can enter the portals to fight the monsters and loot the treasure inside. A Call to Arms is completed by defeating the Boss of the area you entered.
title: Atlas of Worlds

text:
=== Progressing Through the Atlas ===
After defeating the boss of the map opened for A Call to Arms, Commander Kirac will reward the player with a Map Device hideout decoration, which can be placed in the player's hideout to have a personally accessible map device. Completing one of the Tier 1 areas will reveal the areas connected to that area via paths. These connected area (or areas) will be Tier 2- requiring the player to acquire a Map (Tier 2)Map (Tier 2)Monster Level: 69Travel to a Map by using this in a personal Map Device. Maps can only be used once. or higher to access.
Normal map items are divided into 16 tiers:

Tiers 1 through 5 are marked "White"
Tiers 6 through 10 are marked "Yellow"
Tiers 11 through 16 are marked "Red"
Revealing and progressing through the Atlas involves completing a map area by defeating the map's boss, which will reveal any maps directly connected to that map. Each quadrant of the Atlas contains 25 connected normal maps, as well as several unique maps and other special areas.

=== Bonus Objectives and Atlas Passive Points ===

Many areas on the Atlas (including all normal maps) have bonus objectives- for example, white (tier 1-5) maps have the bonus objective of killing the area boss while in a magic or higher rarity version of the map. Completing this bonus objective awards a skill point for the Atlas Passive Skill Tree, which enhances the difficulty and rewards of the areas accessed via the Atlas of Worlds. The player can check bonus objective completion by hovering the cursor over an area.

== Atlas Endgame ==
title: Atlas of Worlds

text:
Each of the four quadrants leads to different Pinnacle bosses, who, upon defeat, will drop Voidstones. These items are powerful tools that can be slotted into the four corners of the Atlas to modify the four quadrants, increasing the tier of areas in that quadrant to 16 and providing bonuses to certain mechanics and drops from that quadrant (including a chance to drop Nightmare maps).

== Area-Specific Mechanics ==

=== Divination cards ===

All areas on the Atlas have specific divination cards whose drops are tied to that area. Holding Alt over a map on the Atlas will display what area-specific divination cards can drop from that area. Some divinations cards do not drop unless the map's tier (or more specifically, drop level, which factors in a monster's rarity or other modifiers) is high enough.

=== Scrying ===

The Nameless Seer has a chance to appear after defeating monster packs in Tier 16 areas on the Atlas of Worlds. He acts as a special merchant with two functions:
title: Atlas of Worlds

text:
The Seer will offer a selection of unique itmes, allowing the player to take one item for free.
The Seer will also offer the ability to scry an area. Scrying an area allows you to override the natural divination card drops of any other non-unique area on the atlas with the card drops of the area the Seer was found in. This function only works one way: the current map's cards are unaffected. A map can only be involved in one scrying pair at once, regardless of whether it is the donor or recipient. A scrying pair can be removed using a Orb of ScouringOrb of ScouringStack Size: 30Removes all modifiers from an itemRight click this item then left click on a magic or rare item to apply it. on the Atlas of Worlds, or by overwriting an existing scrying pair through another Nameless Seer.
It is suggested that the effects of scrying apply to the player character, rather than to the Atlas/map. Consequentially, the character that kills the enemy or otherwise causes items to drop will determine the pool of divination cards that can naturally drop.

== League progress transfer ==
When the current league ends the progress on the Atlas of Worlds is transferred to the relevant parent league. The parent league is generally Standard or Hardcore.
If your account has previously acquired any Voidstones, completing any node on the Atlas will complete every node of the same tier and lower.

Progressing through maps allows the player to obtain passive skill points to allocate in the Atlas tree to enhance the rewards and fights of maps within the Atlas of Worlds.

text:
=== Spending and refunding passive skill points ===
Immediately after receiving Atlas passive skill points, the player has the opportunity to spend those points in the skill tree. If the player leaves the points unassigned, they can be spent later from the Atlas of Worlds screen.
Like with the character's normal passive skill tree, the player can spend Atlas refund point or GoldGoldStack Size: 50000Can be spent at Vendors to remove previously-assigned passive skills. An Orb of UnmakingOrb of UnmakingStack Size: 40Grants an atlas passive skill refund pointRight click on this item to use it. grants one Atlas refund point when used, and Atlas Book of Skill quest items grant 2 Atlas refund points (total of 12 per character). Commander Kirac offers Atlas Respecialisation to respec Atlas skills for 2000 Gold per skill point, and also sells Orbs of Unmaking for 2 Orb of RegretOrb of RegretStack Size: 40Grants a passive skill refund pointRight click on this item to use it. each. 
Once earned, these refund points can be used in any of the allocated atlas passive nodes. Refund points for the Atlas tree cannot be used to remove passive skills from the character's passive skill tree, and vice-versa. Atlas respec points are capped at 65,535; obtaining any more will cause an overflow error and reset to 0.

=== Additional atlas trees ===
Upon completing 50 and 100 bonus objectives on regular T1-16 maps, players unlock an additional atlas tree, allowing quick changing of passives when opening a map without needing to respec points. Atlas respec points are shared between all atlas trees.
title: Atlas Passive Skill Tree

text:
== Passive nodes ==
There are several types of atlas passive skills.

=== Small passives ===

Small atlas passive skills grant minor bonuses related to atlas content.

=== Notable passives ===

Notable atlas passive skills grant notable bonuses related to atlas content.

=== Keystone passives ===

Keystone atlas passive skills significantly alter how certain atlas or league mechanics work.

=== Gateways ===
Gateways allow you to traverse to the opposite side of the Atlas to the other connected Gateway. Both gateways must have points allocated to them in order to traverse between then.

== Version history ==
The Atlas Passive Skill Tree was first introduced in the Echoes of the Atlas expansion, which consisted of smaller sub-trees that only applied to specific maps within an Atlas region. Siege of the Atlas reworked the Atlas passive tree into a single, global passive tree.

text: Awakener's Orb is a currency item. Using it on a "donor" item destroys the item, and allows the player to apply the item's influence to another "receiver" item of the same item class. The second item is then reforged as a rare item with both influence types and new modifiers. In most cases, a single influenced modifier from the donor item is preserved along with a single influenced modifier from the target item. All other mods are randomly rerolled.
title: Awakener's Orb

text:
== Mechanics ==
Awakener's orbs are spent by right-clicking the orb, left-clicking a donor item, and then left-clicking a target item. The two items must be of the same item type, with different influences. Each item must have exactly one influence. The target item's base type, item level, sockets, links, quality and enchantments are retained. The reforging of the target item will ignore Mastercrafting Metamods like Suffixes Cannot Be Changed.
Influence is written/shown in a fixed order from left to right, regardless of the donor/target. In other words, a hunter item donating into a redeemer item arranges the icons the same as a redeemer item donating into a hunter item. The influence icons on the item follow the following order: Shaper > Elder > Crusader > Redeemer > Hunter > Warlord.
One influenced mod (such as a "Shaper's" prefix, or an "Of the Elder" suffix) from each item is guaranteed to merge on the new item, except the case that the two mods are from the same mod group (see paragraph below). The retained mods can be both prefixes, suffixes, or a combination. If an item has two or more influenced mods, one will be selected at random during the merging process.
Notably, some mods (such as Elder and Redeemer Flasks applied to you have #% increased Effect, Shaper and Redeemer x% reduced Mana Reserved, etc.) are mutually exclusive and one will be discarded at random. This exclusivity rule appears to depend on the ModGroup attribute found on datamined websites such as poedb.tw and POE wiki (e.g. all curse on hit explicit mods on ring are in group "CurseOnHitLevel" as show
title: Awakener's Orb

text:
rs to depend on the ModGroup attribute found on datamined websites such as poedb.tw and POE wiki (e.g. all curse on hit explicit mods on ring are in group "CurseOnHitLevel" as shown in their wiki articles or the mod entries in the wiki that start with Modifier prefix), where the two merged mods cannot share the same ModGroup.  It is unclear whether additional, non-ModGroup exclusivity rules exist as this information is not available within the game client.
Modifiers transferred in this way will retain their modifier tier, but the specific value roll within that tier may change.
It is possible to use an Imprint to roll back the use of an Awakener's Orb. The imprint can only be applied to the recipient item, not the donor item that is destroyed.
It is not possible to use an Awakener's Orb on corrupted items; both the donor item and the base item must be uncorrupted.
Certain aspects of this process are deterministic (as previewed through a Hinekora's LockHinekora's LockStack Size: 10Allows an item to foresee the result of the next Currency item used on itModifying the item in any way removes the ability to foreseeRight click this item then left click an item to apply it.):
title: Awakener's Orb

text:
The influenced modifier kept from the receiver item will never change even if the donor item is changed, regardless of the number of influenced modifiers on the receiver item.
The specific random modifiers rolled are determined by the number of influence prefixes and suffixes on the donor item against a specific receiver item.
If a random modifier rolled on the resulting item is part of the base modifier pool or the receiver item's influence pool, using a different item of a different influence and the same number of influence prefixes/suffixes will almost always result in the same modifier regardless of the donor base used, as long as the number of influence prefixes/suffixes on the donor item are the same.
If a random modifier rolled on the resulting item is part of the donor item's influence pool, using a different item of a different influence and the same number of influence prefixes/suffixes will almost always result in a similar modifier from the new influence pool. For example, if a Crusader 1 influence mod donor causes the result to randomly roll #% increased Intelligence, a Warlord 1 influence mod donor would almost always result in it rolling #% increased Strength instead.

text:
The Bestiary is an interface to classify captured beasts from Wraeclast. It is introduced by Einhar Frey, who is first encountered in Act 2 and who helps the player capture and store beasts in the Menagerie.
Beasts are categorized into different types based on their taxonomic rank, divided by family on each tab of the interface. When a specific species of beast is captured for the first time on an account, a checkmark appears next to the beast's name in the Bestiary. This progress is shared across all characters, including across leagues. 
Note that not all beasts are in the Bestiary, as not all beasts are able to be captured. Several capturable Harvest beasts are currently incorrectly placed under the wrong classification.
To itemize a beast, while in the Menagerie, go to the Captured Beast section in the Bestiary page and press Ctrl+left click on a beast. This will create an Imprinted Bestiary OrbImprinted Bestiary OrbRight-click to add this to your bestiary. containing that beast, which can then be traded to other players.

Bleeding, or bleed, is an ailment that deals physical damage over time to the affected target. Moving targets suffer increased bleeding damage. Only physical damage hits can inflict bleed. There are no sources of global chance to bleed or chance to bleed with spells. Thus, bleed is limited to attack skills only. Bleeding can be Aggravated to cause it to always deal damage as if the target is moving.

== Mechanics ==

=== Infliction ===

text:
=== Damage ===
Bleed deals physical damage over time.
Potential damage from one bleed application is based on the base physical damage of attack that caused it: 70% per second if the target is standing still (reduced to 10% if an enemy monster applied it). If the target is moving or are affected by Aggravated Bleeding, bleeding deals additional damage equal to twice the base, for a total of 3 times the base damage (210% per second) .
By default, only the strongest (the highest damage-per-second) bleed application will actually deal damage at any given time.
If Crimson Dance is allocated, the potential damage of one stack is 35% of the inflicting attack's physical damage, regardless of whether the target is moving or not, and the 8 strongest applications will deal damage at any given time. Sustaining all 8 stacks on a target will thus deal an additional 280% of the attack's average physical damage per second. This effectively quadruples bleed DPS in prolonged fights.
Bleed damage is not reduced by armour, but will be reduced by any other sources of physical mitigation, such as endurance charges or Immortal CallImmortal CallSpell, Duration, GuardLevel: (1-20)Cost: (21-36) ManaCooldown Time: 3.00 secCan Store 1 Use(s)Cast Time: InstantRequires Level 34Take less Physical and Elemental Damage for a short time. text:
=== Duration ===
The base duration of bleed is 5 seconds. This means that by default and before reductions (see above), an attack that causes bleed will deal an additional 350% (70% for 5 seconds) over its full duration to a target that isn't moving. If the target is moving for the full duration, this increases to 1050% (350% * 3). If Crimson Dance is allocated, this additional damage decreases to 175% (350% * 0.5) per stack, regardless of whether the target is moving or not.
Separate applications of bleed do not stack cumulatively (unless Crimson Dance is allocated, then it stacks up to 8 times). Each bleed effect remains present on the target until it runs its course, but only the one with the highest damage per second will cause damage at any given moment. For example, assume an enemy is inflicted with bleed for 100 damage per second, then after 2 seconds it is inflicted with bleed for 50 damage per second. The outcome will be 500 damage over 5 seconds followed by 100 damage over 2 seconds.

text:
=== Aggravate ===
Certain effects cause bleeding to be aggravated. Bleeding that is aggravated deals higher damage, as though the target is moving. Aggravate lasts for the remaining duration of the bleed instance.
When bleeding is aggravated, all instances of bleeding on the target become aggravated. The Chance to Aggravate Bleeding is rolled only once for all instances of bleeding and is applied before the bleeding; therefore, if a hit applies bleeding and aggravates at the same time, that instance of bleeding is not aggravated.
The extra damage from aggravated bleeding is separate from the bleeding's normal damage. A 100 DPS bleed that becomes aggravated deals 100 DPS from the bleed effect and 200 DPS from aggravated bleeding. The aggravated damage from that bleed continues to deal damage as long as it's the highest aggravated bleed damage and the monster is stationary.

text:
Aggravated Bleeding grants the same “extra bleeding damage” bonus as the one applied when an enemy is moving. Because these effects are identical, the bonuses do not stack.

=== Modifiers ===

==== Damage modifiers ====
As a damage over time effect, bleed's damage can be affected positively or negatively by some damage modifiers.
The following modifiers will directly affect the damage of bleed:

Damage
Physical Damage (including physical damage over time multiplier)
Damage over Time
Bleeding Damage
Trap, mine, minion or totem damage modifiers will also affect the damage of bleed if it is applied by a trap, a mine, a minion or a totem respectively.
Also, bleed is non-elemental ailment, so Damage from Ailments modifier will also affect the damage of bleed.
Flat Physical Attack Damage modifiers, being count in base attack damage, also affects bleed damage.
Other modifiers of increased/reduced/more/less type affecting hits (attack, melee, ranged, projectile, etc), as well as any damage modifier specific to the skill, do not apply to bleed.
title: Bleeding

==== Defensive modifiers ====
Damage from bleed cannot be affected by mechanics affecting physical damage from hits, such as Armour or Fortify.
To affect incoming damage from bleed, one need to use global (hits and ailments) or ailment damage reduction modifiers.

text:
Blessed Orb is a currency item that can be used to re-roll values of the implicit modifiers on a piece of equipment. (This means the top values of an item above the line and not the bottom 6 values) This can only be used on an item that actually has implicit modifiers that can have a range of values.

== Mechanics ==
A Blessed Orb re-rolls the implicit modifier of an item. It cannot be used on items without implicit modifiers or whose implicit modifiers do not have a range of values. They can be used on items with special implicits, such as synthesised items items with Eldritch implicit modifiers. They cannot be used to alter implicit modifiers on corrupted items, which prevents the user of Blessed Orbs on it. Because of their limited impact and somewhat uncommon rarity, Blessed Orbs are better used for items that already have desirable explicit modifiers and for meeting stat breakpoints like capped resistances and attribute requirements when needed.
Blessed Orbs can not roll the same implicit value that the original item had. If the current implicit value is low, then on average you have better odds of rolling a high implicit value, and vice versa.
Blessed Orbs can also be used to reroll the implicit values on Expedition Logbooks.
Blessed Orbs can also be used on a map containing an Elder Guardian or a Conqueror to reroll the boss contained in the map.

== Item acquisitionBlessed Orb can drop anywhere. ==

text:
Blighted maps are alternate versions of existing maps that contain a more challenging Blight encounter than is normally found on maps. These maps have all the native monsters removed and are dedicated to the Blight encounter. Blighted maps can be opened by accessing the "Blighted Lands" map area on the Atlas.
The map will always have an alternative map icon, as well as these implicit modifiers:

Natural inhabitants of this area have been removedArea is infested with Fungal GrowthsMap's Item Quantity Modifiers also affect Blight Chest count at 25% valueCan be Anointed up to 3 times

== Item acquisition ==
Blight icon chests from completing Blight encounters in maps have a chance to drop a Blighted version of a map. Blighted map drops are not affected by Cartography Scarabs.

== Mechanics ==

Blighted maps only contain a small area with no enemies and a single Fungal Growth that spawns dozens of roots. Multiple waves of monsters will spawn from monster portals all across the map. Monsters move along a fixed route towards the Purification Pump. The player must defend the Purification Pump for 5 minutes, and then defeat all remaining monsters in order to complete the map and grant the rewards. Compared to regular Blight encounters in maps, in Blighted maps players get extended preparation time and Pump durability (health) is increased to 20 (up from 10).
Similar to regular maps:
title: Blighted map

text:
Blighted maps are available in different tiers, with the highest being Tier 16.
Higher tier maps have tougher monsters and can drop rarer, more valuable rewards.
Can be crafted into Magic or Rare rarities, but it greatly increases the difficulty of combat, compared to Normal rarity maps.
Map rarity affects the reward chests and the central drops.
Map fragments that increase Item Quantity, such as Sacrifice at DuskSacrifice at DuskStack Size: 10Area contains a Vaal Side Area5% increased Quantity of Items found in AreaThe Vaal shall never fear the setting of our sun.Can be used in a personal Map Device to add modifiers to a Map., can be used with Blighted maps.
Blighted maps can be increased in quality using Chisels.
Unlike regular maps:

Blighted maps can also be anointed, adding a variety of unique modifiers, including extra experience and significant boosts to rewards.
Blighted maps cannot be used with scarabs, therefore it won't be consumed.
Atlas passive skills don't apply to Blighted maps.
If you fail the blight encounter, it will not count as a map completion, however you can still collect all chests that have been already spawned.
title: Blighted map

text:
== Strategy ==
Blighted maps have a large amount of enemies and a large amount of resources for tower building. The same strategies that work on smaller Blights in maps will be useful, but more tower building and killing will be involved. They are often easier to complete than encounters in maps as more towers can be built quickly to do massive damage and slow the hordes of enemies when player damage may be too low to clear the mechanic.
The following is recommended:
title: Blighted map

text:
Good use of towers: they can clear the encounter even if the player does no damage
Combos of level 3 Seismic/Chilling and Empowering towers with freeze anoint (Opalescent/Silver oils) to stunlock monsters at chokepoints
Level 4 Meteor towers with burning ground anoint (Indigo/Violet oils) and level 4 Scout/Lightning towers to deal high damage
Level 4 Glacial cage or Stone gaze towers to control enemies that bypass primary chokepoint defences
A long-range projectile or spellcaster build or any build that can do high amounts of area damage (melee builds  without good area of effect will find it hard, as monsters attack the central pump from every direction)
To run Normal blighted maps: At least 2 million damage per second (calculated in Path of Building)
To run Rare blighted maps with difficult modifiers: At least 5-10 million damage per second
A method to increase damage against  Rare and Unique mini bosses (such as Assassin's Mark for crit builds, or Sigil of Power for lightning builds)
Explosions and proliferation are helpful at clearing entire lanes of monsters
Adequate defensive layers
Good armour, evasion, life/energy shield, high block chance, 100% spell suppression, life recoup and regen, physical taken as elemental damage, etc.
Capped elemental resistances (fire, cold and lightning resistance at 75%)
A strict loot filter that filters out most of the inexpensive loot

text:
Blocking is a layer of defense that will entirely prevent damage from an enemy hit unless modified by some outside effect like Glancing Blows. The chance to block is a random roll made for each hit. Characters and most enemies have 0% base block chance; enemies with a shield typically have some chance to block.

== Mechanics ==
Blocking a hit prevents all damage and harmful on-hit effects such as status ailments. Only hits can be blocked; it does nothing against damage over time. Block typically mitigates attack damage and spell damage, though secondary damage can be blocked if it originates from a spell or attack skill. No block chance stat exists against direct secondary damage, such as self-damage or non-skill explosions. 
Blocking has no cooldown and can occur as long as the defender has block chance, including during other actions, while frozen, and while recovering from stun or a previous block. It does not require wielding a shield or a specific weapon type.

=== Chance to block ===
The chance to block is a random roll made per hit; it is not entropy-based like evasion. Block has the following base stats

+75% to maximum Chance to Block Attack Damage
+75% to maximum Chance to Block Spell Damage

=== Reflected damage ===
Reflected damage can be blocked; however blocking reflected damage will not trigger on-block effects.

=== Block duration ===
Because block rolls after other mitigation, the game has already calculated stun by the time a hit is blocked. If a blocked hit would have caused a stun, the blocking animation is played. If it would not have caused a stun, then you get a "free" block with no animation. 
Faster Block and Stun Recovery and Increased Block Recovery modifiers reduce the length of the blocking animation.
The following formula is the complete calculation for the duration of the blocking animation (in milliseconds). If you cannot be stunned, the block animation will never play.

text:
=== Pantheon ===
Soul of the Brine King Major Pantheon power provides the unique modifier You cannot be Stunned if you've been Stunned or Blocked a Stunning Hit in the past 2 seconds. 
The Soul of the Brine King can be upgraded to grant an additional #% increased Stun and Block Recovery.

=== Taking damage from blocked hits ===
The You take #% of Damage from Blocked Hits stat causes block's usual 100% damage prevention to be reduced in efficacy, causing the defender to take damage despite blocking the hit. By default, you take 0% of the damage from blocked hits. If this stat exceeds 100%, the defender will take more damage than would have been taken if the hit was not blocked.
Other than this, the mechanics of block are unchanged. A blocked hit still cannot apply on-hit effects, such as ailments or curses. This modifier does not affect the chance to play the block animation based on the amount of damage taken.
Glancing Blows causes players to take 65% of damage from blocked hits, although it also doubles block chance.

text:
Blocking is a layer of defense that will entirely prevent damage from an enemy hit unless modified by some outside effect like Glancing Blows. The chance to block is a random roll made for each hit. Characters and most enemies have 0% base block chance; enemies with a shield typically have some chance to block.

== Mechanics ==
Blocking a hit prevents all damage and harmful on-hit effects such as status ailments. Only hits can be blocked; it does nothing against damage over time. Block typically mitigates attack damage and spell damage, though secondary damage can be blocked if it originates from a spell or attack skill. No block chance stat exists against direct secondary damage, such as self-damage or non-skill explosions. 
Blocking has no cooldown and can occur as long as the defender has block chance, including during other actions, while frozen, and while recovering from stun or a previous block. It does not require wielding a shield or a specific weapon type.

=== Chance to block ===
The chance to block is a random roll made per hit; it is not entropy-based like evasion. Block has the following base stats

+75% to maximum Chance to Block Attack Damage
+75% to maximum Chance to Block Spell Damage

=== Reflected damage ===
Reflected damage can be blocked; however blocking reflected damage will not trigger on-block effects.

=== Block duration ===
Because block rolls after other mitigation, the game has already calculated stun by the time a hit is blocked. If a blocked hit would have caused a stun, the blocking animation is played. If it would not have caused a stun, then you get a "free" block with no animation. 
Faster Block and Stun Recovery and Increased Block Recovery modifiers reduce the length of the blocking animation.
The following formula is the complete calculation for the duration of the blocking animation (in milliseconds). If you cannot be stunned, the block animation will never play.

=== Pantheon ===
Soul of the Brine King Major Pantheon power provides the unique modifier You cannot be Stunned if you've been Stunned or Blocked a Stunning Hit in the past 2 seconds. 
The Soul of the Brine King can be upgraded to grant an additional #% increased Stun and Block Recovery.

=== Taking damage from blocked hits ===
The You take #% of Damage from Blocked Hits stat causes block's usual 100% damage prevention to be reduced in efficacy, causing the defender to take damage despite blocking the hit. By default, you take 0% of the damage from blocked hits. If this stat exceeds 100%, the defender will take more damage than would have been taken if the hit was not blocked.
Other than this, the mechanics of block are unchanged. A blocked hit still cannot apply on-hit effects, such as ailments or curses. This modifier does not affect the chance to play the block animation based on the amount of damage taken.
Glancing Blows causes players to take 65% of damage from blocked hits, although it also doubles block chance.

text:
Breach content involves otherworldly monsters who have stabilized their interdimensional rift to Wraeclast and have begun constructing hives throughout the land, first introduced in Keepers league. It is the sequel of the original Breach mechanic from Breach league.

== Overview ==
Breaches can be encountered starting from The Mud Flats in Act 6. Players can find Ailith, First of the Keepers near the entrance in The Coast, and will provide an introduction to the mechanic.
Breaches are split into two types: Unstable Breaches and Breach Hives. A Breach encounter will feature either one of these encounters, but never both. In maps, a Hive Fortress has a chance to spawn over Breach Hives. In maps, the chance to encounter a Breach Hive/Unstable Breach/Hive Fortress is approximately 40%/45%/15% respectively The keystones Dimensional Foothold and Enemy at the Gates cause all Breach encounters to be Breach Hives or Unstable Breaches, respectively. Note that Breach Hives/Hive Fortresses have priority over Unstable Breaches, and if either a Hive or Fortress is forced to spawn, it will prevent Unstable Breaches from spawning.
All Breach encounters grant an amount of Hiveblood and a chance for one or more wombgifts to drop on successful completion.

=== Unstable Breach ===
title: Breach

text:
Unstable Breaches appear as a massive Breach Hand. Touching it will open an Unstable Breach, expanding outwards for a duration while Breach monsters will spawn in. Breach monsters are unable to leave the circle. A progress bar will appear with two bars: one that increases based on killing Hiveborn monsters, and one that gradually increases over time. The goal is to fill the bar from killing Hiveborn before the timer catches up, collapsing the Breach encounter prematurely.
Defeating enough Breach monsters to fill up the bar will cause the timer to accelerate to max, forming a Stabilized Breach, stopping the timer and Breach expansion. When this occurs, several Rare Hiveborn monsters (and sometimes in maps, Vruun, Marshal of Xesht) near the location of the Breach Hand that must be defeated to successfully collapse the Stabilized Breach. Note that players are intentionally not expected to be able to stabilize Unstable Breaches during the earlier parts of the campaign.
After the Breach collapses, whether it was stabilized or not, loot will drop in a spiral near the character's current location.

text: === Breach Hive ===
title: Breach

text:
Breach Hives appear as a large breach circle containing Breach monsters and semi-organic structures within them. Before beginning the encounter, players can destroy the Breach walls by approaching them or by hitting them. There are also several Flammable Burrows scattered within the Breach Hive, indicated as faded purple dots on the mini-map. Approaching them will create a large explosion that clears all walls within its radius and cause other nearby flammable burrows within range to explode as well. At the center of the Hive at the core (marked by a Breach hand on the minimap) is a button that will summon Ailith, which begins the encounter where the player must defend her against waves of monsters while she prepares a ritual to destroy the Hive.
Once the encounter begins, walking near the hive walls or attacking them will no longer destroy them. The Hiveborn will spawn from rifts that can reach Ailith, indicated as red dots on the minimap. As you progress through the waves, more of the hive walls may get destroyed. Destroying more of the structure before summoning Ailith will allow more monsters to approach and attack Ailith. Each wave progresses when you kill enough Hiveborn, with every new wave causing a pulse to release from the statue and spawning new enemies and potentially destroying more walls. Hive encounters consist of 5 to 8 waves of enemies.

text:
=== Hive Fortress ===

In any tier of map, a Breach Hive may be replaced with a Hive Fortress, a side area containing more Hiveborn monsters. Hive Fortresses belong to the same instance as the main map. The area contains several "Grasping Coffer" chests that can sometimes contain wombgifts and Foulborn unique items.
In the center of the Hive Fortress, a more difficult version of a Hive encounter can be found. These encounters have 24 waves. During the encounter, additional purple flames (skills and buffs) will spawn once every few waves. Up to 6 purple flames can be held on reserve at a time, so it is recommended to use them liberally.
In addition to purple flame skills found in regular Hive encounters, there is one special skill available at the start:
title: Breach

text:
Destroy the Hive walls around Ailith: Optionally destroys the walls that funnel monsters towards Ailith. This skill is removed if not used by wave 4.
After completing the Hive encounter, the Breach hand will start pulsing, doing physical damage across the whole area in intervals. This damage is affected by map modifiers and can be mitigated or blocked. The player must escape from the Hive Fortress successfully in order to collect their rewards. Hands will emerge from the walls to block off several paths and corridors; these appear in the minimap within a wide radius as a small grey hand icon. There is typically only one route to the outer ring of the arena which then leads directly to the exit, and it is possible to start planning the initial route of escape during the waves.
Escaping successfully will grant a significant amount of Hiveblood and drop several wombgifts and sometimes a Hivebrain GlandHivebrain GlandCountless voices murmur,singing of the Hive...Open a portal to the Hive Colony by using this item in a personal Map Device. text:
Path of Exile uses three main attributes – strength, dexterity, and intelligence – and its seven playable character classes (also called core classes) are each associated with one or more attributes. The player chooses a class for their character in the character creation screen. A newly created character starts its journey through Wraeclast at Twilight Strand. Each character class has a different starting location on the passive skill tree, starting attributes and statistics and quest rewards. Later, upon completing the Labyrinth, players can specialize their character by choosing an Ascendancy subclass. The subclasses available depend on the character class chosen. 
The following stats are the same for all new characters, and gain the same amount per level. Characters start with different accuracy ratings, but all gain 2 base accuracy per level.

50 life and gains additional 12 life per level.
40 mana and gains additional 6 mana per level.
15 evasion rating.
Players can use any items or skills, providing they meet the relevant attribute and level requirements. This gives players the freedom to highly customize their characters and design creative builds with unusual play styles. For new players, however, it is generally easiest to invest in the attributes appropriate to their character class.

== Pure Characters ==
There are three "pure" characters, classes that are aligned with one of the three core attributes. They all start with 32 in their primary attributes and 14 in the other two

=== Strength ===
title: Character class

text:
Strength confers raw brute power, and its character class is the Marauder. He wields maces to deal high physical damage, and Strength armour pieces grant him physical damage reduction. Monsters aligned with Strength generally hit hard and take many blows to defeat. The element aligned with Strength is fire.
The Marauder's Ascendancy classes are Juggernaut, Berserker, and Chieftain.

=== Dexterity ===

Dexterity confers agility in combat, and its character class is the Ranger. She uses bows and rapiers to attack quickly and accurately, and Dexterity armour pieces grant her the ability to evade enemy blows more often. Monsters aligned with Dexterity are nimble and difficult to hit, often attacking from a distance or with multiple weapons. The element aligned with Dexterity is cold.
The Ranger's Ascendancy classes are Deadeye, Warden, and Pathfinder.

=== Intelligence ===

Intelligence confers knowledge – of both arcane magic and deadly combat techniques – and its character class is the Witch. She wields weapons like the wand and sceptre with improved critical strikes, and her Intelligence armour pieces grant the wearer a mystical energy shield which protects them from damage and can recharge when they are out of combat. Monsters aligned with intelligence are often spell-casters who can be dangerous if not immediately dealt with. The element aligned with Intelligence is lightning.
The Witch's Ascendancy classes are Necromancer, Elementalist, and Occultist.
title: Character class

text:
== Hybrid Characters ==
There are four "hybrid" character classes in Path of Exile that use a combination of attributes. The Scion starts with 20 in each stats, while the other three start with 23 in each of their main attributes and 14 in the other

=== Strength/Dexterity ===

The Duelist excels at both Strength and Dexterity skills, and fights with swords and axes. He utilizes both the attack speed and evasion from Dexterity and the damage and armour of Strength to quickly deal large amounts of damage while staying safe from physical attacks. 
The Duelist's Ascendancy classes are Slayer, Gladiator, and Champion.

=== Strength/Intelligence ===

The Templar represents Strength and Intelligence, and fights with staves and sceptres. He can become a powerful spellcaster or use his elemental damage to perform strong melee attacks.
The Templar's Ascendancy classes are Inquisitor, Hierophant, and Guardian.

=== Dexterity/Intelligence ===

The Shadow is proficient with Dexterity and Intelligence skills, and fights with daggers and claws. He can deal strong critical strikes with weapons or spells, and his traps and mines can disable enemies or deal high damage.
The Shadow's Ascendancy classes are Assassin, Saboteur, and Trickster.

=== Strength/Dexterity/Intelligence ===

The Scion is aligned with all three attributes, and is therefore the most flexible class in terms of character design and skill use. She starts at the centre of the passive skill tree.
The Scion has one Ascendancy Class: the Ascendant.
title: Character class

== Other ==
Characters, monsters, and items can all be associated with multiple attributes at once. For example, a staff weapon is generally about 70% strength and 30% intelligence. It differs from a maul (which could be 100% strength) because it is better at scoring critical strikes, but doesn't hit for as much raw physical damage.

text: === Corrupted implicit modifiers ===
title: Corrupted

text:
Corrupted modifiers are implicit modifiers from a pool dependent on the item's item category and item level. Like other modifiers, it is possible for a corrupted implicit modifier to change an item's required level if the 80% of the implicit's item level requirement is higher than the item's default required level (e.g. a corrupted implicit modifier requiring Level 56 to roll will add a required Level of 44). Conversely, for most jewellery or quivers, if a corrupted implicit's required level is lower than the item's default level, it can lower the default required level of the item (though it will still be restricted by the required level of explicit modifiers).
Corrupted modifiers replace one (or two with double-corrupted) implicit modifier(s) from an item (if the item already has an implicit modifier(s)) and replace it with the corrupted modifier.
Gilded FossilsGilded FossilStack Size: 10Item is overvalued by vendorsPlace in a Resonator to influence item crafting. can be used to add the implicit modifier Item sells for much more to vendors in addition to any existing implicit modifiers. Items that normally have 1 implicit modifier on them will have 2 implicit modifiers when crafted with a Gilded Fossil, and synthesised items can gain up to 4 implicit modifiers this way. When corrupting these 2+ implicit items, there is a chance that the corrupted implicit will replace the otherwise useless Gilded Fossil implicit. Because the Gilded Fossil has no mechanical uses other than adding to the item's vendor price, adding it to an item will give it the potential to keep one or mor

=== Scourge modifiers ===

In the Scourge league, players could use the Blood Crucible to gather Corruption from slain Scourge monsters to corrupt an item (if not already corrupted) and add two Scourge modifiers, one positive and one negative, into an item. An item can be Scourged multiple times to add higher-tier Scourge mods. Unlike Vaal implicit modifiers, Scourge mods do not overwrite the item's implicits. Currently, there is no way to obtain items with Scourge mods outside of trading in permanent leagues.

=== Upgrading rarity ===
"Upgrading" refers to changing an item's rarity.

=== Reforging modifiers ===
"Reforging" refers to randomly rerolling all of an item's modifiers.

=== Augmenting and removing modifiers ===
"Augment" refers to adding a single explicit modifier to an item. Magic items have a default modifier limit of 2 (1 prefix/1 suffix), while rare items have a default modifier limit of 6 (3 prefix/3 suffix). Rare jewels have a limit of 4 (2 prefix/2 suffix), and certain Experimented base type jewellery have different modifier limits.

Other methods to augment or remove modifiers on items include:

text:
=== Crafting benches and vendors ===
Crafting benches are interactable objects that provide a variety of different crafting options, and may offer exclusive effects or a greater degree of control with crafting.
title: Crafting

text:
Crafting Bench - unlocked in the player's hideout as soon as Act 2, it can apply crafted modifiers to an item, deterministically modify an item's sockets, or apply meta-crafting modifiers, such as Suffixes Cannot Be Changed or Cannot roll Attack Modifiers for more advanced crafting methods. Most crafts in the crafting bench are unlocked by finding crafting recipes in the campaign or in maps.
Vendor recipes - specific vendor recipes can be used to obtain specific items or guarantee certain modifiers on items.
Map Device - unlocked in the Epilogue, the Map Device allows players to apply Exarch or Eater influence to or have the Maven witness a map.
The Divine Font - found in the Lord's Labyrinth; it grants various crafting options for gems, and is the primary way to obtain transfigured gems.
Beastcrafting - sacrifices specific types of Beasts from Bestiary encounters for various crafting methods, including guaranteed flask suffixes that grant immunity to ailments, access to Aspect reservation skills, and a deterministic method of adding 6-sockets or 6-links to an item by sacrificing a Black Mórrigan.
Syndicate Crafting Bench - Certain crafting benches allow you to craft an item with the provided currency for a limited period of time.
Harvest crafting - spends Lifeforce obtained from Harvest for various crafting methods, many of which guarantee a random modifier matching a specific tag. It can also change stacks of currencies or fragments into different types, swap elemental resistance modifiers between different elements, or add certain enchantments to weapons and body armour.

text:
=== Critical strike multiplier ===
Critical strikes cause hits to deal "extra damage" compared to a non-critical strike, the magnitude of which is determined by critical strike multiplier (i.e. crit multi). Player characters have a base crit multi value of 150%, while monsters have a base crit multi value of 130%, or 50% and 30% "extra damage" respectively.

=== Reduced extra damage from critical strikes ===
Take #% reduced Extra Damage from Critical Strikes modifiers multiplicatively reduce the Critical Strike Multiplier exceeding the baseline damage (100%). Similar numerical modifiers stack additively and are capped at 100% reduced extra damage from critical strikes, which is equivalent to Take no Extra Damage from Critical Strikes. For example, a character with 30% reduced extra damage from critical strikes against a monster will be calculated as follows:

The default critical strike multiplier for monsters is 130%, so the extra damage is 130% - 100% = 30%.
The total reduced extra damage is 30%, so multiply the extra damage by 0.7.
30% * 0.7 = 21% extra damage. Therefore, critical strikes will be treated as if a monster has 121% crit multi instead of 130%, and will deal 21% more damage on critical strike instead of 30%.
title: Critical strike

text:
=== Ailments ===
Critical strikes inherently have always Ignite, always Freeze, and always Shock. These ailments can still be discarded if they do not reach the minimum ailment threshold.
Damaging ailments (bleeding, poison, and ignite) from critical strikes do not scale with crit multi by default, but inherently have +50% to Damage over Time Multiplier, additive with other sources of Damage over Time Multiplier stats. Allocating Perfect Agony allows critical strike multiplier to scale the Damage over Time Multiplier value.
Minions and monsters both have an inherent +30% to Damage over Time Multiplier for Ailments from Critical Strikes, which is in line with, but also distinct from their default 130% Critical Strike Multiplier.

The currency system in Path of Exile revolves around a variety of different orbs and scrolls. Each currency item serves a specific function in the crafting and enhancement of a character's equipment, or allowing restructuring of the character's passive skill tree.
Currency items are used to pay for items in player trading.
GoldGoldStack Size: 50000Can be spent at Vendors is a type of non-tradable resource.

== Currency items ==
Currency items can be found as drops from monsters or chests, bought directly from different vendors in town, or received through the use of the vendor recipe system by trading specific configurations of items to any town vendor. Currency items play a large role in the player to player trading system, with rare orbs able to be traded for powerful equipment, or even for other types of orbs that a player might want for crafting.
Currency may be applied by right clicking the currency item, then left clicking the target item. Holding Shift allows repeated use without right clicking. Socket and quality currencies may be applied repeatedly by holding Ctrl and left-click.

=== Basic currency ===
Basic currency items are currency items not tied to a specific league mechanic. These include currency with no specific drop restrictions, but can also include currencies that can only drop in maps.
title: Currency

Shards of currency items and scroll fragments are obtained primarily by selling items to vendors. These can be combined to form complete currency items by stacking them.

Endgame currency is an unofficial subcategory of drop-restricted currencies that can only be obtained through specific endgame mechanics or encounters related to maps or the Atlas of Worlds and its bosses.

== Currency exchange resources ==
Exchange rates between different currency items is largely dependent on the item's scarcity and the demand for it by players willing to trade, and differ between the Softcore and Hardcore Trade in Standard or in leagues. Due to the continuously fluctuating nature of the Path of Exile economy, it is impractical to keep an updated table of currency exchange rates here. Instead, please refer to these tools and resources:

pathofexile.com/trade (official player-to-player trade site)
poe.ninja (third-party tool with single-page overview and value-over-time tracking)

Damage is the process by which a player or monster's life or energy shield is reduced.
This page focuses on damage being dealt by the player. For information on damage dealt by minions, see Minion. For information on how elemental damage affects the player, see status ailments and resistances. For information on when damage is applied see, receiving damage.

== Damage calculation ==
The basic damage calculation is:
title: Damage

text:
Damage = (Base_Damage + Added_Damage) * Increased_Damage * More_Damage * Hit_Rate * (Critical_Strike_Damage * Critical_Strike_Chance)
Base_Damage: The primary damage of the skill.  This is either specified in the skill itself (and increases with the level of the skill gem), or is determined by the damage of your weapon (in the case of most Attacks).
Added_Damage: Additional flat damage applied, modified by the skill's damage effectiveness value.
Increased_Damage: Additional percentage damage applied. All applicable sources of increased damage stack additively (e.g. two +10% increased damage modifiers add together to make 20% increased damage: 100% + 10% + 10% = 120%).
More_Damage: Additional percentage damage applied.  All unique sources of more damage are multiplicative with each other (e.g. two +10% more damage modifiers will multiply on top of each other: 110% * 110% = 121%).
Hit_Rate: The rate at which the damage is applied, typically based on attack speed or cast speed.
Critical_Strike_Damage: See Critical Strike Multiplier.
Critical_Strike_Chance: See Critical Strike Chance.
In general:, More Damage is usually more effective than Increased Damage, due to diminishing returns from stacking increased damage modifiers, and the multiplicative nature of More Damage modifiers.
title: Damage

text:
=== Damage variance ===
Damage variance describes the difference between the highest possible value that a source of damage can roll and the lowest possible value. Sources with higher differences are described as having higher damage variance, with lightning damage being characterized as having the highest damage variance of all damage types. For example, Adds 190 to 220 Cold Damage is an example of a source with low damage variance, while Adds 1 to 1000 Lightning Damage would be an example of a source with high damage variance. Mechanics like Damage is Lucky works favourably with skills with high damage variance.
The damage number rolled is rolled per hit, and not per skill use, unlike crits.
Some sources of damage are characterized by a lack of damage variance. All sources of damage are encompassed by one of four categories:

text:
== Damage type ==
A hit can be composed of several types of damage, but each damage type is calculated separately, including damage range rolls. Currently there are five types of damage:
title: Damage

text:
Physical damage - Considered the default damage type. Auto-attacks typically deal physical damage before conversion, and almost all weapons (and unarmed) have base physical damage. Physical damage over time can be inflicted with the bleed ailment, or another common debuff, Corrupted Blood.
Fire damage - One of three elemental damage types. Dealing a critical strike with fire damage inflicts ignite, however ignites also occur based on chance to ignite. Fire damage over time from ignites, burning ground, or other sources is classified as burning damage.
Cold damage - One of three elemental damage types. Hitting an enemy with cold damage can inflict the chill ailment, while dealing a critical strike with cold damage can inflict freeze. Cold damage over time can be inflicted by certain spells, typically also applying Chill.
Lightning damage - One of three elemental damage types. Dealing a critical strike with lightning damage can inflict shock. Base lightning damage tends to have higher variability in damage ranges, with minimum and maximum damage values often being significantly further apart than similar fire or cold damage modifiers. Lightning damage over time is significantly less common than its counterparts, mostly limited to the Siphoning monster modifier, Shock and Horror's beam skill, The Shaper's beam, and some environmental hazards.
Chaos damage - Considered the rarest damage type, chaos damage bypasses energy shield and damages life directly. Chaos damage has the benefit of not being reflectable. Chaos damage over time can be inflicted with the poison ailment. Many
