text:
=== Damage ===
Ignite's base burning damage is 90% of the flat damage of the hit per second. Therefore, over the base duration the target will take 360% of the base damage dealt. Ignite inflicted by enemies deals 200% of base damage over 4 seconds, or 50% base damage per second.
Like other damaging ailments, ignite DPS is not directly related to immediate hit damage. Instead, ignite DPS is calculated separately by taking the flat damage of the hit (consisting of base and added damage modified by conversion) and multiplying that flat damage with damage modifiers relevant for ignite. This independent calculation prevents double-dipping by stats that apply to both the hit and ailment, such as the attacker's #% increased Fire Damage or the defender's Fire Resistance.
Due to the separated calculation, various hit-specific modifiers will never directly affect ignite DPS, such as Melee Damage, Attack Damage, Spell Damage, Area Damage, double or triple damage, resistance penetration, lucky damage, or critical strike multiplier. text:
The Immortal Syndicate is a mysterious organization being investigated by Jun Ortoi. The player must neutralize the Syndicate members residing in the zone, then interrogate them for intelligence on their stronghold and leader, or bargain with them in different ways. Syndicate members can drop veiled items, and strongholds can contain various rewards depending on the position and rank of members, including scarabs.

== Mechanics ==

=== Members ===

The Immortal Syndicate consists of the Syndicate Mastermind and a roster consisting of up to 14 of 17 other members, who are encountered in maps if the Immortal Syndicate has spawned on the map. Players will encounter members at random. They will appear on the minimap  and may be guarding a Transport (), Fortification (), Research () or portal to the player and attempt to assasinate them (Intervention).

Gravicius will never appear on the very first Syndicate Board in new leagues. Rin only joins the Syndicate as a potential option after the player reaches Maps.

=== Investigation Board ===
title: Immortal Syndicate

text:
Each known Syndicate member on the board will display the following: Rank, Task, and Syndicate Gear.
Ranks are indicated by the number of stars on the top right, going up to 3 stars (Sergeant -> Lieutenant -> Captain). Higher-ranked members grant better rewards, hinted at by their tasks, but also equip more Syndicate Gear that make them more difficult. Executing a member raises their rank, while interrogating them lowers it. A member must be assigned to a division to have a rank and have their reward appear at the safehouse. If a member's rank falls to 0, they will become unassigned. Each division can have up to 5 members (including the leader), with a minimum of 2.
The board also shows the relationship between Syndicate members. Trusted members (green lines) are more likely to assist each other in combat, while rivals (red lines) are more likely to attack or betray them instead.
Each division has a leader. Leaders do not appear as primary targets and will only appear to help or hinder another member. If the leader is interrogated or their rank is lowered to 0, one of their subordinates in that division (or an unassigned member if no subordinates exist) with the highest rank will become the new leader.
title: Immortal Syndicate

text:
=== Encounter ===
The Immortal Syndicate is divided into four divisions: Transportation, Fortification, Research, and Intervention. One random division can be encountered in an area in the campaign starting from Act 9; in maps, the player can encounter up to three (either Transportation or Fortification, and guaranteed Research and Intervention). If multiple events exist in an area, the active event must be completed to begin the next one.
title: Immortal Syndicate

text:
Transportation: Begins when the player approaches the caravan. An assigned Syndicate member escorts a caravan along a fixed path towards an exit gate. Defeat the member to complete. Reinforcements will run away after the assigned member is defeated.
Fortification: Begins when the player approaches the fort. Destroy the gate and defeat the assigned member to complete. The fort can contain projectile turrets and killable healing totems. Reinforcements will run away after any member is defeated.
Research: Begins when the player goes through the stairs to the underground laboratory. Rare scientist enemies will attempt to destroy evidence over a period of time; defeating them will slow down the time limit. Defeat the member within the time limit to complete. Reinforcements will run away after any member is defeated.
Intervention: Begins randomly, typically while the player is already in combat. The member and reinforcements will aggressively chase the player, attempting to kill them. Defeat the member to complete. Reinforcements will run away after any member is defeated.
Once all members of an event have been defeated or successfully escaped, defeated members can be handled in one of three presented options. One of these options is always to release the member (middle button); this results in no change to the board state but still causes the member to provide default loot and experience. If multiple members are present, the options may change depending on their order of interaction and relationships with other members
The other two options consist of "Interrogate" and one other

title: Immortal Syndicate

text:
Interrogate: Imprison the member and gather intelligence for the current division's safehouse based on their rank over the next three events. While being interrogated, they cannot appear or reinforce other members while being interrogated. Interrogating lowers the rank of the member when they are released, and will leave them unassigned if their rank is lowered to 0. Interrogating the division leader immediately removes them from leadership and promotes another random subordinate (or an unassigned member if there are no subordinates) to leader. Up to 3 members can be interrogated at once; interrogating a fourth will immediately release the least-recently interrogated member without granting pending intelligence. This option is always available (outside of safehouses).
Execute: Kill the member and raise their rank. If their rank was zero at the time, they will be assigned to the division of whoever they were reinforcing currently. The member gains a new Syndicate Gear item if they have fewer than three. If there are three or downed members, all of them will offer the Execute option. This is the only available option to take against the leader in a safehouse.
Betray: Sabotage another member in some way and become rivals with them. This option is only available while there are two members and they are not already rivals. The two remaining members are very likely to offer "Betray" as an option if they have a "trusted" relationship.
Bargain: Gain a reward of some kind. This option only shows up when only one member is present.
title: Immortal Syndicate

text:
=== Outcomes ===
The following outcomes are possible from Bargain:

Gain Intelligence on a division
Recruit an unranked member; raises their rank, adds them to their division, and becomes Trusted with them
Switch divisions with another member (of the same rank)
Leave the Immortal Syndicate; they will be replaced with someone else
Immediately complete all interrogations: remaining Intelligence is gained, prisoners are released, and their ranks are reduced by 1
Destroy all items (Syndicate Gear) on members in their division
Gain Intelligence and become Neutral with a Rival
Remove all rivalries from all members on the same division
Drop veiled items, scarabs, a stack of currency, a random unique item, or a map.
The following outcomes are possible from Betray:

Gain Intelligence on another division
Steal ranks from another member while removing the rank of that member
Become the new leader of a division
Remove another member from the Immortal Syndicate; they will be replaced with someone else
Destroy all items (Syndicate Gear) on members of another division
Raise rank of all members of their division and lower rank of another

text:
Syndicate members gain a random piece of Syndicate Gear (also referred to as Equipment) when they are Executed which grant them additional combat stats or skills. These are displayed on the Investigation Board interface.
The same Syndicate Gear cannot be attached to multiple members at the same time, and a member cannot have multiple gear of the same type. The maximum number of carried gear is three. Players cannot obtain these gear as they are not real items.
Syndicate Gear can be destroyed as a Betray or Bargain option.

text:
Once intelligence in a division reaches 100%, you can raid their safehouse. Talk to Jun in the hideout to open 6 portals to a safehouse. == League merge ==
When a league is merged with different Betrayal board states (e.g. a temporary league merge into permanent league), the higher intelligence value of each division between the two leagues is kept. Other aspects of the Immortal Syndicate, including the members, their divisions, and their ranks, retain their state in the parent league.

== Ruthless mode ==

There are many differences to safehouse loot with Ruthless mode enabled. Generally speaking, looting safehouses in Ruthless mode provides more ways to obtain pieces of equipment for specific slots, but is much less generous with currency items and crafting options.

text:
Items in Path of Exile are used to represent not just a character's equipment but a variety of other game features. Items can be moved around between locations using the mouse cursor, including the inventory, worn items, stashes, and others, as well as on the ground. Not all types of items can be moved to all item locations. Different item types take a different amount of space in grid based item locations such as inventory and stashes.
Depending on their type, items can have attributes such as rarity, quality, item affixes and item level.

== Loot items ==
In Path of Exile, "items" usually refers to loot items. These are items that have a physical representation in the game world as loot. They are often dropped by slain monsters or loot containers. When a player commands their character to pick up an item, it goes into the character's inventory where the player can then make use of it. In towns or hideouts, items can be stored in the stash to free up inventory space. Items can be purchased from or sold to NPC vendors. Most items can also be traded between players.

=== Equipment ===

Equipment categories includes armour, weapons, jewellery, and flasks. Rarity is indicated by text colour (normal, magic, rare or unique).

=== Currency ===

Currency items are used to modify other items, and are also used for trading or gained from vendors for selling equipment. They have a light brown text colour by default.

=== Divination cards ===

Sets of Divination cards can be exchanged for a certain item, and have specific drop locations. They have a light-cyan text colour by default.
title: Item

text:
=== Quest items ===

Quest items are found on the ground like other items, or given as rewards for completing quests. They cannot be placed anywhere but in inventory or back on the ground. By default they have a bright green text colour.

=== Gems ===

Skills in Path of Exile are granted by gems which are treated as regular items. The skill can only be used when the appropriate gem is socketed in an equipment item being worn by the character. Skill gems, by default, appear in blue-green text when on the ground.

== Other items ==

=== Cosmetic items ===

Cosmetic items use a separate cosmetic tab for managing them and applies to the whole character instead of on specific items.

=== Hideout decorations ===

Hideout decorations and crafting benches, when not in use in a hideout, appear as items in a hideout tab. They can be right clicked from this screen to add them to a hideout.

A Keystone is a unique and powerful passive skill node that significantly impacts the way a character is played.

== Interactions ==

=== Interactions with unique items ===
Some unique items grant a keystone status without needing to have the keystone allocated in the passive tree. In these cases the status only applies once. If you allocate the keystone and use the unique it will be the same as if you had only done one. If a Timeless Jewel modifies a keystone then the unique item will grant the original keystone. This is different from annointing a notable where the timeless jewel changed notable will be assigned.
Some unique items have stats which are similar to keystones. These effects are separate from the keystone and will be treated as two different modifiers. Uniques which add a keystone effect will have the exact name of the keystone in their effect list.

=== Stat removal ===
Stat: The stat in question.
Removed: The stat is removed by this keystone. Keystones that require this stat cease to function.
Altered: The keystone in some way either relies on the stat or alters it. If the stat is removed by another keystone, this keystone ceases to give its benefit.
In short, keystones in the Removed column block the benefits of other keystones in the Altered column for that stat. Only stats for which there is a potential conflict have been listed.

text:
Leagues in Path of Exile represent the game worlds or domains that characters exist within. A single character can only belong to one league at any time, and can't interact with characters outside that league. Leagues are split in 2 different categories: permanent and temporary leagues. Each is narrowed down further with optional game modes that represent different play styles by introducing key conditions and restrictions to gameplay.

== Permanent leagues ==

=== Standard league ===
Standard leagues are permanent, default leagues that only include mechanics that are core to the game, have no additional modifiers, and exclude any content from the current challenge league. Standard leagues include: Standard (Softcore/Trade), Standard Hardcore, Standard Solo-Self Found, and Standard Hardcore Solo-Self Found and their ruthless versions.
title: League

text:
=== Void league ===
Characters used in hardcore versions of Ruthless mode, certain event leagues (such as Endless Delve or Mayhem), or in a Valdo's Puzzle BoxValdo's Puzzle BoxStack Size: 10Contains a Mysterious Map with a Foil Unique RewardI can find no method of destroying the dangerous contents within...  perhaps, someday, you will find a way.Right click to open. map with the Players who Die in area are sent to the Void mod are automatically transferred to the Void League upon death or at the end of the event's duration. Characters in Void Leagues cannot be accessed from the character selection screen and can only be deleted or kept as a trophy. Their equipment and passive trees are still visible on a player's web profile and can be imported into the Path of Building third-party software.

== Temporary leagues ==
Temporary leagues have a limited duration, which can vary from 12 minutes to 4 months. They are usually defined by specific modifiers or features that permanent leagues don't have. When a league ends, characters from temporary leagues are transferred to the corresponding permanent league, unless voided.

=== Challenge leagues ===

Roughly every 13-16 weeks, a new challenge league is released that provides players with a fresh start. Each challenge league includes new:
title: League

text:
League Mechanic: A new optional league mechanic that players can interact with typically once per zone.
Expansion Content: New content from the accompanying expansion, including but not limited to unique items, bosses, lore, game mechanics, and additions or reworks to the endgame Atlas of Worlds mapping system.
League Challenges: A set of optional challenges that can be completed for cosmetic rewards throughout the duration of the challenge league.
Cosmetic Content: A new Kirac's Vault Pass is released for each challenge league, where completing map objectives in the Atlas grants free items related to Atlas progression. It also includes a paid version with mystery boxes and exclusive microtransactions as rewards.
It also adds new balance changes and reworks, cosmetics, bug fixes, and other changes to the game that affect all leagues, as detailed in the patch notes.
When a challenge league ends, all characters and their stash will be sent to their respective parent permanent league. Map progress will be transferred, along with maps. However, the map progress will be reset in Standard league once the new temporary league (and the accompanied expansion) starts. Players restore their atlas completion progress by completing any single T16 legacy map (or partial restoration of the progress by complete a legacy as high tier as they can). Voidstones and Atlas passive progress (only the invitation and pinnacle bosses kill part) are not reset at the start of each expansion, however.
As of Version 3.27.0, dying in the hardcore challenge league will transfer the character to their resp

text:
=== Event leagues ===

Event leagues are temporary leagues that are typically shorter in duration. They often include additional modifiers to make the event more challenging or rewarding. At the end of the event, characters and their stashed items are migrated to Standard league or Void league.
During race seasons, players could earn points towards unlocking alternate art items depending on their placement, with additional prizes awarded to top racers.

=== Private leagues ===

Private leagues are independent, temporary leagues that can be purchased with microtransaction points. Private leagues are customizable, allowing players to select their name, start time, amount of players, duration, and additional modifiers. When creating a private league, you can choose a league type to base it on. This can be a variation of the current challenge league or one of the permanent leagues. By default, every private league has a base cost of 120 Path of Exile store points, a duration of 10 days, and 10 player slots. You may increase the number of players or the duration of the league at an additional cost when creating the league and throughout its duration. The player that creates the league can either pay for the cost directly or crowdfund it, allowing for other players to contribute Path of Exile store points to fund the league.
You may also choose additional modifiers to make the league more challenging at no extra cost. These modifiers will be active for the entirety of the league's duration and cannot be deactivated. Options include:
title: League

text:
Increased Monster Damage: Monsters deal 10% (Tier I) and 20% (Tier II) increased damage.
Increased Monster Life: Monsters have 20% (Tier I) and 40% (Tier II) more life.
Increased Monster Speed: Monsters have 10% (Tier I) and 20% (Tier II) increased attack, cast, and movement speed.
Increased Monster Elemental Damage: Monsters gain 15% (Tier I) and 30% (Tier II) of physical damage as extra fire, cold, and lightning damage.
Increased Monster Area of Effect: Monsters have 35% (Tier I) and 70% (Tier II) increased area of effect.
Reduced Player Resistances: Players have -20% (Tier I) and -40% (Tier II) to all resistances.
Additional Monster Projectiles: Monsters fire 2 additional projectiles.
Famine: Life, mana, energy shield, and flasks do not refill when you go to town.
No Stash: Players have no access to the stash or guild stash)
No Magic or Rare Items Drop: (Items of magic or rare rarity will not drop, they can be crafted.
No Vending: NPCs will not have the option to sell or buy.
Private leagues are popularly used by players who are interested in progressing through a league in a group and restrict trading amongst themselves, normally referred to as Group SSF (GSSF). Players can also base their private league on an event league type. Event leagues are only available occasionally (and for a fixed period), but can be created for free with a restricted set of modifiers.
title: League

text:
== Game mode options ==
There are three additional game mode options available during character creation in permanent and temporary leagues: Hardcore (HC), Solo Self-Found (SSF), and Ruthless (R). These game mode options may be enabled in any combination to add rules and restrictions to the game. The character is placed in an experience ladder comprised only of characters that have the same options enabled.

=== Hardcore ===
When a character dies with hardcore mode enabled, they are eliminated from the hardcore league ladder. Usually this means the character is migrated to the corresponding non-hardcore league ladder, where the character can still be played. If Ruthless mode is also enabled, the character experiences true permadeath; they are migrated to Void league and can no longer be played. In either case, dead characters' final placement on the hardcore league ladder is shown with an annotation indicating that the character died.

=== Solo Self-Found ===

Solo Self-Found mode (SSF) places restrictions on how players can interact. Players are not allowed to join parties or trade with other players. This tends to make progression more difficult, as players must rely solely on the items that they find themselves.
Because SSF does not allow trading, non-SSF league ladders are often referred to by players as "Trade league". From the character selection screen, players can choose to migrate characters from SSF to Trade. The "Migrate All" button migrates all SSF characters, stash tabs, hideouts and league progress.

=== Ruthless ===
title: League

text:
Ruthless mode enables alternate game rules that create extreme item scarcity and make many other subtle changes that are meant to increase the game's difficulty.
Players cannot choose to migrate characters out of a Ruthless league ladder. Note that when a character dies with hardcore and Ruthless mode enabled, that character is migrated to Void league and can no longer be played.

== Version history ==
Prior to Keepers league (version 3.27.0), hardcore characters that died in challenge leagues were migrated to the non-hardcore Standard league ladder, as opposed to the non-hardcore challenge league ladder. This allowed new league-exclusive items to be prematurely be "ripped" to permanent standard leagues prior to end of league migration. It is no longer possible to do this in newer temporary leagues.
title: League

text:
League Mechanics are a set of challenge league features which were reworked and permanently added to the game after their respective league finished.  Each represent a powerful way to obtain crafting material, item drops, or augment items.  They are named after the league in which they first appeared and are sometimes referenced by that name in game.
Most are considered Extra Content and their chance to be encountered in maps can be positively modified. Many can be modified or eliminated entirely with Atlas tree passives.

= List of mechanics =

== Abyss ==
Abysses are interactable objects which spawns cracks and pits that spawn monsters. The Abyss cracks trail randomly along the area, and on the final pit it spawns an Abyssal Trove, containing rewards. Occasionally, they may instead spawn a Stygian Spire or an entrance to the Abyssal Depths, which contains a boss. Abysses can close up if the player takes too long to kill the monsters. Abysses are marked on the minimap with a green icon .
title: League mechanics

text:
== Affliction (The Viridian Wildwood) ==
A high-level area may spawn a portal at the start that leads to the Viridian Wildwood, a forest covered in perpetual darkness. Sacred Wisps will uncover the darkness as you move, but you can only uncover a limited amount of darkness before you must return. You can collect three types of Wisps that are dispersed into the main zone once you leave the Wildwood, empowering random enemies by increasing their power and item drops. You may also find various random encounters inside the Wildwood.
In Affliction league, the Wildwood could contain an Azmeri Wanderer NPC that grants access to a Wildwood ascendancy class, granting access to unique abilities.

== Ambush (Strongboxes) ==
Strongboxes are a special type of loot container. When opened, a strongbox will release groups of monsters to surround and attack the character. Strongboxes come with affixes that affect its drops and hazards and can be modified with currency items.

== Anarchy (Rogue Exiles) ==
Rogue Exiles are unique monsters with player skins and use players skills. On death, exiles drop a large amount of items, including one for each equipment slot.

== Bestiary (The Menagerie) ==
Beasts are marked on the minimap with a yellow icon  or red icon  and can be hunted with Einhar Frey. Captured beasts can be used for beastcrafting in The Menagerie for crafting effects.
In Bestiary league, the player would have to capture the beasts by themselves using nets.
title: League mechanics

text:
== Betrayal (Immortal Syndicate) ==
The Immortal Syndicate can appear and has three encounters per area. Syndicate members are marked on the minimap  and may be guarding a transport , fortification  or research . They may also appear out of portals and attempt to assassinate the player.
Defeating the syndicate members will provide intelligence in the investigation which is coordinated with Jun Ortoi. Once intelligence in a faction reaches 100%, the player can raid their safehouse for significant rewards based on the leader and rank of the safehouse members. At high levels, safehouse leaders can drop a map fragment used to challenge the Syndicate Mastermind.

== Beyond ==
When an area has a Beyond encounter enabled, enemies have a chance to spawn a small red orb on death. If there are enough other red orbs around each other, they will spawn a pack of hostile Beyond demons. Occasionally, a Beyond boss may spawn instead. Once a Beyond boss spawns, no more Beyond monsters can be spawned in that area.

== Blight ==
Blights are tower defence-like encounters that can spawn from Fungal Growths in any map area, which will always be accompanied by Sister Cassia. The player must defend the pump while building towers until all monsters are slain.
Blight encounters are also found in Blighted maps and Blight-ravaged maps that have all the monsters removed, save for a single special Blight encounter.
title: League mechanics

text:
== Breach ==
Breaches come in two forms: Unstable Breaches and Breach Hives.
Unstable Breaches appear as grasping hands when approached create an expanding circle that summons Hiveborn monsters. Unstable Breaches collapse after a given time, which can be extended by killing Breach monsters. If enough Breach monsters have been slain, the Breach become stabilized, summoning more Breach monsters.
Breach Hives are surrounded by organic walls and flaming burrows that destroy nearby walls when touched. Reach the core to summon Ailith, and the player must defend her against waves of enemies while she prepares to destroy the Hive. Endgame Breaches may contain an entrance to a Hive Fortress that contains an extended defence mission.
When a Breach encounter is complete, the player gains Hiveblood that can be spent on the Genesis Tree to open a Wombgift and collect its rewards, which include Foulborn currency and Foulborn unique items.

== Delirium ==
title: League mechanics

text:
A Mirror of Delirium is a glittering black gateway which spawn within a close distance from the zone entrance. Once a player passes through it, it spawns a gray fogs that spreads outwards throughout the map, beginning the Delirium encounter.
Delirium is a zone-wide effect that spawns new enemies and empowers existing ones, and increases in intensity as you venture further out. As the player kill enemies inside the mist, a reward bar on the bottom left will start filling up. The fog dissipates outwards over time, and the Delirium encounter ends if you're outside of the fog long enough or when ended early.
Delirium orbs can be used to add a permanent Delirium effect to a map.

== Delve (Azurite Mine) ==
Voltaxic Sulphite appears on the minimap as a golden yellow mineral  and can be mined with Niko, Master of the Depths. It provides fuel to explore the Azurite Mine which is one of the Endgame activities.

== Domination (Shrines) ==
Shrines can appear randomly in most areas, granting significant bonuses to nearby monsters or casts spells at nearby players, and are often guarded by monsters. Players can activate the shrine to temporarily gain its bonuses.

== Essence ==
Areas can contain imprisoned monster empowered by essences. Activating the imprisoned Rare monster three times frees the trapped monsters. Monster will drop the essences they were holding once slain, which can be used for crafting.
title: League mechanics

text:
== Expedition ==
The player will encounter one of the four Expedition NPCs. The player can place explosives in the area to unearth monsters and chests. Explosions can be used to unearth Remanants which add a difficulty modifier and rewards to any subsequent monsters or items unearthed.
An Expedition logbook can drop and be taken to Dannig, who can open portals to larger Expedition areas with more remnants, flags and placeable explosives.

== Harvest ==
A portal leading to the The Sacred Grove may spawn in areas. There, you can find multiple patches of plants connected to each other in pairs. You can activate one of these patches to begin harvesting it by defeating the monsters that spawn from it. These monsters drop Lifeforce, which are used for various Harvest crafting options via the Horticrafting Station.
In Harvest league, the player is in charge of growing the plants by planting seeds within the Sacred Grove then slaying the monsters that emerge from them after they grow over time and placing machinery to store and dispense Lifeforce to grow higher tier plants.
title: League mechanics

text:
== Heist (The Rogue Harbour) ==
Rogue's MarkersRogue's MarkerStack Size: 50000Creates a portal to the Rogue Harbour from a Town or HideoutUsed as Currency for services in the Rogue HarbourRight click on this item while in a Town or Hideout to use it., contracts, and blueprints can drop randomly as loot, or be obtained by opening a Smuggler's Cache. These can be used in The Rogue Harbour to participate in a heist, one of Path of Exile's endgame activities.
Heists involve infiltrating an area with a fellow rogue, killing enemies and opening chests without alerting the area, with the goal of retrieving the target item at the end. Once the area goes on lockdown, the player must then make their way back to the entrance alive to secure the loot. Completing contracts earns Markers and blueprint intel, which are used to set up a grand heist for more valuable loot.

== Incursion (Temple of Atzoatl) ==
A Temporal incursion is a short-duration visit to a temple room. Defeating one of two Vaal Architect in the incursion or using a Stone of PassageStone of PassageThis item can be placed into an Altar of Passage to create a connection between two adjacent rooms in the Temple of Atzoatl. This item will drop on the ground when leaving an Incursion. will customize and upgrade The Temple of Atzoatl. After all incursions are finished, a map of the Temple may be opened.
title: League mechanics

text:
== Legion ==
Legions are ancient armies frozen in the midst of battle. They can be encountered by touching a Timeless Monolith , which spawns the Legions and gives the player a window of time in which they can be "killed". Once the timer ends, "killed" mobs are broken out and can fought for rewards.
Emblems obtained from the monolith encounters can be used in the map device to open a special Legion encounter, which rewards Timeless jewels.

== Mirage ==
Zone where Mirages can be encountered contain Afarud monsters that are guarding a captured djinn. Slaying its captors will summon Varashta, who will offer a Wish to take into the Astral Plane and open a portal leading there. Mirage areas are imperfect copies of an area within the zone. They contain the same monsters and league mechanics as the original, but they may differ slightly, sometimes switching them to variations that can only be found in Mirages. A Mirage encounter is complete once the monsters guarding the astral chains are killed.
Mirage encounters can drop special coins used to Imbue a skill gem, corrupting it to add a permanent level 1 support gem effect to it, or coins used to transform Afarud or Restored Maraketh uniques. League mechanics warped by the Mirage can also drop exclusive items.

== Rampage ==
Rampage is a "kill-streak" mechanic that grants bonuses as you continue killing enemies within a short period of time. 
Rampage can only be accessed via certain unique items and modifiers.
title: League mechanics

text:
== Ritual ==
Multiple Ritual altars can spawn in areas. Once the enemies around the altar are slain, interacting with a Ritual altar begins a Ritual encounter. The altar traps the player within its area and spawns enemies killed near the altar until all enemies are slain. Each subsequent Ritual encounter in the same area will spawn all the monsters that were spawned by previous altars.
Each enemy slain during a Ritual encounter grants Favour. Favour is used to purchase items offered by the Ritual altars and does not carry over outside the zone. Items can also be deferred instead, paying a part of its cost to have it reappear in future Ritual encounters.

== Sanctum ==
Forbidden TomesForbidden TomeArea Level: (68-83)Mundus noster cecidit. Daemones ubique sunt. Librumhunc in sacrarium conicio, ut forte alius viam inveniat...Take this item to the Relic Altar in the Forbidden Sanctum to enter. have a chance to drop randomly in areas. You can use them to enter the Forbidden Sanctum, a roguelike-inspired dungeon where you must travel deep into the Sanctum while avoiding enemies and traps that damage your Resolve. The players can acquire boons and afflictions along the way that make the run easier or harder, as well as collect Relics that can be slotted to give yourself a bonus for future Sanctum runs. It is one of Path of Exile's endgame activities.
In the Forbidden Sanctum, you can acquire currency items immediately, at the end of the floor, or at the end of the dungeon. Certain unique Relics allow you to gain exclusive unique items by completing a Sanctum run with it.
title: League mechanics

text:
== Sentinel ==
Sentinels are constructs that when deployed empower enemies in exchange for increasing their item drops. A sentinel has a chance to spawn at the beginning of high-tier maps.
In Sentinel league, Sentinels could be equipped and deployed by the player and enhanced using the Sentinel Controller skill tree, but each Sentinel could only be used a limited number of times. New Sentinels could be crafted using the Power Core by combining two Sentinels.

== Settlers (Kingsmarch) ==
Upon reaching the endgame, players can visit the town of Kingsmarch. There, you can spend GoldGoldStack Size: 50000Can be spent at Vendors to hire workers and assign them to passively farm crops, mine or smelt ores, or disenchant items for Thaumaturgic Dust. These items can be sent out as shipments to other regions in exchange for rewards. All Kingsmarch worker activities are done in real time as long as there is enough gold in the Treasury to pay their wages. The speed of each task and the chance of a shipment returning with reduced rewards depends on worker levels. 
Ore deposits spawn in zones. Clicking an ore deposit will begin an encounter, and once the encounter is complete, the ores will be sent to Kingsmarch for processing.
Shipments can provide tattoos and runegrafts as rewards, depending on the port the shipment was sent to. The Recombinator crafting bench costs gold and Thaumaturgic Dust to use. You can also hire Atlas Runners to run your maps using the Kalguuran Map Device.
title: League mechanics

text:
== Tempest ==
Areas containing Tempests will randomly spawn coloured circles of winds that empower or hinder both allies and enemies inside its radius after a delay. Enemies empowered by a Tempest often drop more items.
Currently, Tempests cannot be encountered normally, but can be made to spawn through various means, such as Scarab of Radiant StormsScarab of Radiant StormsStack Size: 20Limit: 1Area contains a Resplendent TempestThe great cacophony of life roars to a crescendo.Can be used in a personal Map Device to add modifiers to a Map. or in The Temple of Atzoatl when the temple has the room Tempest Generator or its upgraded variants.
In Tempest league, zones would contain a random Tempest. Act zones would cycle between Tempests in real time. A larger variety of Tempests were also available.

== Torment (Tormented Spirits) ==

A Tormented Spirit is a green spirit which flee when encountered and imbue any normal or magic monsters with dangerous powers or possess a rare or unique monsters to empower it. Monsters touched or possessed by a Tormented Spirit have improved item drops.
title: League mechanics

text:
== Ultimatum ==
The Trialmaster can appear to offer an Ultimatum encounter. To begin, you must choose a difficulty modifier to add to the encounter. You must them complete up to 10 waves (by default) of the objective without leaving the zone, failing the objective, or dying. For each wave you complete, you earn a reward. You may either end the encounter and take all your earned rewards, or continue to the next wave by adding another modifier. If you fail the encounter, all earned rewards will be lost.
Ultimatum encounters may reward an Inscribed UltimatumInscribed UltimatumCan be used in a personal map device to open portals to the Trialmaster's Domain and attempt his challenge. Portals will close once the challenge begins. While viewing your Atlas, Right-click this item to pinpoint its location. that opens up an arena where you wager its requisite item to gain a reward if you can complete an extra-long Ultimatum wave.

== Warbands ==
Warbands are four factions of special monsters. Warbands can drop exclusive unique items or magic items with an exclusive modifier.
Currently, Warbands can only be found in certain maps as map bosses, or in specific nodes in the Azurite Mine. There are no Atlas passive skill directly associated with Warbands.
In Warbands league, random packs of a certain Warband could occupy various zones. Act zones would cycle between Warbands in real time.

= Removed mechanics =
title: League mechanics

text:
== Archnemesis ==
In Archnemesis league, players can customise a Rare monster's mods by applying Archnemesis modifiers to petrified monsters, found throughout every area. Each Archnemesis modifier applied to a monster carries over to subsequent petrified monsters in the area.
The mechanic was not added to the core game after Archnemesis league, but the new monster modifiers replaced old systems and were reworked several times after.

== Bloodlines ==
Bloodlines is a special type of monster modifier that can appear on Magic monsters.
In Version 3.18.0, many Bloodlines modifiers were removed or merged into Archnemesis modifiers. Archnemesis modifiers were replaced with a simpler modifier system in Version 3.20.0.

== Breach (Breach league) ==
Breaches are timed monster-spawning portals identified by a red hand-like construct within a purple circle . Walking into the hand will activate the breach, expending its area gradually then collapsing after a certain period of time. Breach monsters drop splinters used to form a Breachstone, which opens up an area containing one large Breach that leads to a boss.
This form of Breach was replaced with the Breach from Keepers league in Version 3.28.0.

== Crucible ==
The Crucible Forge allows players to unlock and level up Crucible passive trees on weapon and shields. Experience towards the Crucible passive tree is gained by killing Crucible monsters. The Forge of the Titans contains a forge that lets you sacrifice an item to combine its Crucible tree with another.
The mechanic was not added to the core game after Crucible league.
title: League mechanics

text:
== Harbinger ==

A Harbinger is a blue glowing monster named with strange runes. They can only be harmed by killing their minions and mainly drop currency shards.
Harbingers were removed from the game in Version 3.28.0.

== Invasion ==
Invasion Bosses are unique monsters that can appear in zones and "invade" it.
Invasion bosses were phased out of the game over time. It was last offered as a map device crafting option in Version 3.3.0. Additionally, many Vaal side area bosses are based on Invasion bosses.

== Kalandra (Lake of Kalandra) ==
Interacting with a Mirrored Tablet displays a map represented by grids. The player is given a choice to modify or add a tile to the tablet. Once all empty grids on the tablet have been filled, you can enter the Lake of Kalandra to loot it for rewards, with loot scaling as you move further away from the entrance.
The Lake of Kalandra can contain a Reflecting Mist. The Reflection gives you a choice between two Mirrored rings or amulets to take, which have multiplied positive or negative values. The modifier values inverted on their counterparts. Rarely, you can be given the option to reflect your own ring/amulet to create two items with the same effect.
The Lake of Kalandra was not added to the core game, but in Version 3.25.0, tier 16+ map monster packs can occasionally spawn a Reflecting Mist, with a chance to drop an itemised version of itself.
title: League mechanics

text:
== Legacy (Leaguestones) ==
Leaguestones can be slotted to add one of 17 previous league mechanic to the next zone you enter a limited number of times, up to three at a time.
Leaguestones were only available during Legacy league.

== Mercenaries ==
Players can encounter a Trarthan Mercenary in areas. There are three options available for each mercenary: hire them for a gold fee, take one of their items, or exile them and temporarily prevent mercenaries of the same attribute alignment from appearing. All three options require the player to defeat them in a duel. Defeating a mercenary raises Renown, and dying to a mercenary or choosing to not fight them lowers it. Higher Renown results in more difficult but more rewarding mercenaries are and increases the chance of an Infamous Mercenary from spawning.
Players can have a hired mercenary accompany them. These mercenaries act like allied party members who assist in combat and can be equipped with your own items. If a mercenary dies, they will not lose their items, but you will need to pay a gold fee to revive them.
Mercenaries can sometimes hold Trarthan gems, which the player can take as a reward. Infamous Mercenaries can also have exclusive unique items or an equipment with an exclusive Infamous modifier on them.
Mercenaries were not added to the core game after Mercenaries league ended.
title: League mechanics

text:
== Necropolis ==
The Lantern of Arimor allows players to preview monsters that are present in an upcoming zone, as well as random modifiers attached to them. Players can choose what monsters will be affected by the modifiers by swapping them around or use an Ember of the Allflame to transform them into a different monster. Monsters can drop corpses that are used for crafting in the Necropolis.
The mechanic was not added to the core game after Necropolis league.

== Nemesis ==
Nemesis is a special type of monster modifier that can appear on Rare monsters.
In Version 3.18.0, many Nemesis modifiers were removed or merged into Archnemesis modifiers. Archnemesis modifiers were replaced with a simpler modifier system in Version 3.20.0.

== Metamorph ==
Monster organ sample may drop from monsters marked on the mini-map with a circular green icon . These can be combined to create a powerful Metamorph boss monster. A sufficiently powered Metamorph can drop itemised organ samples that can be taken to Tane's Laboratory to create an even more powerful Metamorph.
Metamorph was removed from the game in Version 3.23.0.
title: League mechanics

text:
== Perandus ==
Perandus chests are guarded by monsters and magical effects that can only opened after enough of its guardians have been slain. They contain Perandus CoinsPerandus CoinStack Size: 5000Trade coins to Cadiro Perandus. that can be traded to Cadiro Perandus, who will offer a random unique items for coins.
Perandus chests did not spawn normally, but could be made to spawn with a map device craft or Perandus Scarabs.
Perandus mechanics were removed from the game in Version 3.16.0.

== Prophecy ==
A Silver CoinSilver CoinStack Size: 30Cross Navali's palm with silver to receive a prophecy. can be used to receive a Prophecy from Navali. Each Prophecy will triggers its effect when you fulfill the condition it meets. Some Prophecies let you upgrade a unique items into a Fated item.
Prophecies were removed from the game in Version 3.17.0.
title: League mechanics

text:
== Scourge ==
In Scourge league, players receive the Blood Crucible, which is filled with the blood of slain monsters. The device can be activated to transports the character into a parallel reality. This version of Wraeclast is inhabited by demons known as The Scourge. When the Blood Crucible's blood runs out, or if the player chooses to go back, the character is instantly shifted back to normal reality.
Equipment can be placed into the Blood Crucible. After killing enough Scourge Demons, the item can be transformed (Scourged). It becomes corrupted and gains two Scourge modifiers, which are in addition to the regular implicit and explicit mods. The Blood Crucible could be upgraded to improve Scourge outcomes.
Blood Crucible mechanics were not added to the core game after Scourge league, but Scourge monsters replaced old Beyond demons later.

== Synthesis ==
Synthesis league mechanics included the Memory Nexus and Fragmented Memories. The player must stabilize Memories found in zones as the area slowly fades away to capture it. Captured memories are used to create paths in the Memory Nexus that you can enter and loot for rewards, increasing as you chain more memories together. The Synthesiser can be used to combine three fractured items into a synthesised item with implicits based on the components' modifiers.
The mechanic was not added to the core game after Synthesis league, but synthesised and fractured items can be found or crafted from other various mechanics, and unique Synthesis maps containing bosses from Synthesis league can be found in the endgame.
title: League mechanics

text:
== Talisman ==
In Talisman league, a monster can be claimed a Talisman, causing it to be empowered with various abilities. The monster will drop the Talisman on death, but other monsters can claim it before you can. The Stone Circle can be used to sacrifice five of the same tier talismans to summon a monster holding a talisman of a higher tier. If five tier 3 talismans were sacrificed, it opens a portal to a boss fight against Rigwald, the Wolven King.
These mechanics were not added to the core game (though the Delve node Ritual Grounds contains monsters empowered by Talismans), but Talismans could be acquired from various mechanics. Unique talismans are part of the core drop pool.

== Trial of the Ancestors ==
The Trial of the Ancestors is a tournament against fallen Karui chieftains and their tribes in the afterlife. The players is tasked to assemble a team of warriors, gear them with equipment or field items, then lead them to victory by destroying the enemy team's totems and earn rewards with each victory.
The mechanic was not added to the core game after Ancestor league.

Leech recovers an amount of life, mana, or energy shield over time, relative to the damage inflicted on an enemy. Leech is based on the damage taken by the enemy, not the amount of life removed.

== Mechanics ==

All leech mechanics act the same way for life, mana, and energy shield. Examples in this article use life, but if the character has equal statistics for a different resource (mana or energy shield), they will apply in the same way. 
Whenever a character with some source of leech hits a monster, a leech instance is created. Hitting multiple enemies with a single use of a skill creates that many leech instances.
Life Leech instances have the following properties by default:
title: Leech

text:
Each instance is independent.
Multiple leech instances stack and apply simultaneously.
There is no limit to the possible number of active leech instances
Each instance Recovers the character's life for the Damage Dealt * % damage Leeched as Life up to a maximum of 10% of maximum life.
Each instance Recovers at a rate of 2% of maximum life per second.
Each instance Recovers until the total amount of leeched damage was recovered or the character reaches full unreserved life.
The total recovery rate of all life leech instances is limited to 20% of maximum life or mana per second (10% for energy shield). The extra recovery over that cap will be ignored.
Leech grants recovery to the entity that hits the target. If a minion or totem with leech hits an enemy, leech will grant recovery to that minion or totem, not the character. Skills used by totems and other proxies create leech instances with recovery caps based on the player's maximum life, not their own. === Modifiers ===
Leech can be modified significantly through passives, support gems, and equipment. Modifiers affecting life leech are damage Leeched as Life, Maximum Recovery per Life Leech, total Recovery per second from Life Leech and Maximum total Life Recovery per second from Leech.

Additional damage Leeched as Life reduces the amount of damage required to reach the maximum possible amount of life that can be recovered by a single instance.
50% increased Maximum Recovery per Life Leech increases the default 10% of the maximum life that can be leeched by an instance to 15%.
50% increased Maximum total Life Recovery per second from Leech increases the default 20% of maximum life that can be recovered per second from all instances combined to 30%.
#% increased total Recovery per second from Life Leech increases the player's recovery from leech, allowing the cap to be reached with fewer hits. It does not modify individual leech instances (and correspondingly has no effect on leech duration).

text:
=== Leech duration ===
The duration of a life leech instance is defined by the maximum recovery per life leech, divided by the leech rate of 2% of maximum life per second. By default, the maximum amount of life leeched per instance is 10% of a character's maximum Life, resulting in a maximum duration of 5 seconds.
No stat currently exists to modify the base rate of a leech instance. The maximum recovery may be modified through Maximum Recovery per Life Leech, which in turn modifies maximum duration. For example, a 100% increase from Brutal Fervour will result in a maximum recovery per life leech of 20%, recovered at a rate of 2% per second for 10 seconds. 
Partial instant leech will reduce the total over time recovery, not the rate. For example, when 10% of leech is instant, and the leech instance recovers 1% instantly and 9% over time, its duration will be 4.5 seconds. 
Modifiers to total Recovery per second from Life Leech amplify recovery from leech, not the base rate of the leech instance. Multiplying recovery does not 'empty' a leech instance faster.
Additionally all instances of life leech are discarded as soon as the character reaches full unreserved life. This discarding can be prevented by overleech mechanics, for example by "Life Leech effects are not removed when Unreserved Life is Filled" effects like Immortal Ambition or Offering to the Serpent (Synthesised). Petrified Blood also enable overleech as it ignores leech above low life without removing it. The leech duration is not modified by those effects, they just prevent premature end of the leech. 
Examples:

text:

Examples: 
1. A character with none of the leech modifiers changed has 1.000 maximum life, with 1% of damage leeched, and hits 1 enemy 1 time for 4.000 damage. The leech is 40. It leeches 20 life per second for 2 seconds leeching a total of 40 life.
2. A character with none of the leech modifiers changed has 1.000 maximum life, with 1% of damage leeched, and hits 1 enemy 1 time for 40.000 damage. The leech is 400, reduced to the maximum of 100 total per life leech (instance). The character recovers 20 life per second for 5 seconds leeching a total of 100 life.
3. A character with none of the leech modifiers changed has 1.000 maximum life, with 1% of damage leeched, and hits 5 enemies 5 times each for 40.000 damage. The leech of each instance is 400, reduced to the maximum of 100 total per life leech (instance), with 25 leech instances. The character wants to recovers 2500 life per second, but is limited to 200 life per second from the Maximum Total Life Recovery Per Second from Leech. Each instance has a duration of 5 seconds, because it reached the Maximum Recovery per Life Leech. Each individual leech instance ends 5 seconds after the initial hit. The total recovered health depends on the time spread of the hits, due to all maximums being reached.

text:
=== Combined Recovery Rate ===
The total life leech recovery rate is the sum of all recovery rates from all life leech instances.
This combined rate is subject to the total leech rate cap, which is by default 20% of the character's maximum health.
Reaching this maximum rate requires a number of leech instances equal the total maximum rate cap divided by the leech rate of each instance.
For a default character, this is 10 instances, provided that each hit deals enough damage to reach the maximum amount that can be leeched per instance.

=== Instant leech ===
Effects that cause some or all of leech to be instant will still be capped by maximum recovery per leech. For partial instant leech, the duration of non-instant leech will be equal relative to its remain duration after instant leech.
For example, using life leech with the 10% of Leech is Instant mod and no other modifiers to maximum leech, a single hit that leeches life for the maximum amount will recover 1% of your life instantly and the remaining 9% over 90% of the leech duration (4.5 seconds by default).
Instant leech is not affected by modifiers to (leech) recovery rate, since its rate is instant.

== Types of leech ==
Several types of leech apply exclusively to certain skill types. Some leech types only work for attacks, others only works with elemental damage or all sources of physical damage. Any such specializations are defined in the modifier.  
Generally the leech modifiers follow this template: 
#% of X Y Damage Z Leeched as Life/Mana
Where X can be:

Physical/Fire/Cold/Lightning/Elemental/Chaos
Y can be:
title: Leech

text:
Attack/Spell
and Z can be:

Dealt with {Weapons} 
Note that if X, Y or Z are not specified it means that it applies to all those types.

Legions are ancient armies frozen in the midst of battle. They can be encountered by touching a Timeless Monolith, which breaks out the Legions and gives the player a window of time to defeat them. This encounter is considered Extra Content and has a baseline 8% chance to appear in any non-unique map area.

== Overview ==

Players can find a Legion by interacting with a Timeless Monolith. Monoliths have a base greater than 8% chance to spawn in a map.
Monoliths can also be found via other sources:
title: Legion

text:
By use of a Legion ScarabLegion ScarabStack Size: 20Limit: 5Area contains an additional Legion EncounterWhat good is peace to a warrior?Can be used in a personal Map Device to add modifiers to a Map.
As a room in The Temple of Atzoatl (the Hall of Mettle room and its upgraded versions).
In The Climb (Act 1) - Will always have Eternal and Karui legions
In The Dried Lake (Act 4) - Will only have Eternal legions
Interacting with the Monolith will reveal a battle between two Legion factions that are in stasis. A timer will start once the Monolith is activated. During this phase, the enemies can be "killed", breaking them out of stasis and allowing them to be fought when the timer ends for rewards. The timer can range from 14 to 20 seconds (or more with Atlas passives), with a longer timer in lower-level zones. Once the timer runs out, all the enemies that were broken out of stasis will remain and start attacking. Enemies that didn't get broken out will disappear.
Schism: Alternatively, taking the Timeless Conflict keystone will disable the Legion timer. Instead, breaking out monsters and chests from stasis will contribute progress towards a Schism, as shown by a progress bar. Once the progress bar is full, the Schism will occur and the Legion encounter will begin. Breaking out monsters and chests with rewards or more powerful monsters will contribute more progress towards the Schism.
Some Legion enemies have a symbol above their heads, indicating an additional reward type they will drop. Chests and War Hoards can also spawn, which can be destroyed and opened after the timer run
title: Legion

text:

Destroying a Chest or War Hoard will free all nearby enemies without symbols in a radius around it. The general of each Legion can occasionally spawn, always spawning in the far rear of the formation. If a general spawns, the monolith will display a wave of purple on the bottom in the direction of the general.
Generally, rarer, more rewarding spawns will spawn further away from the monolith. Therefore, it's advised to move deep into a formation as quickly as possible if you are looking for rare spawns.

== Mechanics ==
Rarity: Legion Sergeants are rare monsters whereas Legion Generals are unique monsters.

== Items ==
There are two types of currency associated with monoliths; each are specific to the legion.

=== Splinters ===

Legion enemies and chests can drop Splinters of their Legion. 100 Splinters of the same type can be combined into an Emblem.

=== Emblems ===

Emblems are obtained from combining Splinters. They can be put into a map device in order to open a portal to the Domain of Timeless Conflict. You must use at least two Emblems of different Legions to open a portal to the Domain. A fifth slot for the Map Device can be unlocked by completing a Nightmare map or Maven's Invitation: The Atlas, allowing all 5 Emblems to be used (commonly called a 5-way). Unrelenting Emblems occasionally drop as a reward from the Domain of Timeless Conflict when all five factions are present.

There are a total of five different legions. The Eternal Empire, Karui, and Vaal are the most common, with the Templar Legion being rarer, and the Maraketh Legion being the rarest.

text:
Maps are items used to open portals to specific map areas with varying monsters and league encounters. They open the way to the most challenging and rewarding encounters and therefore play a crucial part in the endgame of Path of Exile.
As most item classes, maps come in all rarities and can be crafted  with currency items to change their modifiers.

== Acquisition ==

While levelling, players can find their first maps as drops as early as Act 8, with an increasing chance to be found later thorough the campaign. Players cannot use maps until the Epilogue.
In the Epilogue, the player will wake up in Karui Shores and the quest A Call to Arms will lead to Commander Kirac who gives the player a Tier 1 magic map. The map device mechanics and the Atlas of Worlds are also introduced here: with it, maps can be used to open 6 Portals to a randomised instance of the selected layout in the Atlas in which monsters can be fought.
Player's progress can be visualized on the Atlas. Completing a map of the chosen layout will reveal adjacent connected areas, unlocking new regions that can be entered. The player starts in the centre of the Atlas where the first maps with an area level of 68 are located.
Map drops are not affected by party size.

=== Tiers ===
title: Map

text:
There are 16 standard tiers of maps, each tier corresponding to an area level. The lowest tier drops during progression through the campaign and once inside the map, higher tier maps start dropping. Magic and rare monsters can drop maps that are +1 tier above and map bosses can drop +2 tiers above the map area the character is in, respectively.
Moving from one group of map tiers to the next often imposes a challenge as the higher tier maps become harder to sustain. Furthermore, mid-tier and top-tier maps introduce higher values for the mods they can roll, new mods that are more challenging, and combinations of mods that are not allowed to coexist on low-tier maps. Many Atlas passive skills improve map drops.
When a Voidstone is socketed into the Atlas, all maps in that quadrant will have their minimum map tier increased to 16. Found maps will also drop one tier higher and maps below tier 16 will be converted to gold. Voidstones also add a global effect to all maps in the Atlas, including a chance for tier 16 map to drop as a Nightmare map.

=== Upgrades ===
If a player has three maps of the same tier, they can be sold to a vendor to receive a new map one tier higher.
title: Map

text:
== Crafting ==
A map can be crafted with currency. Using an Orb of AlchemyOrb of AlchemyStack Size: 20Upgrades a normal item to a rare itemRight click this item then left click a normal item to apply it. on a white map adds random modifiers and upgrades its rarity to rare. Like equipment, they come in normal, magic, rare, and unique rarities, and can have their own special affixes which may make them more difficult, but also increases their potential rewards. Maps can also have quality, which can be improved with Chisels, adding buffs such as increased monster pack size or increased item rarity.

=== Modifiers ===

Each (non-unique) map can have up to 3 prefixes and 3 suffixes, just like other items. Currency related to rarity also works the same, for example, an Orb of AlchemyOrb of AlchemyStack Size: 20Upgrades a normal item to a rare itemRight click this item then left click a normal item to apply it. will turn a normal map into a rare. Modifiers for maps change the properties of the map when one is in that map, thereby making it more difficult and (usually) resulting in increased item quantity for all drops on that map. High increased quantity also affects the drop rates of maps while in a particular map, so high modifiers will increase your chances at continuing to get map drops and finding higher level maps to use.
title: Map

text:
=== Corruption outcomes ===
Like most other items, maps can be corrupted using a Vaal OrbVaal OrbStack Size: 20Corrupts an item, modifying it unpredictablyRight click this item then left click an item to corrupt it. Corrupted items cannot be modified again.. One of the following effects will occur:

No effect (other than adding the corrupted property).
Reroll the item with random affixes. Rare maps will have 4-6 affixes.
If the map is Tier 1-15, it has a 50% chance to increase its tier by one.
When a Shaped or Elder Map gains a tier, it will become a Shaped or Elder (respectively) Map base of one tier higher, even if that map isn't unlocked on the player's Atlas. This system only exists on Standard, as it is no longer part of the current atlas system.
If the map is Tier 16, it has a ~10% chance to change into a rare tier 16 Vaal Temple MapVaal Temple MapMonster Level: 83Area contains 10 additional guarded Vaal VesselsCorruptedTravel to a Map by using this in a personal Map Device. Maps can only be used once..
Reroll the map into a rare item with eight random affixes, retaining the map base.
Add a special Vaal implicit. Any implicit mods already on the map will be retained.
Certain map corruption implicits cannot appear on Blighted maps and Blight-ravaged maps; the total chance to add any map corruption implicit is unchanged, however.
In addition to these effects, all bosses of corrupted maps have a chance to drop Sacrifice Vaal Fragments or Vaal Skill Gems.
A corrupted map cannot be further modified with currency, except using the Tainted currencies.
title: Map

text:
== Unidentified Maps ==
It is possible to put unidentified maps into the map device. Non-unique unidentified maps gain a +30% item quantity bonus when running these maps, but even when you enter the map the specific modifiers to the map are not revealed to you, even though the overall quantity, rarity and pack size is. Some are easy to observe, burning or chilled ground are very obvious for example, but others are harder to know immediately (if there are enough obvious modifiers, together with the quantity, rarity and pack size you might be able to determine what the mods are, though). As such, it's recommended that you have a strong character before tackling such maps; otherwise the map could have many dangerous affixes to put your character in danger. Unidentified maps can be obtained as map drops or by vendoring 3x magic or rare maps of the same base type.
This bonus does not apply to unidentified unique  maps.
title: Map

text:
== Other map categories ==
Maps can drop as an influenced base. There are four different types of map influences, Shaper, Elder, Conqueror, and Originator. These maps can contain special enemies and bosses that drop map fragments that are used to challenge their respective pinnacle bosses. It is also possible to add Exarch or Eater influence to a map using the map device's eldritch beacons once unlocked.
Shaper, Elder, and Conqueror maps can drop influenced item bases, and Originator maps contain petals that grant an increased chance for items to drop with Memory Strands.
Shaper Guardian Maps use a special map base and are used to enter specific maps containing the Shaper Guardian, while Elder Guardian and Conqueror are regular influenced maps that contain the boss.
Memory influenced maps (or Originator maps) and Nightmare maps can can roll special, extra-difficult modifiers that cannot be rolled in regular maps.
Blighted Maps (and Blight-Ravaged Maps) can drop from Blight encounters in maps. Blighted Maps only contain a single extra-lengthy Blight encounter with more lanes and enemies than regular Blights.

text:
=== Map fragments ===

Map fragments are to enter special areas that often contain various high-level boss areas. Some of these areas require a full set of fragments in proper alignment to enter. Fragments can also be placed with a regular map to increase map item quantity. Vaal Fragments and Mortal Fragments also add a Vaal side areas to the map.
Scarabs can also be used to add additional modifiers to the map, and Divine Vessels are used to capture certain boss souls to upgrade a Pantheon power.

text:
The Map Device is a world object that allows the player to access certain areas in the Atlas of Worlds by placing items such as maps, map fragments, or miscellaneous map items inside it. The Map Device starts with three slots for fragments, and up to two additional slots can be unlocked.

== Accessing the Map Device ==
In the Epilogue, players will first gain access to a map device in the Karui Shores. After completing the mission A Call to Arms, the player will also receive a personal Map Device decoration which can be placed in your hideout and used instead. This personal Map Device can then be used by any character that has completed Act 10.
A map device is also found in The Chamber of Sins Level 1 in Act 7, which is used to enter Maligaro's Sanctum using Maligaro's MapMaligaro's Map"Certain maps can only be rendered in the most vivid of viscera." - Inquisitor Maligaro. This Map Device cannot be used to open any other maps.

== Mechanics ==
Clicking on the Map Device will open the Atlas. From there, you can select a visible map area on the Atlas to enter. Then, place a map item with a tier equal or higher than the map's tier to access the area.
It is also possible to place other map-related items alongside a map for bonuses:
title: Map Device

By default, the map device has 3 additional items slots usable to open and modify areas. Two additional slots can be unlocked for a total of 5 slots. To unlock the additional slots, the player must do the following, in any order:
title: Map Device

text:
Complete a 10-boss Maven's Invitation: The Atlas for the first time
Complete a Nightmare map for the first time
For special areas that don't use maps to access, the receptacle will only accept valid items to be placed within it. Generally, only one item is required, but for areas that require a set of fragments, the fragments will need to be arranged in a certain order. Right-clicking the item will automatically focus the screen to the area and place the relevant fragments into the Map Device.
The map device interface comes with a collapsible 4x5 mini-inventory or "rucksack" that can store maps, map fragments, and currency items. This inventory is shared with the map device interface for Kirac (Maven's Invitations) and Eagon (memory threads) to allow for quick crafting.
The player will also unlock various upgrades to the map device as they progress through the endgame, such as enabling Maven, Exarch, or Eater beacons that permit Maven-witnessing a map boss or adding Exarch or Eater influence to your maps, or unlocking additional Atlas Passive Skill Tree presets to quickly switch between up to 3 different Atlas tree layouts. Progress on these beacons can be seen on the center of the Atlas UI. The buttons to activate them can be seen on the right side of the map receptacle. Only one of these beacons can be active at a time.
Six portals to a map or endgame area are opened when the Map Device is activated. A portal is consumed each time you enter the area, and the number of portal uses are shared within a party.

== Lore ==
Players encountered two Map Devices in throughout the Act 1 to 10. The Ancient Reverie Device in The Chamber of Sins Level 1, which was repaired before Act 7 and allowed the player character to use Maligaro's MapMaligaro's Map"Certain maps can only be rendered in the most vivid of viscera." - Inquisitor Maligaro during Act 7. The device cannot be used again afterwards. The player also encountered another nonfunctional map device in the Eternal Laboratory subarea of The Solaris Temple Level 2. That map device (known as the Reverie Device) was made by Malachai, and is canonically a copy of the device in the Chamber of Sins. The Reverie Device was previously functional until version 3.0 in the Merciless difficulty of The Solaris Temple Level 2.
A third device was located in The Templar Laboratory which was made by Valdo Caeserius, though this area is no longer accessible due to the change of endgame timelines. This map device exploded during the epilogue of the Conquerors of the Atlas expansion. The map device in The Templar Laboratory was functional from version 3.0 until 3.9. This map device is also used in Path of Exile Mobile, 20 years before the first game. A fourth device exists inside of The Shaper's Realm.
In previous expansions Conquerors of the Atlas and Echoes of the Atlas (version 3.9 to 3.16), player restored a fifth map device from spare parts in the Vault of Venarius as part of the Picking Up the Pieces quest; it is implied that these were remnants of the map device Venarius used to encounter the Elder. In the same patches, a sixth device can be seen

of the Picking Up the Pieces quest; it is implied that these were remnants of the map device Venarius used to encounter the Elder. In the same patches, a sixth device can be seen during Sirus boss fight, which is located on the Cathedral Rooftop (in the Atlas of Worlds, not the The Cathedral Rooftop in Oriath). This map device connects to the one in the Templar Laboratory (now restored), allowing the player to chase down Sirus. The Sirus encounter is not part of the current storyline, and the boss encounter is considered an interactable "memory" that generated by the power of the Atlas.
In the expansion Siege of the Atlas, Commander Kirac explains that the Citizen Vanguard has secured at least 3 functional map devices set up in the bunker at the Karui Shores. More decorations similar to the personal Map Device can be seen in the Kirac's Vault subarea of the Karui Shores. Portals from the map device in either Karui Shores or hideout are shared, preventing the ability to open two different map instances at once. When opening a map that contains a Smuggler's Cache as part of Kirac's master mission, he claims that the "criminals" may possess their own map device.

A memory influenced map, also referred to as an Originator influenced map or Tier 16.5 map, is a special type of map that contains the influence of the Originator. Memory influenced maps have the implicit modifier Area is Influenced by the Originator's Memories. They primarily differ from other map influence types due to being able to roll different affixes from regular maps and have a greater chance to drop items with memory strands.

== Acquisition ==
title: Memory influenced map

text:
Starting from tier 3 maps, non-unique maps can rarely randomly spawn a cluster of rose petals that deterministically drops a memory influenced map of the current map's tier.
After encountering Eagon and discovering a Memory Tear, Eagon will offer a series of pre-determined memory influenced maps; this series of maps is known as a memory thread, and begins the Threads of the Originator quest line. The final map of each memory thread is a memory guardian map. After completing the quest, memory tears can appear randomly in any non-unique map found on the Atlas of any tier. They cannot appear in Shaper Guardian Maps, Vaal Temple MapVaal Temple MapMonster Level: 83Area contains 10 additional guarded Vaal VesselsCorruptedTravel to a Map by using this in a personal Map Device. Maps can only be used once., or Nightmare maps, however.
Tier 16 maps have a chance to drop as memory influenced maps. Internally, these are referred to as "tier 16.5 maps". These have the same drop conditions as regular maps and are affected by any mechanics that affect map drops. No other Tiers of memory influenced maps can be obtained randomly. It is possible to drop Shaper Guardian, Elder Guardian, or Conqueror maps with memory influence.
Unique maps, Nightmare maps, and other map variants such as blighted maps cannot have memory influence.
Maps affected by a Templar AstrolabeTemplar AstrolabeStack Size: 10Adds a Shaped Region to a quadrant of the AtlasRight click this item and then left click a Map on your Atlas to apply a Shaped Region. are memory influenced.

== Mechanics ==
title: Memory influenced map

text:
Equipments in memory influenced maps have a greater chance to drop with Memory Strands.
Players can collect Rose Petals from killing Originator-influenced monsters or clusters of petals randomly scattered throughout the map. Rose petals increase the chance for items to drop with memory strands. Certain memory thread altars have effects that automatically consume petals to activate an effect. All collected petals are lost on death, but not when switching areas.
Memory influenced maps can have modifiers from the regular map modifier pool as well as most Nightmare map modifiers.

A mine (or remote mine) is a type of proxy. Mine skills throw a device that uses that skill when detonated. Placed mines reserve mana while placed and most mines create an aura that affects nearby enemies.

== Mechanics ==
title: Mine

text:
=== Throwing mines ===
When a character uses a mine skill, they throw the mine(s) to the target location. Throwing a mine counts as using a skill, but not as casting or attacking. 
Characters have a base mine throwing speed of 0.3 seconds. When multiple mines are thrown in a single action, the throwing time is increased based on the number of additional mines - stats that grant additional mines show help text stating (Throwing Mines takes 10% more time for each additional Mine thrown).
Throwing a mine uses mana and reserves an amount of mana, indicated by the skill's mana reservation. The mine will continue to reserve mana until it is detonated or destroyed.
Once a thrown mine lands on the ground it becomes invisible to enemies. This is mostly relevant to PvP since there are no monsters that use mines.

Right click to remove from a socket., create mines with an aura that becomes active while those mines are placed and alive. The effects of these auras stack cumulatively, up to a limit specified by the skill. These auras are affected by aura modifiers. They have a base radius of 3.5 metres and are scaled by modifiers to area, including those specific to auras. 
Mines remain active for a limited duration, after which they expire. Mine duration is specific to each mine skill. If a mine is not detonated before it expires, it is destroyed. Mine duration is not affected by skill effect duration modifiers. Likewise, mine duration modifiers do not affect the duration of skill effects created by mines.
title: Mine

text:
Mines will be destroyed if they take any damage.
Mines cannot be targeted directly, but they are vulnerable to area of effect damage.
Mines cannot be damaged while they are traveling through the air, or while they are detonating.
Mines are invulnerable for 2 seconds after they have been thrown.
There is a limit on the number of mines a character can have active at one time. By default, a character can have 15 mines active at once. Throwing an additional mine that would exceed the active mine limit will cause the oldest mine to be destroyed. There are passive skills that can increase this limit.

=== Detonating mines ===

While the player's character has any mines active, the Detonate Mines action (mapped to D by default) becomes available. Using the Detonate Mines action initiates a detonation sequence starting with the mine closest to the target location. The detonation sequence detonates the first mine instantly, then after a brief delay, another mine within a short range of the previous one will also be detonated. This continues in an accelerating fashion, where the delay between detonating the next mine decreases each time. Once there are no more mines within proximity to the last one detonated, the detonation sequence will stop.
The mine skill gem will state what its Base Mine Detonation Time is, and that time is modified by Detonation Speed modifiers. Each successive mine detonation in a given detonation sequence has 10% More Detonation Speed.
