text:
=== Mine skill use ===
Mines release their skill effect almost immediately after their detonation, then finish the rest of their attack or cast time, then die or re-arm. This means speed modifiers are generally not useful for mine skills, though they're not completely without effect. For example, a faster use time will allow mines to detonate an additional time sooner, and a slower use time will allow them to stay alive longer to enable leech with Machina MittsMachina MittsMurder MittsEvasion: (363-486)Energy Shield: (75-98)Requires Level 67, 51 Dex, 51 Int(200-250)% increased Evasion and Energy Shield1% of Damage dealt by your Mines is Leeched to you as Life(30-20)% reduced Recovery rate of Life and Energy Shield5% increased Recovery rate of Life and Energy Shield per Power ChargeLose a Power Charge each second if you have not Detonated Mines RecentlyBiology is but a machine, begetting effusion of energies; death is but a curse, that can be given... or reversed.. 
Mines have a targeting radius of 6 metres. This is a maximum; mines do not target enemies outside the range of their skill, which may be smaller.

=== Mines as separate entities ===
Like other proxies, mines are separate entities that use the player's skill, and that skill contains the player stats. This includes modifiers to damage, debuffs, and practically all on-hit effects, such as Curse Enemies with Frostbite on Hit. The skill does not contain effects that specifically check the character, such as most on-kill effects.

Minions are entities separate from the player: they are allies, but not party members. Unlike proxies, minions have their own skills. They do not possess the player's stats unless those stats specifically affect minions or allies.

text:
=== Duration ===
Minion Duration is affected by both modifiers to skill effect duration and minion duration.

Example - [Tested 3.23] Summon Skeletons has a base duration of 20.00 seconds as per the gem description. If one takes the Enduring Bond wheel (northeast of the witch's starting position), it adds 3 sources of minion duration (+12%, +12%, +20%) and one source of skill effect duration (+20%). This totals to +44% minion duration and +20% skill effect duration. The final duration calculation is: 20.00s * (1 + (0.44 + 0.20)) = 20.00s * 1.64 = 32.80s duration.
Final/current minion duration can be verified by hovering over that minion skill when it's assigned a slot in the skill bar, as this displays the skill's stats post-calculation/modification.

text:
Modifiers generally change various aspects of the entity they are affecting. Most commonly modifiers apply stats, however they can also apply buffs or grant skills and can often be found on items, monsters, strongboxes or areas.
A modifier should be seen as an instance of change applied to an entity. A basic modifier does nothing on its own, it is given the effect by the associated stats (and their values), buffs and skills.

== Mechanics overview ==
A modifier applies statistics, a buff or grants a skill to an entity. Modifiers are specific to items, monsters, strongboxes or areas.
Since not all statistics have a visible text, it is possible that some effects are granted by the modifier but are not visible to the player. On the wiki, some of these effects have a custom text specific to the wiki and are noted with (HIDDEN) in the description. In particular area and monster effects may be hidden from the player.
Modifiers can either be innately applied (as "implicit" modifier) to entities, be granted under specific conditions or randomly generated.
Some specific circumstances like the rarity of a monster, being touched or possessed by a Tormented Spirit, etc can also apply modifiers innately without them being randomly generated.
Modifier generation is gated by specific conditions that govern if and how likely a modifier is going to appear:
title: Modifier

text:
Mod domain governs the type of entity the modifier is going to appear and may confer some specific rules (such as the number of affixes).
Mod generation type determines how the modifier is generated, for example whether it's a prefix, suffix, corrupted or always applied (like on unique items)
Mod level governs the minimum required level of the entity for a modifier to appear (i.e. the item level, monster level, area level), and for items only raises the item's level requirement to 80% of its value
Mod group/family prevents other modifiers from the same family to be randomly generated on the same entity
Tags in conjunction with weights are used to further restrict the types of modifiers that can appear and set the relative chance to be randomly applied. (for example, shaper and elder get a corresponding tag)
The values of stats include a minimum and maximum value, which is most commonly used on items - the actual value of the stat in the cases where minimum and maximum are not the same will be randomized within with equal chances, so for example a Stat with a minimum value of 1 and a maximum value of 3, can either be 1, 2 or 3 at 1/3 chance for each value.
If a buff is specified, Modifiers also include a value for the buff, but unlike for Stats it is not randomized and fixed.
If a skill is specified, the specified skill (at the specified level) will be granted to the relevant entity. The modifier does not include values for the skill other then the level as they're defined by the skill itself. Often this is found on items, where they grant skills, such as The Whispering IceT

text:
== Local and global ==
Modifiers can be categorized as "local" or "global" modifiers.

=== Local ===
The concept of "local" modifiers has broadened since its original technical definition. This can be seen by the use of (local) in the trade site for modifiers that failed to meet the original criteria of just base stat modifications, like #% chance to Poison on Hit.
Currently, local modifiers can be identified by fulfilling any of the following requirements:
title: Modifier

text:
Item Properties: The modifier is unconditional and could affect innate properties of the item
Hand-specific: The modifier explicitly states that it applies to the item, such as "with this Weapon"
Weapon Hit Effect: The modifier is on a weapon and could apply on a hit with a generic weapon, unrelated to the numeric damage dealt
Item Properties: Item properties encompass all default properties of an item, including its base stats, attribute and level requirements, and sockets and links. Base stats can be found at the top of the item's tooltip. For example, #% increased Attack Speed and Adds # to # Physical Damage on a weapon will modify the "Attacks per Second" and "Physical Damage" stat on the weapon itself. Certain stats may not be immediately obvious, as most base items have that stat's default value at 0. For example, Adds # to # Fire Damage on a Solarine BowSolarine BowBowPhysical Damage: 16-24Elemental Damage: (121-133) to (184-197)Critical Strike Chance: 5.50%Attacks per Second: 1.30Requires Level 70, 212 DexAdds (121-133) to (184-197) Fire Damage directly adds to the weapon's base damage, of which Fire Damage is usually 0 for weapons. Default base stats are displayed in white, while modified base stats are displayed in blue (with the exception of fire/cold/lightning/chaos damage on weapons, which are colour-coded based on their damage type and have a base stat of 0).
title: Modifier

text:
Quality effects are always considered local as they affect an item's base stat(s). Catalyst quality effects are also local, which instead functions as #% increased X Modifier magnitudes modifiers, which are the only type of local modifier that can be found on jewellery (as jewellery only have implicit modifiers, level requirements, and sometimes sockets as base stats).
The following is a list of local base stat modifiers which can be quickly identified as local, if unconditional (Note that this list does not cover all local mods, just local mods that affect base stats):
Weapons: #% increased Physical Damage, Adds # to # X Damage, #% increased Attack Speed, #% increased Critical Strike Chance, +# metres to Weapon Range
Any other type of #% increased Damage is never local, as generic weapons only have base Physical Damage.
Armour: +# to Armour/Evasion Rating/maximum Energy Shield/Ward, #% increased Armour/Evasion/Energy Shield/Ward
Shields: +# to Armour/Evasion Rating/maximum Energy Shield, #% increased Armour/Evasion/Energy Shield, +# to Block Chance
Flasks: All flask modifiers are local
Jewellery: Only #% increased X Modifier magnitudes (including Catalyst quality) and modifiers relating to level and sockets are local
Maps: #% increased Item Quantity, #% increased Item Rarity, #% Monster Pack Size
Hand-specific: Modifiers that include "with this Weapon" or "Main/Off Hand" should be considered local, despite being conditional, as they only apply to attacks using that specific hand/weapon. These types of modifiers are technically global modifiers that apply locally to one or
title: Modifier

text: l, despite being conditional, as they only apply to attacks using that specific hand/weapon. These types of modifiers are technically global modifiers that apply locally to one or both hand(s), and therefore cannot be scaled by other local increases.
title: Modifier

text:
Weapons that add specific damage to the main or off-hand also display these values in their base stats as if combined, although they display correctly in the character stats screen (C by default) and skill tooltips as well as being correctly handled for Battlemage. Other main/off-hand stats like (50-100)% more Main Hand attack speedWingsOfEntropyMainHandAttackSpeedFinalUnique__1_Intrinsic(50-100)% more Main Hand attack speed do not visually affect the base stats but are correctly reflected in the character stats screen. Two-handed weapons are always considered as being in the main hand (left), while shields are always considered in the off-hand (right).
Weapon Hit Effect: Stats on weapons that apply on an attack hit with a generic (modifier-less) weapon (e.g. #% Chance to Poison on Hit, #% Chance to Maim, #% of Physical Attack Damage Leeched as Life) are considered local. Flat modifiers to accuracy or chance to hit on weapons are also considered local, as chance to hit is hand-specific and determined on hit. While Poison and Bleeding chance are local, Ignite chance is always global, as generic weapons do not have base fire damage and therefore cannot ignite.
title: Modifier

text:
=== Global ===
Global modifiers encompass all other modifiers that are not local. All conditional stats are global except for the main/off-hand stats listed above. Global stats never modify an item's base stats and instead apply to the character's stats, and therefore cannot interact directly with other local modifiers. For example, the damage from  Adds # to # Physical Damage on a weapon is scaled by #% increased Physical Damage and quality on a weapon, but Adds # to # Physical Damage to Attacks from the ring is not (as rings do not have base damage) and added separately in addition to the weapon's base damage before calculating any other global increased/more modifiers. Modifiers that state "Global" are always global.
In general, conditional modifiers should always be considered global.
Hybrid modifiers (modifiers with more than one line per stat) treat each line independently. A hybrid modifier can have both local and global parts, such as of Tacati - 30% chance to Poison on Hit, (26-30)% increased Chaos Damage (Suffix).

== Conditions ==
Modifiers usually include conditions which are used to determine how they appear. These are generally used to govern the creation of explicit modifiers on entities.

=== Domain ===
The domain of a modifier specifies what kind of game object it applies to. The domains are primarily reverse engineered, as detailed information has been removed from the game files.

=== Generation type ===
The mod generation determines "how" the mod will be created on an item. The generation types are primarily reverse engineered, as detailed information has been removed from the game files.
title: Modifier

=== Mod Level ===
The required level of the relevant entity. For example, this can be the required item level or a monster level. 
However, there are cases where this is not respected: in particular this is the case for any mods that are directly given to other entities, such as implicit mods including enchantments or monsters with innate mods.
The mod level is also a factor in calculating the level requirement of items; raising the level requirement up to 80% requirement of the mod (with the requirement rounded down to the nearest whole integer).
In particular this is the case for mods on unique items and for enchantments

=== Group/family ===
Each modifier belongs to one or more groups (or families). These restrict which modifiers may appear on an object together. Only one modifier from any given group may appear on an object; in other words, all modifiers belonging to a group are mutually exclusive with one another.
This is often used used to influence the crafting of items, where players will add a mod from an undesired group of modifiers to block it. This means the undesired mods in that group will not be added when crafting currency is used. Together with the item level requirements, this creates the "tiered" system of modifiers.

=== Tags ===
Mods use the internal Tag system to determine on which entities they can appear and how likely they are to appear on entities. Tags are classified as spawn weight tag and mod tag:

=== Spawn weight tag ===
Spawn weight tag primarily functions like this:

Find the Tags on the basetype.
Match the Tags against the mod's list of tags.
For the found mods get the associated spawn weighting of the tag.
If the spawn weighting is zero, discard the mod, otherwise use it.
If multiple tags apply, the left-most tags are most important, where the right most tags are the least.
So, for example:

For example, when a Fertile CatalystFertile CatalystStack Size: 10Adds quality that enhances Life and Mana modifiers on a ring, amulet or beltReplaces other quality typesRight click this item then left click a ring, amulet or belt to apply it. Has greater effect on lower item level, non-unique jewellery. The maximum quality is 20%. is applied to jewellery, it will apply a quality that increases the magnitude of modifiers with the Life or Mana tags, up to 20%. A modifier normally granting "+79 to Maximum Life" on the item will be enhanced to instead grant "+94 to Maximum Life", and a modifier normally granting "Non-Channelling Skills have -7 to Total Mana Cost" will be enhanced to instead grant "Non-Channelling Skills have -8 to Total Mana Cost". Modifiers enhanced this way will round down decimal values.
Fossils multiply the weights of modifiers that match the type of the fossil, For example, Metallic FossilMetallic FossilStack Size: 20More Lightning modifiersNo Physical modifiersPlace in a Resonator to influence item crafting.s will multiply the weight of modifiers with the Lightning tag by 1000%, and the modifiers with Physical tags by 0%. Effectively, this will result in modifiers with the lightning tag to appear 10x more oftenwhen the item is rolled, and modifiers with the physical tag never rolling.

==== Heist Enchantments ====
Many heist-exclusive enchantments can modify the magnitudes of modifiers of certain tags, both positively and negatively. These enchantments can be acquired either through the use of a Tailoring OrbTailoring OrbStack Size: 20Adds or replaces an enchantment on a body armourThis may reforge the body armour's socketsRight click this item then left click on the item you wish to modify. on a body armour, use of a Tempering OrbTempering OrbStack Size: 20Adds or replaces an enchantment on a weaponThis may reforge the weapon's socketsRight click this item then left click on the item you wish to modify. on a weapon, or found already rolled as an item in a Curio Display at the end of a Blueprint wing. (All Grand Heist layouts with "Enchanted Rare Body Armour" and "Enchanted Rare Weapon" as a reward type).
For example, the enchantment 8% increased Explicit Life Modifier magnitudes will enhance a modifier that normally grants "+100 to Maximum Life" to granting "+108 to Maximum Life". Some Heist enchantments come with downsides. The hybrid modifier 10% increased Explicit Life Modifier magnitudes + 25% reduced Explicit Speed Modifier magnitudes will increase the magnitudes of modifiers with the Physical tags by 10%, but reduce the magnitudes of modifiers with the Speed tag, such as 19% increased Attack Speed by 25%.
title: Modifier

text:
==== Harvest Crafting ====
Many Harvest crafting methods interact with modifier tags. 
The craft "Reforge a Rare item with random modifiers, including a (tag) modifier" will completely reforge the modifiers of a Rare item, similar to a Chaos OrbChaos OrbStack Size: 20Reforges a rare item with new random modifiersRight click this item then left click a rare item to apply it., while guaranteeing a modifier with the specified tag. If there are no valid tags in the mod pool to roll for the selected item, the craft cannot be used. The add/remove crafts work as expected.
The craft "Change a modifier that grants (Element) Resistance into a similar-tier modifier that grants (Different Element) Resistance" will swap a resistance modifier of a certain element into that of another one.
title: Modifier

text:
This method works for modifiers beyond the generic "+#% to (Element) Resistance". It also works for the incursion architect-exclusive resistance-granting modifiers. For example, the modifier of Puhuarte - +(46-48)% to Cold Resistance, (30-50)% increased Damage with Hits against Chilled Enemies (Suffix) can be reforged into of Puhuarte - +(46-48)% to Fire Resistance, (45-52) to (75-78) added Fire Damage against Burning Enemies (Suffix) and vice versa. This can be used to swap to another, more desired mod, or to effectively "divine" the modifier. This is generally more desirable than with the normal resistance rolls, as modifiers with "(30–50)% increased Damage with Hits against Chilled Enemies" have much higher roll variance and thus more value can be obtained.
This craft preserves the tier, but not the roll within that tier. This property may be used to reroll a higher value intentionally, by switching back and forth between your desired element and another one. Each time you switch back to the type that you want, the modifier values will be re-rolled. This method is recommended for builds with high levels of investment, as usually a few % of resistance is not worth spending the lifeforce.

== Modifier Tier Rating ==
Modifier Tier Rating is a mechanic first introduced in Necropolis league's gravecrafting that is able to prevent low tier modifiers from rolling. The exact mechanics are not fully known, however there are two popular models that may explain how this system works.

text:
=== Redistribution model ===
The more popular explanation is that it can block low tier modifiers without directly affecting the relative weight of mod types during mod generation. Unlike fossils, which act like a multiplier to the weights of certain modifier types (e.g. 10x weight for Fire modifiers), modifier tier rating prevents a percentage of eligible mod tiers within each mod type, exclusive, rounded up to the nearest whole number:

With +50 to Modifier Tier Rating, it will prevent the lowest 34% of mod tiers from rolling. With +100, the lowest 50%, and +200, the lowest 67%, and so on. The weights of the blocked modifiers are redistributed to the tiers of modifiers of the same mod type, such that the relative weights within a mod type remain the same, and the relative weights for each mod type against the total pool of prefixes/suffixes remain the same. Modifiers with only a single (eligible) tier are unaffected by modifier tier rating.
For example, assume a modifier type (e.g. the prefix #% increased Fire Damage) has three tiers that can roll at the item's item level, with Tiers 3/2/1 having weights of 1000/600/200 respectively. With a modifier tier rating of +100, preventing the lowest 50% tier modifiers from rolling, exclusive, this prevents Tier 3 from rolling and redistributes the weight of 1000 to the other eligible tiers. The weights of Tiers 3/2/1 are now 0/1350/450 respectively. Tier 2 is still 3x more likely to roll than Tier 1, and chance of rolling any increased Fire Damage prefix versus any other prefix modifier type is still the same with a total weight of 1800.

Necropolis league was a challenge league. It launched on March 29, 2024 as part of Path of Exile: Necropolis in version 3.24.0. It ended on July 23, 2024.

== League mechanic ==
Players will meet Undertaker Arimor, who will give you the Lantern of Arimor. You can use the Lantern before you enter a zone, revealing types of monsters that will appear in the zone, as well as a modifier attached to them. These modifiers cause monsters to be haunted, enhancing them in various ways, and can be rearranged to have them affect a different monster. Sometimes, the modifiers will cause monsters to become Devoted instead, providing beneficial bonuses when killed. Devoted monsters appear more often the more haunted monsters you kill.
Haunted monsters will sometimes spawn with Unresolved Anguish, allowing their corpses to be collected and sent to the Necropolis. You can bury these corpses at the Necropolis to add its attached crafting modifier to the Tome of Arimor, which will consume all buried corpses to create a random rare equipment, or a unique item with a certain set of corpses.
In addition, Haunted monsters can drop an Ember of the Allflame, which can be used on the Lantern to convert a monster into a different type. Monsters from the Allflame Ember have special effects, such as granting increased experience, turning them into harmless frogs, or being able to drop tattoos.

Nightmare maps are a special type of Tier 16 map which can be used to enter maps containing "Nightmare" bosses, enhanced versions of certain league mechanic bosses. These maps are meant to act as a bridge to uber pinnacle boss content and drop fragments that grant access to those encounters. They are not part of the Atlas of Worlds, and are not affected by certain Atlas mechanics such as Astrolabes. They may sometimes be referred to by the community as a tier 17 map, purple map, T17, or uber map, due to being reworked versions of the former Tier 17 maps.

== Mechanics ==
Nightmare maps have an area area level of 83 like other T16 maps. They are somewhat similar to but more challenging than Shaper Guardian maps.

Nightmare maps are affected by the Atlas Passive Tree.
Nightmare maps are affected by map fragments from your Map Device when opened.
Nightmare maps differ from regular T16 maps in the following ways:
title: Nightmare Map

text:
Nightmare maps cannot be used to open regular T16 Atlas maps. They can be used to open Nightmare map exclusive areas located behind the Atlas voidstone sockets.
Nightmare maps roll from a range of modifiers that can be found in Red Tier maps (tier 11-16) and exclusive modifiers that can also be found in memory influenced maps.
Nightmare map-exclusive modifiers grant a significant modifier to pack size, item rarity, currency drops, map drops, or scarab drops.

Nightmare maps will always have 6 affixes. They can have 8 affixes when corrupted.

== Acquisition ==
Voidstones, when socketed into the Atlas of Worlds, have a chance to convert Tier 16 maps into a Nightmare map. This chance does not increase linearly per Voidstone socketed. The initial conversion chance can be calculated with the following formula:

, where 
  
    
      v
    
    \color [rgb]{0.6392156862745098,0.5529411764705883,0.42745098039215684}v
  
 is the number of socketed Voidstones.

With average map investment and four Voidstones, a player can expect a Nightmare map drop roughly once every 5 maps. To prevent a massive disparity of Nightmare map drops with certain "juicing" strategies, Nightmare map drops are subject to "diminishing returns" within a map; this means that the first Nightmare map dropped in a map will use the above conversion rate, then diminish to a unannounced point for subsequent drops in the same map.
Nightmare maps cannot drop inside a Nightmare maps.

== Drops ==
Each Nightmare map boss has an exclusive unique item, with an approximate 5% drop chance. Each boss also has an exclusive exceptional support gem, also with an approximate 5% drop chance. Each boss can also only drop specific uber pinnacle fragments, matching the pinnacle bosses found in their quadrant.
title: Nightmare Map

text:
The number of fragments dropped is indirectly scaled by area item quantity modifiers (including Eldritch altars); certain estimated breakpoints will guarantee a specific range of fragment drops; the average number of fragments dropped scales almost linearly with IIQ until at least 250% IIQ.

title: Original Sin

text: The passive skill tree is a large network of passive skills, or nodes, that provide stats that affect the player's character (or their minions). All classes use the same tree, but start in different places. When a character levels up or completes certain quests, they gain one passive skill point, which allows the player to allocate a node on the skill tree that is connected to another allocated node.
title: Passive skill

text:
== Mechanics ==
Characters can accrue 99 passive skill points from levels, 23 points from quests, and 1 optional point from the quest Deal with the Bandits if all three Bandit Lords were killed. Players can refund skill points using skill refund points acquired from Orbs of RegretOrb of RegretStack Size: 40Grants a passive skill refund pointRight click on this item to use it. and quest rewards (up to 20), as well as the Respecialisation option using Gold via NPCs.
The Scion's Ascendancy classes grant additional passive skill points, typically 5 in most setups (6 passive points can be acquired on the Reliquarian if you skip taking the Jewelry Notable).
While the passive tree may seem complicated, it actually only has two parts. It can be thought of as a map with suburbs and roads. The clusters of related passive nodes that boost a specific area (swords, spells, damage types, evasion, etc.) are like suburbs.  These will form the bulk of a character's build. The pathways between these clusters, comprised entirely of nodes that give +10 to a certain attribute, are like roads. Some of these roads can cover a great distance much quicker than if the player detours through the suburbs: what may look like a short path with passive boosts could be much longer than taking the +10 to attribute path.
Pressing C (default) in-game and hovering over each of the three attributes will show what these do. Anything the attributes don't do, such as increase ranged damage or attack speed, will likely be handled by passive nodes on the skill 'tree'.
title: Passive skill

text:
=== Layout ===
The character classes and their approximate starting position on the tree
title: Passive skill

text:
The tree can be divided into three primary sectors of equal size, one-third of the relatively circular tree, surrounding a central wheel. They are the north or blue sector, the southwest or red sector, and the southeast or green sector.
The north or blue sector is also known as the magic sector; passives there boost intelligence, elemental damage, energy shield, wand damage, minion stats, etc. Everything related to magic and the skills normally found on blue gems.
The southwest or red sector is also known as the melee sector; passives there boost strength, armour, physical damage, and nearly every known aspect of melee combat, as well as all skills normally found on red gems.
The southeast or green sector is also known as the ranged sector; passives there boost dexterity, ranged projectile damage, evasion, most known aspects of ranged combat, and all skills normally found on green gems.
As the player moves to the borders between sectors, the passive skills available there become more hybridized between the two.
Each character starts at the border of the inner wheel of the tree at a different location. The Witch, for example, starts at the due-north border of the inner wheel, smack in the middle of the blue sector showing her preference for magic. The wheel of character images (on the right) shows which position each class starts in and therefore their preferred method of combat; the Marauder starts in the middle of the red sector showing a preference for melee combat, and the Ranger starts in the middle of the green sector for ranged combat, with the other characters starti
title: Passive skill

text:
s in the middle of the red sector showing a preference for melee combat, and the Ranger starts in the middle of the green sector for ranged combat, with the other characters starting in a position to put them in more of a hybrid role to start.
The exception is the Scion, who starts in the center of the passive tree, giving her the flexibility to move into more specialized parts of the tree.
While nothing hinders players from immediately leaving the starting area to make a character outside of their recommended archetype (for example, a melee physical Witch), such a player would have a hard time acquiring build-appropriate skill gems early in the campaign (they would have to trade or buy it from other players or level another character to Act 6 first), and their Ascendancy choices would likely have a harder time supporting such a build.
title: Passive skill

text:
== Passive nodes ==
There are several types of passive skills.

=== Small passives ===

Small passive skills only grant attributes or minor bonuses to the character.

=== Notable passives ===

Notable passive skills grant notable improvements to the character.
Some notable passive skills can only be acquired from cluster jewels or anointing. Cluster jewels provide a unique set of notables. While most notable passives on the main skill tree can be anointed, there are some notable skills that can only be obtained by anointing (29 as of game version 3.25).

=== Masteries ===
title: Passive skill

text:
When you allocate a cluster's Notable passive skill through the normal method (that is, travelling there through the skill tree), you may allocate a Mastery passive on that cluster. Masteries are present in all clusters outside of the class's starting area, and allocating it lets you acquire one passive effect within the cluster category, indicated by their icons, e.g. health, two-handed weapons, curses. The set of mastery passives offered are shared among their respective cluster categories.  Once you select an option from a category, you cannot select that option again by taking the mastery passive of another cluster of the same category.

Right click to remove from the Socket.) will not let you allocate a Mastery passive.

=== Keystone passives ===

Keystone passive skills significantly alters how the character functions. Some of them are granted exclusively from unique cluster jewel and unique Timeless Jewel.

=== Jewel sockets ===
Jewel sockets are passives that can be filled with jewels. By default, they are empty and don't grant any bonuses. There are currently 21 sockets distributed around the tree, 15 of which are "basic" and 6 of them being Large Jewel Sockets, which can socket cluster jewels.

=== Ascendancy passives ===
title: Passive skill

text:
Every character has an opportunity to gain a subclass called Ascendancy class that grants access to an Ascendancy skill tree specific for the character class chosen.

== Tattoos ==
Tattoos can be applied to a passive skill in the skill tree to transform the passive into a different passive. Most tattoos are applied to the minor +10 attribute nodes on the tree, and some on +30 attribute notables. Up to 50 tattoos can be applied on one character.

== Runegrafts ==
Runegrafts can be applied to a Mastery passive skill in the skill tree to transform it into a different passive. Only one of each type of Runegraft can be applied at a time.
title: Passive skill

text:
== Planning your build ==
With the number of nodes on the skill tree, the variety of starting positions, the number of passive skill points you can gain and the variety of available Jewels, the number of possible configurations of skill builds on the tree is so large it can for all intents and purposes be considered infinite. Planning a good build in this tree can be a daunting task for many players, but there are ways to make it much easier.
There is a VERY effective Search function at the top of the passive tree viewing window. If you put a word, or even part of a word, into this search function, every single passive node in the entire tree that has this word either within its name or its main effect description sentence will be highlighted by a pulsing glow, easily visible even with the tree view zoomed out to the maximum. You can then quickly hover your mouse over that node for more details on what it specifically does, and compare its position to the parts of the tree you have already allocated points to. 
To then proceed with an effective build design, do the following:
title: Passive skill

text:
Think of an effect that you want, such as a specific Passive listed within another page on the Wiki that sounded attractive, or a more general concept such as passives that affect Shields.
Type a corresponding key word into the search function, such as part of the name of the specific Passive you're looking for or a concept word like Shield.
Zoom out the tree view and find the corresponding glowing nodes, and hover your mouse over them to check the corresponding direct effects
Compare the positions of these passive clusters with the node path you've already unlocked, and determine the most efficient path that uses the lowest number of Passive points to get you to the desired nodes and/or puts you nearby/through other nodes with other effects that will also greatly help you in other ways later.
Get the passive skill points through the normal means, and apply them according to plan.
With a bit of work you should be able to plan out an extremely effective character design using the above process.

=== Unique Jewel interactions ===
Some unique jewels can grant different bonuses depending on the specific socket they are socketed into and/or the other passive skills that have or have not been allocated.

text:
Poison is an ailment that deals chaos damage over time to the affected target.

== Mechanics ==
A hit of damage that has a chance to poison is capable of inflicting poison. Only physical and chaos damage are able to inflict poison by default. Unlike Freeze, Ignite, and Shock, critical strikes that deal physical or chaos damage do not inherently inflict poison.
Poison is a stacking debuff. Each application—or 'stack'—of poison deals chaos damage over time until its duration expires. There is no limit to the number of poison stacks a target can have. A single "hit" can apply a maximum of one poison stack, therefore having more than 100% chance to poison grants no additional benefit.
title: Poison

text:
=== Damage ===
The base damage per second dealt by a single poison is based on 30% of the combined flat physical and chaos damage of the hit. This DPS is not based on hit damage taken by the enemy; it is a separate calculation, starting from flat damage (base and added modified by conversion) before modifiers. This prevents stats like chaos resistance from mitigating poison twice. It also means hit damage modifiers such as penetration or double damage do not affect poison damage, except indirectly through e.g. Cruelty SupportCruelty SupportSupport, DurationIcon: YLevel: (1-20)Cost & Reservation Multiplier: 140%Requires Level 18Supports any skill that hits enemies. Portions of poisons inflicted by non-chaos damage are affected by modifiers that would increase the source damage type for the corresponding portion of the poison damage.
However, since poison only deals chaos damage, it is only mitigated by the defender's modifiers to chaos damage taken. So for example, poisons inflicted with physical damage would deal full damage against enemies that are immune to physical damage. However, the hit must deal at least one point of chaos damage, otherwise the enemy would receive no poison-eligible damage and therefore be incapable of being poisoned.

All projectiles have a speed, which can be altered by Projectile Speed modifiers. Reduced projectile speed has a maximum of 99%, but there is no limit for increased projectile speed. 
All projectiles also have a duration (which can be infinite). In most cases, this duration is not mentioned on the skill itself and cannot be modified. text:
=== Ground and airborne projectiles ===
Most projectiles travel through the air. However, some travel along the ground.
Airborne projectiles can be aimed up and down cliffs and other height transitions and can impact the ground or ceiling. This can sometimes cause the projectile to miss a target's vertical hitbox when dealing with a steep angle, as they may fly over the heads of enemies or harmlessly impact the ground at the enemy's feet. Airborne projectiles will pass through most low obstacles such as small chests and rocks.
Projectiles that travel along the ground are subject to the same restrictions as a walking player. This means they cannot be fired up or down cliffs or ledges, and will instead collide with the edge. text:
== Projectile Behaviours ==
When a projectile successfully collides with an enemy or obstacle, the projectile either ends, or continues with one of the projectile behaviours described below. If an attack projectile misses a target (due to insufficient accuracy) it will continue through the target without colliding. 
Whenever a projectile collides, it will attempt each of its remaining behaviors, prioritized in this order: Split, Pierce, Fork, Chain, Return. Only a single behaviour can occur per collision. For example, a projectile with a remaining Chain and Return will Chain if a target exists to Chain to, but it will Return immediately against a single enemy. A projectile with Pierce and Chain will Pierce enemies, but can Chain from terrain with % chance to be able to Chain when colliding with terrain (as terrain cannot be pierced).

==== Split ====
title: Projectile

text:
==== Return ====

The projectile returns in the direction of its creator. Unlike other behaviours, returns allows one additional collision (per simultaneous set) against targets that were already hit. If a projectile returns directly from an enemy, that enemy cannot be hit by other returning projectiles in the same set. A projectile can normally only return once. 
Return has the lowest priority among projectile behaviours.
Sources of returning projectiles include:

title: Quality

text:
== Mechanics ==
Any item that drops with randomly generated quality can drop with up to 30% quality. This chance is weighted, with the majority of items having 0% quality, and quality above 20% being progressively more rare. Certain monster reward modifiers can also cause all non-gem items that can have quality to have 1%-30% quality. Any normal rarity or unidentified item with at least 1% quality will have a temporary Superior affix. 
Quality can be applied via currency to most equipment (quivers being the exception), as well as gems, maps, and strongboxes. Each item type has a currency item associated with it that increases its quality. Quality does not affect the requirements for using an item or the mana cost of skills.
Increasing the quality on weapons and armours also makes crafting sockets and links with Jeweller's OrbsJeweller's OrbStack Size: 20Reforges the number of sockets on an itemRight click this item then left click a socketed item to apply it. The item's quality increases the chances of obtaining more sockets. and Orbs of FusingOrb of FusingStack Size: 20Reforges the links between sockets on an itemRight click this item then left click a socketed item to apply it. The item's quality increases the chances of obtaining more links. easier. Each 1% quality improves the result by 1%. This makes obtaining many sockets and links 20% more likely on 20% quality items and even likelier on 30% quality items.
Increasing quality via currency is generally capped at 20%. However, there are certain methods that can increase quality beyond that, including:

Certain Harvest crafting crafts can apply enchantments on weapons and body armours that could change the effect of quality on that item instead of the default quality (weapon physical damage or body armour defences). text:
== Skill gems ==
Both skill gems and support gems may have quality. Every skill is affected by quality differently, but it frequently improves the damage dealt with the skill or provides small improvements like increased Area of Effect. Even those that do have their damage improved will see different improvement rates for a given amount of quality.
The quality of skill gems may be improved with a Gemcutter's PrismGemcutter's PrismStack Size: 20Improves the quality of a gemRight click this item then left click a gem to apply it. The maximum quality is 20%.. These upgrades always improve a skill's quality by 1%. Alternatively, a level 20 non-awakened support gem and a Gemcutter's PrismGemcutter's PrismStack Size: 20Improves the quality of a gemRight click this item then left click a gem to apply it. The maximum quality is 20%. can be vendored (sold to a NPC) for a level 1 gem with 20% quality.
The effect of quality scales with the base quality effect, however, only whole numbers will be granted (and thus the effect will always be rounded down); for example 3% quality on a gem with 0.5% effect will only grant 1% effect and not 1.5% effect. Effects with some degree of fractions are rounded to their natural bases (i.e. seconds will be rounded to milliseconds, etc.). 
It is possible to get a gem's quality above 20%. Corrupting a gem can increase its quality by up to 23%. Reservation is a method of using a resource, typically mana or life, to pay for auras, herald skills, buffs, mine skills, or any skill with an ongoing effect. Some items may also reserve resources. Rather than paying the cost once as with normal skills, a portion of the resource is set aside as unusable for as long as the skill is active. Reserving a resource does not affect its maximum, so percentage modifiers such as Regenerate 1% of Maximum Life are unaffected when you reserve life, for example.
Reserved resource values from Skills are multiplied by support gem cost & reservation multipliers as usual. text:
Resistance modifies the amount of damage taken from elemental (fire, cold, or lightning) or chaos damage. It can be changed with equipment, passives, buffs/debuffs, and other modifiers.
Resistances work separately from damage reduction and are not treated as such.

== Mechanics ==
Resistance reduces or increases the amount of damage taken from certain damage types, whether it is a hit or damage over time. It is calculated after damage avoidance and before damage reduction effects.
All entities have resistance values. Player resistances can be viewed in the Defence tab in the Character panel (default hotkey C). An estimate of enemy resistances are indicated by icons beneath their life bars.
Modifiers which affect "elemental resistance" apply to fire, cold, and lightning resistances equally. Sources of elemental resistance will not apply to chaos resistance, but sources that affect "all resistances" will apply to elemental and chaos resistances. Physical resistance does not exist.
Resistances have a default maximum of 75%. Having resistances above the maximum will not provide any further reduction to damage, though some mechanics will consider excess resistance values (See Uncapped resistances and Overcapped resistances). Maximum resistance can be increased with sources of +#% to Maximum [Type] Resistance(s), up to a hard limit of 90%.
Negative resistances are hard capped at -200%. The effects of x% reduced Resistance(s) is capped at 100%.

=== Damage mitigation ===

text:
==== Resistance penalties ====
A permanent penalty to all resistances (including Chaos Resistance) is applied to player characters depending on their progression in the story. It is not possible to avoid this penalty before entering the Epilogue and maps.

Completion of Part One: -30% to all resistances
Completion of Part Two: -30% to all resistances (-60% total)

=== Resistance inversion ===
Effects that treat resistances as inverted will multiply the target's capped resistances by -1. The higher the enemy's resistance value, the more benefit inversion will provide. Conversely, this modifier against an enemy with negative resistances will cause it to be treated as if it had positive resistances. Inverted resistances are still subject to maximum/minimum resistance caps.

text:
=== Resistance penetration ===

Only hits can penetrate resistances. Penetration is applied as damage is dealt, after other resistance calculations. Penetration applies to capped resistance value, so an enemy with 75% capped resistances against a hit with 30% penetration will take damage as if they had 45% resistances.
Negative resistances are capped at -200%, but penetration can exceed this value as it does not directly modify the target's resistances.
"Reverse penetration", typically in the format of Your Hits treat X Resistance as #% higher than actual value, is additive with penetration values.

=== Ignore resistances ===
Stats that grant the ability to ignore resistances prevent resistances from being calculated in the damage formula but do not affect the enemy's actual resistance stats. Mathematically, ignored resistances can be treated as always 0% and discards any further resistance increases or reductions, inversions, or penetration. This modifier can result in a damage loss if the ignored resistance was already negative.

=== Overcapped resistances ===
In-game alt text: Overcapped Resistance is the amount by which Uncapped Resistance is higher than Maximum Resistance
Overcapped resistances are your total resistances that exceed your maximum resistance value. Only resistances up to a player's maximum resistances will provide damage mitigation but overcapped resistances serve as a buffer against resistance reduction such as curses and exposure before they can reduce your resistances below your maximum resistances. It can be calculated by subtracting the uncapped resistances (on the left) from the maximum resistances (on the right) in the player's character stats menu. === Increased/Reduced resistances ===
Modifiers that increase or reduce resistances by a percentage, e.g. X% Reduced Elemental Resistances are multiplicative against your uncapped resistances. Note that this mod is distinctly different from mods like -X% to Elemental Resistances. There is a cap at 100% reduced Resistances (permanently setting your resistance to 0 and causing it to be unable to be modified further other than penetration. As reduced resistance modifiers cause your resistances to become less negative or less positive, they are detrimental for builds that use Doryani's PrototypeDoryani's PrototypeSaint's HauberkArmour: (1107-1488)Energy Shield: (190-255)Movement Speed: -5%Requires Level 67, 109 Str, 94 Int(150-200)% increased Armour and Energy Shield+(60-90) to maximum LifeDeal no Non-Lightning DamageArmour also applies to Lightning Damage taken from HitsLightning Resistance does not affect Lightning Damage takenNearby Enemies have Lightning Resistance equal to yours"This was the first step in some grand design,lost to the ages, now ours to decipher."- Dominus, High Templar or stack additional maximum resistances as they increase the investment required to reach the desired caps. The modifier X% Less Elemental Resistances works similarly but is multiplicative with itself and other sources, not additive.

text: Resonators are a class of items similar to currency items that allow for the crafting of rare items when fully socketed with fossils. Fossils can be removed from a partially-socketed resonator, but once a resonator has been fully socketed, the fossils cannot be reclaimed. Fossil modifiers that prevent certain types of modifiers from appearing supersede modifiers that grant more of a modifier type. Resonators will display a full list of modifiers granted from socketed fossils when hovered over. Resonators cannot be socketed with multiple of the same fossil. Resonators also inherit item use restrictions from socketed fossils.
title: Resonator

text:
Chaotic and Alchemical Resonators function similarly to Chaos OrbChaos OrbStack Size: 20Reforges a rare item with new random modifiersRight click this item then left click a rare item to apply it. and Orb of AlchemyOrb of AlchemyStack Size: 20Upgrades a normal item to a rare itemRight click this item then left click a normal item to apply it. respectively. Unlike these orbs, resonators cannot be used on items with metamods such as Prefixes Cannot Be Changed or Cannot roll Caster Modifiers, similar to essences.
Resonators can stack while in an unsocketed state. Players can unstack a single resonator by holding the Shift key and clicking while holding a stack of resonators. Additionally, holding the Shift key while holding a stack of fossils to socket into the resonator will prevent accidentally picking up the resonator instead, which can occur while trying to fill resonators quickly.
Resonators are considered Delve Stackable Socketable Currency. There is an older variant of this item class available, called Delve Socketable Currency. They are converted to the new item class upon pickup. The old variant is no longer obtainable.

text:
Rituals are encounters that spawn from Ritual Altars. After activating the Altar, players must defeat the enemies enclosed within the Ritual Circle, gaining Tribute in the process. Players can then spend the earned Tribute to purchase various types of rewards including pre-identified rare items. Tribute gained is tied to the area and does not carry over to Ritual Altars found in other areas.
This encounter is considered Extra Content and has a baseline greater than 8% chance to appear in any non-unique map area.

== Mechanics ==

Ritual Altars can be randomly encountered while playing through the campaign (guaranteed first encounter in The Northern Forest in Act 2) and have a baseline greater than 8% chance to randomly spawn in any end-game map. The amount of Altars that appear in each instance is either three or four. All of the Altars in an instance are part of the same set: same type, spawn pool and reward pool. Rituals will typically also spawn additional packs of monsters from the Viridian Wildwood.
title: Ritual

text:
Players must first kill the monsters guarding a ritual altar before being allowed to activate the ritual.
Clicking the altar begins the ritual and encloses players in the area of the Ritual Circle.
Monsters will spawn in multiple waves, each wave harder than the last. Tribute is earned from each monster killed.
After killing all the monsters within the ritual, or if players die or portal out before this, the combat phase ends and players can loot the altar.
All altars share a single spawn pool; when an altar is activated, all dead monsters within that altar circle get added to the pool. Monsters that appear in earlier altars will reappear but give 40% reduced tribute per reappearance.
The reward penalty is additive. The first time a monster is summoned it gives 100% tribute, on the next ritual it gives 60%, then 20% on the third, and finally no tribute on its fourth ritual.
If a naturally generated unique monster, including the map boss, spawns and dies within the ritual altar's influence, it will spawn in subsequent rituals. (with less tribute rewarded each time)
Clicking the altar displays the Ritual Favours interface that allows players to select their rewards. Some rewards are hidden and will be revealed after more rituals on the same map are completed.
Players can then move to other areas of the Map and complete all the altars to unlock more rewards.
Small, moving blood pools will appear under killed enemies that count towards the ritual when activated. Luring monsters into a ritual circle will not add them to the encounter (except the map bosses); they must have alrea
title: Ritual

text:
r killed enemies that count towards the ritual when activated. Luring monsters into a ritual circle will not add them to the encounter (except the map bosses); they must have already been tied to that ritual when the map was opened. Monsters spawned by shrines, Delirium, Legion, Niko encounters, Tormented Spirits, Rogue Exiles, and Hunted Traitors can be revived by a ritual if they spawn near an altar. Other monsters from league mechanics cannot be revived.
The amount of tribute earned from killing the monsters during the encounter depends on the monster's rarity, and how many times it has appeared in a ritual in the current map:
title: Ritual

text:
It is important to note that the rarities of monsters spawned at a ritual altar is not always equivalent to the rarities of monsters that were killed for that ritual. (i.e. even if you kill exclusively normal monsters before activating the ritual altar, the ritual encounter itself will still be able to spawn magic or rare monsters. Likewise, the monster modifiers of slain magic or rare monsters are not preserved when revived in a ritual.)
Summoned minions (e.g. Undead minions spawned by Necromancers or adds spawned by map bosses) do not get added to the monster pool, and minions summoned during an encounter provide no tribute when killed.
 Players can use the Ritual Rewards button to view the number of rituals in the area, number of completed rituals and the reward pool.

== Rewards ==

After completing a ritual, players can click the Altar to display the Favours interface that allows players to select their own rewards, in exchange for Tribute points. Tribute points do not carry over between zones; if you can't afford an item, you can Defer the item to pay part of its cost (with fees) and have it appear again later.
title: Ritual

text:
All items are identified and players can see the exact mods and rolls of the item before selecting the reward. (Veiled mods can only be unveiled after purchase)
After a reward is selected and withdrawn, it cannot be returned/refunded.
All of the altars in the area are part of the same set, and share the same pool of rewards.
Completing a single ritual will only reveal 1/2 or 1/3 of the possible rewards, completing all of them reveals all rewards.
Rewards can be rerolled for 2,000 tribute points. === Deferring rewards ===
Deferring allows players to mark rare rewards that they cannot presently afford with the Tribute they have, and those same items will re-appear in a later ritual.
title: Ritual

text:
Players must pay 10% of the original cost + a 5% additional deferral fee (before atlas modifiers) to defer that item. Both fees are relative to the original cost, with some rounding applied.
The original cost is the initial cost of an item before it is deferred once, not the current cost of the item. So deferring an item will always cost the same, even when it shows up again.
Deferring an item will always be more costly than just buying it outright because of the 5% deferral fee.
Deferred items will appear in future ritual windows, discounted by 10% of its original cost per deferral.
It is currently undetermined how long it takes for deferred items to show back up; however, more valuable items may take longer to reappear.
An item can be deferred 9-10 times (10 times sometimes with rounding) until the cost is under 10% of the original; after this point, players will receive an error message stating that the item deferring failed because the cost is too low.
Each time a deferred item appears in the rewards window and is not deferred again, the next time it appears its cost will increase by 10% of its original cost, nullifying one deferral. Once an item reaches its original cost, it will appear with a red border; if not deferred at this point, it will disappear from the deferred rewards pool.
You can infinitely ping-pong an item by deferring it and then not deferring it, alternating times. While this is inefficient, it might be necessary to reserve another good item due to a lack of tribute.
There is a maximum amount of 50 items that can be deferred at one time. Once the maxim
title: Ritual

text:
is inefficient, it might be necessary to reserve another good item due to a lack of tribute.
There is a maximum amount of 50 items that can be deferred at one time. Once the maximum is reached, a deferred reward must be obtained or removed from the pool to defer additional items.
The pool of deferred items is not shared between characters; each character has an independent deferred item pool.
Deferring is available starting from zone level 46. In practice, this only affects the Ritual encounter in Act 2.
It is recommended to keep at least 2000 tribute after rerolling a window to be able to ensure the most expensive rewards can be deferred, which is approximately 20,000 tribute at original cost.

== Ritual variations ==
Ritual Altars spawn in various types, listed below. Each type has different modifiers, giving a different set of buffs to enemies and environment effects.
Altars which use the Gore Portal EffectGore Portal EffectPortalThis character's portals use the Gore effect. model, are surrounded by a fence, and change the hue of the environment when active are considered "Ritual Altars with Special Rewards", or a "Special Ritual". These rituals have rewards all of the same type per reward window refresh, either all Unique items, currency, or divination cards except the Vaal Ritual, which alters the rewards in a different way.
The Nameless Ritual can appear in Tier 14+ Maps and is also considered a Special Ritual. Unlike the other Special Rituals, however, it has a unique, taller version of a regular altar, and the King in the Mists's voicelines are played when interacting with these rituals. Additionally, its rewards are exclusively a guaranteed An Audience With The KingAn Audience With The KingOn the edge of existence,he watches with ire.Open a portal to the Crux of Nothingness by using this item in a personal Map Device. Settlers league was a challenge league. It launched on July 26, 2024 as part of Path of Exile: Settlers of Kalguur in version 3.25.0. It ended on June 9, 2025.
Settlers league was extended multiple times due to the release of Early Access for Path of Exile 2, causing it to be the longest league to date at over 45 weeks. There have been a few events held during its extended period; the Necro Settlers event was held from November 2024 to February 2025, and the Legacy of Phrecia event was held immediately after until April 23. A special set of private leagues were also made available during May.

== League mechanic ==
Players will assist characters from Kalguur to construct the town of Kingsmarch and establish a shipping trade route between Wraeclast and Kalguur. The player can collect GoldGoldStack Size: 50000Can be spent at Vendors from enemies and loot containers, which are used to fund construction projects and pay workers in Kingsmarch. Many of the activities in Kingsmarch use real-life timers.

=== Workers ===
Kingsmarch requires paid workers to operate its main functions. The hiring process is done through Raulf, the Recruiter, who will provide a list of random workers with varying specialty levels. You can refresh the worker stock by paying Gold. You can also fire workers via Raulf.
Workers have a initial recruitment fee and their hourly wages. Idle workers do not drain funds if there is no work for them.
title: Settlers league

text:
=== Resources ===
Resources are used for town upgrades and shipment. Each resources will be collected over time, with higher level workers increasing the rate of collection. There are four different types of resources:

Ores: Raw material can be extracted from mineral deposits located in zones. You must then have workers on Mining to extract the resources from the deposits.
Bars: Smelters will turn mined ores into bars. Bars are worth more than ores in shipments.
Crops: Workers assigned to Farming will generate crops as long as their wages are being paid.
Thaumaturgic Dust: Rog will take items to be converted into Thaumaturgic Dust over time. The rate at which the equipments are disenchanted scales with worker Disenchanter levels.

=== Shipment ===
Resources can be sent in shipments to different locations, which will make its trip to the location within the allotted time and return with loot. The rewards received from shipments depends on the shipment value and resources sent. The more valuable the shipment, the more Risk is generated, which have a chance to trigger a negative effect, such as losing workers or decreasing shipment value. Loading in workers with higher Shipping level decreases the amount of Risk generated.

=== Atlas Runners ===

Once you've constructed a Kalguuran Map Device, you can hire Atlas Runners to run maps and collect items from them. The amount of items received and the chance of a worker dying scales with the workers' Mapping level. Multiple maps can be queued on the Map Device.

=== Services ===

==== Runesmithing ====

text:
Runesmithing allows you to add an enchantment modifier to non-unique weapons using runes received from shipments to Kalguuran regions.

==== Recombination ====

The Recombinator allows you to spend Gold and Thaumaturgic Dust to reforge two different equipment into a single item with a combination of mods from both items.

==== Currency Exchange Market ====

Faustus, the Financier can give you access to the Currency Exchange Market, allowing you to buy and sell currency, fragments, and more between players asynchronously. A Gold fee is charged with each transaction.

==== Respecialisation ====
Faustus, the Financier can respec skills on your passive skill tree for a Gold fee. Ascendancy passive skills will cost ten times more Gold to respec.

==== Black Market ====
Faustus, the Financier can sell you an equipment of random rarity for Gold.

In the great majority of cases, a monster's ailment threshold is equal to its maximum life. It primarily differs for especially high-life monsters (such as The Shaper), where the threshold is reduced to allow ailments to be applied with hits that wouldn't ordinarily reach the required life thresholds. Playtesting estimates the ailment threshold on Sirus, the Awakener of Worlds to be 25 million damage, or approximately 35% of boss life.

Spell Suppression is a type of mitigation associated with dexterity. By default, it provides a chance to lower the damage of hits and ailments inflicted by spells by 40%.

== Mechanics ==
Characters do not have any base chance to suppress spells. It can be obtained from various sources, typically associated with dexterity or evasion: for example from passive skills in the Shadow/Ranger areas of the passive tree, rolled randomly on evasion armour, and directly from dexterity with the Magebane keystone. 
Spell suppression rolls its chance per spell hit. It can be stacked to 100%, guaranteeing suppression. The spell damage prevented is normally 40%, which can be raised by Prevent +#% of Suppressed Spell Damage. The same multiplier applies to the DPS of damaging ailments, relevantly Ignite and Poison, as Bleeding cannot be applied by spells. Secondary damage caused by spells is also mitigated by spell suppression.
Spell suppression occurs toward the end of mitigation, after resistances and damage reduction, but before stun and block.

Whenever a player or monster is hit, there is a chance they will be stunned. A stun interrupts whatever that creature was doing while a brief animation is played.

== Mechanics ==
Hits have a chance to stun based on their damage compared to the target's maximum life. The base duration of the stun animation is 350ms.

Stun is determined before damage is prevented by block. When a blocked hit stuns, a block animation is performed instead.
Recovering from stun does not prevent a new stun. Many enemy bosses cannot be stunned while stunned and for 4 seconds after a stun ends, however.
Damage over time, reflected damage, and self-damage cannot stun.
Critical strikes that result in cold damage being taken may fail to stun under certain conditions. For details see Stun § Interaction with cold damage crits.
Hits that Freeze but are not critical strikes with cold damage can stun normally. "On stunning" and "when stunned" effects will occur immediately. Characters will not perform the stun animation until action speed allows, typically after unfreezing.
Certain monster skills are not able to stun at all, typically skills that hit rapidly in a barrage or an area.
Picking up an item grants a brief immunity to stun.

text:
== Exceptional support gems ==

Exceptional support gems are special endgame versions of support gems that can be obtained from endgame encounters and bosses, unlocked after defeating the Incarnations during the quest Threads of the Originator for the first time. They can be "Greater" variants of existing support gems, enhancing their effects in interesting ways, or may be completely unique support effects. If they are "Greater" versions, they are mutually exclusive with their regular counterparts and only the exceptional version will apply, if possible. Exceptional supports have a default maximum gem level of 3 and require significantly more experience to level up. Exceptional support gems cannot be purchased from a vendor and must be obtained through specific methods.

== Awakened support gems ==

Awakened support gems are a sunsetted system of endgame support gems prior to the rework of exception support gems. They could originally be obtained from Maven-witnessed map bosses, Maven's Invitations, and the Maven herself as a pinnacle boss. Currently, most of them are considered legacy items and can only be traded for in permanent leagues, with the exception of awakened exceptional support gems listed above.
They are considered the same gem as their non-awakened counterparts. If a skill gem is simultaneously supported by an awakened support and its non-awakened counterpart, only the awakened support gem's effects will apply, if possible.

text: == Mechanics ==
title: Synthesised item

text:
Synthesised items are items with one to three Synthesised implicit modifiers. Except the implicit, a synthesised item has the same defences, APS or damage values as the normal base, as well as attribute requirements. They also have "Synthesised" as a prefix of their name, as well as  symbol in front and at the back of their name.
Corrupted implicits may replace Synthesised implicits through corruption. Each corrupted implicit replaces one Synthesised implicit; items can have a mix of both.
Like other modifiers, it is possible for a Synthesised implicit modifier to change an item's required level if the 80% of the implicit's item level requirement is higher than the item's default required level (e.g. a synthesised implicit modifier requiring Level 56 to roll will add a required Level of 44). Conversely, for most jewellery or quivers, if a Synthesised implicit's required level is lower than the item's default level, it can lower the default required level of the item (though it will still be restricted by the required level of explicit modifiers).
Synthesised items can be enchanted, which doesn't affect implicits.
A normal Synthesised item cannot be turned into a unique item using an Orb of ChanceOrb of ChanceStack Size: 20Upgrades a normal item to a random rarityRight click this item then left click a normal item to apply it..
It is impossible to create influenced Synthesised items. For example, players cannot use Elderslayer's Exalted Orb on Synthesised items.
Synthesised items cannot have a fractured modifier. Fracturing Orbs cannot be used on Synthesised items.

== Synthesis process ==

=== Current ===
Harvest crafting allows transforming of items into Synthesised items: the original base changes into corresponding Synthesised base, random Synthesis implicits are added and if any implicits were present on the original item they are removed. Synthesised items cannot have influences or be fractured.
Beastcrafting with a Vivid Vulture allows the rerolling of a Synthesis implicit modifier.

== Synthesised implicit modifiers ==

Synthesised implicit modifiers replace any implicit modifiers that items have normally.

These items were not deleted after the hotfix and are now legacy variant items that can only be obtained through trade.

A temporal incursion is a short-duration visit to the past wherein two Vaal architects are vying for control of a room within the Temple of Atzoatl. The objective is to murder one of the architects so that the other can prevail, thereby altering the Temple in the present time.

== Access ==
After meeting her in Act 7, Alva Valai will have a chance to spawn in most zones, allowing the player to enter three Incursions - There will be three separate entrance points throughout any map she spawns in. She does not spawn in side areas or if the zone is more than 10 levels lower than the level of the player. Alva can also appear in maps. You can increase the chance of an Alva encounter appearing with related Atlas passive tree nodes.
Each time players encounter Alva Valai in the wilderness, she can open a time portal, allowing a visit to an incursion room in the ancient Vaal Temple of Atzoatl during its construction.
During the Incursion League, she would appear in almost every zone, but would only allow access to one Incursion per zone as opposed to the current three.

== Incursion rooms ==

Players have a short time, initially 10 seconds, to spend in each temporal incursion. During this time, they can (in descending order of priority):
title: Temporal incursion

text:
Kill one of two Vaal Architects who guide the temple's construction. This will either change the room in the present-day Temple of Atzoatl to a different type with the surviving architect's theme, or upgrade it to the second or third tier of the same theme and improve rewards. Damaging the Architect extends the incursion duration.
Pick up a Stone of PassageStone of PassageThis item can be placed into an Altar of Passage to create a connection between two adjacent rooms in the Temple of Atzoatl. This can be traded, stashed, or placed in the Relic Altar to continue the Sanctum run. All of your progress, including Resolve, Inspiration, Aureus, Boons, Afflictions, etc. are carried over between floors. A Sanctum run contains 4 floors, each containing 8 rooms. The 8th room of each floor always contains a Boss. Each floor after the first also adds +1 to area level from the initial Forbidden Tome (up to +3 on the last floor), up to a maximum of area level 83.
Crashing during a Sanctum room will reset the room's progress, as long as the player did not fail the room due to resolve loss. However, any changes to your resolve and inspiration during the room's progress will be retained. Aureus and rewards are locked in upon successful completion of a room. It is possible to return back into the room from the reward room to kill any remaining enemies or ope
