tained. Aureus and rewards are locked in upon successful completion of a room. It is possible to return back into the room from the reward room to kill any remaining enemies or open aureus chests. 
Each Sanctum run is independent between characters on the same account.
title: The Forbidden Sanctum

text:
== Relic Altar ==
The Relic Altar is unlocked in Act 10 after unlocking the Forbidden Sanctum through the quest Aiding an Archivist.
Each character has its own Relic Altar and uses separate Relics. However, the Relic Locker is shared between all of your characters in the same league.
Relics placed in the Relic Altar are locked in for the entire Sanctum run as soon as they are confirmed and cannot be added or removed in the middle of a run. The current run must be completed, failed, or forfeited to add or remove Relics.
The Relic Altar contains 18 inventory spaces, but 12 are initially locked and can be obtained by defeating specific minibosses or floor bosses.

=== Unlocking ===
Locked inventory spaces for the Relic Altar can be unlocked by completing various rooms or floors in the Forbidden Sanctum.

== Mechanics ==
title: The Forbidden Sanctum

text:
=== Resolve ===
Resolve is an additional stat player characters have while exploring the Sanctum, somewhat similar to Ruin from Ultimatum league.
The default maximum Resolve is 300. Resolve is maintained between rooms, and the player is ejected from the Sanctum if it hits 0, resetting all floors and rooms. Being ejected does not count as a death, nor does it remove experience.
Resolve is lost from hits from monsters or traps in the Sanctum. Closer proximity to monsters reduces the Resolve lost on hit.
Minions and non-party allies do not cause Resolve to be lost if hit.
A fixed amount of Resolve can be restored in Fountain rooms.
Gaining additional Maximum Resolve will also cause the character to gain current Resolve of the same amount. Losing Maximum Resolve will not further affect the current Resolve.
Accursed Pacts that cause you to Lose #% Maximum Resolve and the Minor Affliction "Spiked Exit" can be safely taken even with only 1 Maximum Resolve, and will have no effect (they cannot fail a run by itself).
Maximum Resolve is soft capped at 1000; however, it is possible to exceed these values from sources that modify maximum Resolve at the start of a room/floor.

==== Resolve defences ====

Defensive mechanics such as evade/dodge chance, damage reduction, block, spell suppression, and avoidance do not directly affect the loss of Resolve. However, the primary defence stats scale certain Resolve-specific defences found exclusively in the Sanctum:
title: The Forbidden Sanctum

text:
Resolve Mitigation: Mitigation prevents a portion of Resolve loss and scales with your Armour. #% Resolve Mitigation from Enemy Hits
Resolve mitigation scales approximately logarithmically, up to 40% at ~3 million armour.
Resolve Avoidance: This scales with your Evasion Rating. #% chance to Avoid Resolve loss from Enemy Hits
Resolve avoidance scales approximately logarithmically, up to 40% at ~3 million evasion rating.
Resolve Aegis: Up to 50% of Resolve loss from Enemy Hits is removed from the Aegis before Resolve or Inspiration. Aegis is broken when any Resolve is lost from Enemy hits. Aegis is instantly restored after 4 seconds of no Resolve being lost. Resolve Aegis scales with your maximum Energy Shield. # Resolve Aegis
Resolve aegis scales approximately logarithmically, up to ~65 at ~160 thousand energy shield.

=== Aureus ===
Aureus is a type of non-tradeable currency similar to Azurite which can be found in the Sanctum from chests or from killed enemies. Aureus is collected automatically when the player is near it.
Aureus can be traded to the merchant for a small amount of Resolve recovery, various Boons, or relics.
Aureus is maintained between rooms and floors, and is reset when the Sanctum run ends.
Aureus drops from Templar Stash chests, as well as from Guards and Bosses when killed.
Half of your current Aureus can be converted into gold at the Gilded Font at the end of each floor. The conversion ratio increases at higher levels.
title: The Forbidden Sanctum

text:
=== Inspiration ===
Inspiration acts as a buffer over your maximum Resolve, somewhat similar to Energy Shield in comparison to life.
Inspiration cannot be recovered like Resolve.
Inspiration is soft capped at 1000; however, it is possible to exceed these values from sources that modify Inspiration at the start of a room/floor.

=== Boon ===
Above your inspiration bar, major boons are grouped in a symbol with a very thick and bright yellow bordered boon symbol, while all minor boons are grouped in a plain yellow bordered boon symbol. Boons are shown when hovering the according symbol.
Boons grant various benefits to your Sanctum run and can help recover or mitigate damage to your Resolve, increase your Aureus and rewards, debuff monsters, grant Inspiration, or provide other helpful buffs.

=== Affliction ===
Above your inspiration bar, major afflictions are grouped in a symbol with a very thick and bright purple bordered boon symbol, while all minor afflictions are grouped in a plain purple bordered affliction symbol. Afflictions are shown when hovering according symbol.
Afflictions grant various downsides to your Sanctum run and can reduce or prevent Resolve recovery, spawn additional traps, buff monsters, affect your Aureus generation, or hide rooms or rewards on the Sanctum Map.

== Room layouts ==

See the above link for annotated minimaps of each room type, including enemy locations and shortcuts. Each room other than the miniboss room contains several Guard unique monsters, as well as one of three tasks to complete the room:
title: The Forbidden Sanctum

text:
Find the Exit (locate the exit door)
Linear: The exit door is located at the the end of a series of traps.
Four corners: The exit door is located randomly in one of four directions on the map.
Defeat all the Guards (defeat every rare monster and Unique Guard)
Arena: Guards will spawn in waves in a small arena with traps.
Linear: Guards are located in packs along a set path.
Defeat the Boss (defeat minibosses based on map bosses)

Note: most "Find the Exit" rooms have shortcuts that require movement skills.

== Room Reward Types ==
Note: All room types other than boss rooms can become Afflicted. Afflicted rooms are indicated by a purple border and cause the character to gain an Affliction on entry.

=== Item Reward Room ===
 When players are offered rewards, they have three options:
title: The Forbidden Sanctum

text:
Receive #x <item1> now
Receive #x <item2> at end of the Floor ("at end of the next Floor" if on room 8)
Receive #x <item3> on completing the Sanctum
The quantity and/or types of items improve based on the area level of the zone, the current floor, and how long you defer the reward, at the cost of risking the reward entirely if the player fails the run. Item chests have a 5 Aureus fee to open.
Rarer currency items like Mirror of KalandraMirror of KalandraStack Size: 10Creates a mirrored copy of an itemRight click this item then left click an equipable non-unique item to apply it. Mirrored copies cannot be modified., Divine OrbDivine OrbStack Size: 20Randomises the values of the random modifiers on an itemRight click this item then left click a magic, rare or unique item to apply it., Exalted OrbExalted OrbStack Size: 20Augments a rare item with a new random modifierRight click this item then left click a rare item to apply it. Rare items can have up to six random modifiers., and Sacred OrbSacred OrbStack Size: 10Randomises the numeric values of base defences on an armourRight click this item then left click an armour to apply it. become available on Floor 3 and 4. These items can only appear as a stack of 1 on Floor 3.

=== Treasure Reward Room ===
 Contains chests of Aureus; comes in 2 types: Minor Treasure Reward (2 chests) or Major Treasure Reward (5 chests).

=== Fountain ===
 Fountain rooms contain an interactable Fountain which grants Recover 25% of Maximum Resolve for a 5 Aureus fee.
title: The Forbidden Sanctum

text:
==== Benevolent Fountain ====
 Benevolent Fountain rooms contain an interactable Benevolent Fountain which grants Gain a Random Boon for a 150 Aureus fee.

==== Afflicted Fountain ====
 Afflicted Fountain rooms contain an interactable Afflicted Fountain which grants Recover 50% of Maximum Resolve, but also inflicts a random minor Affliction on you, for a 5 Aureus fee.

==== Radiant Fountain ====
 Radiant Fountain rooms contain an interactable Radiant Fountain which grants a random Boon, removes a random Affliction, and grants 200 Inspiration for a 5 Aureus fee. Rerolls Afflictions on Afflicted Rooms on the current floor if an Affliction was removed.

=== Merchant ===
 Merchant rooms contain the NPC Divinia who sells you Boons or relics in exchange for Aureus. She can also recover 50 Resolve once per encounter for a 200 Aureus fee.

=== Accursed Pact ===
 Accursed Pact rooms allow you to accept any of three random Accursed Pacts which grants both an upside and downside, as well as an item reward upon accepting at least 1 Accursed Pact.

The options that state "Lose #% Maximum Resolve" will not fail the run if Maximum Resolve is 1.
Attempting to use the Gain 200 Inspiration, Lose 200 Resolve Pact when you have less than 200 Resolve will cause an error, stating "Not enough Resolve".

=== Boss Room ===
 Always the 8th room of any floor.

== Enemies ==
Each room in the Sanctum contains a number of normal and rare enemies. All rare enemies must be killed before being able to complete the room.
title: The Forbidden Sanctum

text:
=== Sanctum Guards ===
Each room contains several unique Sanctum Guards. All Guards must be killed before being able to complete the room.

Minibosses and bosses drop a large quantity of Aureus and have an increased chance to drop relics.
Killing each miniboss and boss for the first time unlocks several tiles in the Relic Altar.
Boss rooms contain a chest for any accumulated Item Rewards for the floor, as well as two additional Item Reward chests. Lycia's room only contains the accumulated Item Rewards chest.

After defeating Lycia's first form, the player can enter a portal to an arena called The Beyond to face her second form. Both forms must be defeated to access the reward chest
Lycia's second form eliminates the Resolve bar and no longer uses Resolve mechanics. Dying during the second form will count as a failed run and prevent looting of the final reward chest.
Lycia, Herald of the Scourge in "The Beyond" will always drop a Unique Relic, as well as a chance to drop one of her exclusive items:

text:
=== Relics ===

Relics are a type of item that is exclusive to the Sanctum league. They can be placed in the Relic Altar to provide buffs to various mechanics related to the Forbidden Sanctum.

Relics can be found in the Sanctum as rewards from guards, minibosses or bosses, or purchased from Divinia for 300 Aureus.
They can be stored in a special separate stash, which can also be placed as a hideout decoration.
To equip a Relic, they must be placed in the Relic Altar on a 5x4 grid with two of the corner slots blocked off. Additional grid slots can be unlocked as you progress, up to a total of 18 slots.
Relics are unmodifiable and always drops as Magic or Unique. They cannot be Rare.
Relics of the same base can be vendored 5 to 1 to obtain a new one with random modifiers.

Totems are a type of creature. They can appear as both monsters and as allies, and are a type of proxy when summoned by skills.

== Mechanics ==
Totems are damageable objects. They have their own resources (e.g. life) and stats (e.g. resistance, action speed). They die when their life is reduced to zero, and do not leave corpses.

=== Offensive stats ===
Totems are a type of proxy: a separate object that has access to one of the player's skills. The player's skill is used with the player's stats, not the totem's. This means:
title: Totem

text:
Totems use all of the player’s stats that affect their skills, including damage, area of effect, speed, on-hit effects, and modifiers that apply or modify debuffs. While totems are not 'you', many stats worded as 'you' or 'your' still apply to the skill used by a totem.
Totems do not snapshot: any changes to the player’s stats immediately affect skills used by totems.
Totem’s own offensive stats never affect the skill they use. In many cases, totems are prevented from gaining their own offensive modifiers to avoid confusion, as they would not be functional. They cannot gain rage, frenzy or power charges, offensive buffs, and are ignored by offensive auras.
In the rare case a totem deals damage outside its skill, like Hinekora, Death's Fury's on-totem-kill explosion, that damage will not scale with the player's stats. (Not to be confused with Totems Explode on Death effects, which is damage from the player.)

text:
Transfigured skill gems are alternate versions of existing skill gems, denoted by having "of X" as a suffix that alters its function and balance. While they are technically the same item as their default versions, they can often drastically change the identity of the skill, even changing its gem tags and mechanics.

== Overview ==
Transfigured gems that have been corrupted to grant a Vaal skill will provide the transfigured base skill and Vaal skill. Vaal versions of skills do not have transfigurations.
Trigger cooldowns are shared between multiple skills of the same type, which include their regular versions and alternate versions such as transfigured and Trarthan gems.
Skill microtransactions are compatible with their respective transfigured versions.
Within stash tabs, transfigured gems can be searched by searching for "transfigured" or any set of characters composing the word, including "trans" or "sfi".

== Acquisition ==
Transfigured skill gem can be acquired from these sources:

Using the Divine Font at the end of the Labyrinth allows players to obtain transfigured gems with varying degrees of randomness. This is the case for most skill gems.
The Fortification Syndicate Safehouse with Tora stationed contains a trapped chest that can contain transfigured gems.
In The Tunnel in Act 9, there is an unmarked lever inside the Trial of Ascendancy (around the last third of the gauntlet) that opens a secret room containing a chest that drops a random transfigured gem (once per character).

== List of transfigured skill gems ==
title: Transfigured skill gem

text:
There are 197 transfigured skill gems, of which there are 35 red, 75 green, and 87 blue gems.

== Version history ==
The transfigured gem system, introduced in 3.23, replaced three older systems  that enhanced or altered the effects of skills: alternate quality gems, labyrinth helmet enchantments, and unique threshold jewels. It also took, or took inspiration, from prior league systems, such as 3.21's Crucible Passive Tree notables.

== Support gems ==
Some traps store limited uses and replenish one use after a cooldown period. A counter is shown on the skill icon which indicates how many uses are currently stored.
There are currently 8 support skill gems with the Trap gem tag:

=== Targeting ===
When using trap skill gems the character will throw whichever variant of the skill is equipped. In this respect aiming can be achieved by moving the mouse over the area where damage is required. This is the only way that the trap's damage can be selectively applied as upon detonation the trap's area of effect is what determines the damage radius.

=== Interaction with player stats and support gems ===
Traps and mines act much like totems in that when they cast their payload, it is the trap/mine that casts the skill, not the player. This means:
title: Trap

text:
==== Leech ====
Leeching: Players cannot leech health or mana via traps. The trap/mine is actually doing the leeching, but they self-destruct after they're triggered, so leeching has no practical effect.

==== Reflection ====
Damage reflection: Damage is reflected back to the traps/mines and not the player, so they are safe to use on damage reflecting monsters, maps, or PvP targets.

==== Trigger Conditions ====
Trigger gems: Traps and mines (and totems) will not work with "Cast on..." trigger gems, even if the trap/mine has a "Spell" type gem tag/keyword; the player places or throws the trap/mine, but the trap/mine is doing the actual spell-casting.

Trarthan gems are alternate versions of existing skill gems, denoted by having "of Trarthus" as a suffix that alters its function and balance. While they are technically the same item as their default versions, they can often drastically change the identity of the skill, even changing its gem tags and mechanics.
They are functionally similar to transfigured gems.

== Overview ==
Trarthan gems that have been corrupted to grant a Vaal skill will provide the Trarthan base skill and regular Vaal skill. Vaal versions of skills do not have Trarthan variations.
Trigger cooldowns are shared between multiple skills of the same type, including any transfigurations.
Skill microtransactions are compatible with their respective Trarthan versions.

== Acquisition ==
Trarthan gems can be found in Heist large chests that contain Gem rewards.
In Mercenaries league, Trarthan gems could be obtained by taking the gem from a mercenary with the gem offered as a reward after winning a duel.

== List of Trarthan gems ==

There are 12 Trarthan skill gems.

== Version history ==
During Mercenaries league, Trarthan gems could be obtained by winning a duel with a mercenary equipped with one.

The Trials of Chaos, also known as Ultimatum, is a league mechanic introduced with the Ultimatum leagues. It was added to the core game in Version 3.23.0.

== Mechanics ==
The Trialmaster and an altar can be found in The Vaal City and The Temple of Decay Level 1 in Act 7. It has an 8% chance to spawn in maps. The altar displays a reward, the objective, and three modifiers to choose from. The player must select a modifier before beginning the trial.
There are four possible objectives:
title: Ultimatum

text:
Defeat waves of enemies: Kill enemies to fill up a progress bar.
Survive: Don't die until the 15 second timer runs out. Monsters enrage if left alive for too long.
Stand in Stone Circles: Stand in each stone circle for a duration until they light up.
Protect the Altar: Kill enemies to fill up a progress bar without letting the altar be destroyed. The altar recovers part of its life between rounds.
After successfully completing a round, the encounter is frozen in time, and the player is offered two choices: end the trial and receive the accumulated rewards, or aim for more rewards and start the next round by selecting a new modifier to add.
If the player's character dies, stays outside of the circle for too long, or receives 7 stacks of Ruin, the Ultimatum is failed and all rewards will be removed. The Altar being destroyed in "Protect the Altar" encounters also is considered a fail state.
Each trial has 10 rounds. In Tier 14+ maps (area level 81+), upon starting the final round, there is a chance (~3% ) you will get teleported into the Trial of Ordeals' arena and face the Trialmaster as a boss. According to the game files, in addition to the Ultimatum modifiers selected each round, monsters gain hidden stackable multipliers to life and damage: 15% more life each round after the first up to round 10, which is multiplicative per round, increasing to 35% more for the three rounds added by Gruelling Gauntlet, and an additive 5% increased damage per round up to round 10, then 15% increased for Gruelling Gauntlet rounds.

text:
=== Partying ===
When facing a Trial of Chaos with other players, each player will be offered their own individual set of rewards. When an individual player fails the trial, they will lose their rewards but the trial will continue with the remaining players.
In between waves, the players will vote on which modifier to add to the next wave. The one with the most votes gets added. In case of ties, a mod is randomly chosen between them. Players have a limited time to vote, but the timer is paused if at least one party member is not present in the zone.

A unique item is an item with a specific name, unique artwork, and a predetermined list of modifiers. Unique items usually have the same implicit modifier as a normal item of the same type.
Unique items are meant to be less powerful overall than high-level rare items, but offer unique gameplay and allow special character builds to be based around them.
Currently there are 1,189 released unique items, including maps and items with modifier variants. For a timeline when each unique item was added, see the timeline of unique items.
This list does not include unique strongboxes and Vaal side areas.

== Unique item types ==

== Obtaining unique items ==
The following is a non-exhaustive list of ways that unique items can be obtained. Unique items can always be traded.

The actual drop levels of unique items are not known; however, there are examples of unique items that are known to only drop from very high level content, such as maps. Each unique item also has its own drop rate. These rates are not publicized by Grinding Gear Games, but certain unique items are clearly much more common than others.
Optional content: Optional game content is a prevalent source of unique items. Random unique item drops are often given to the player as reward for engaging with certain optional game content such as Heist, the Immortal Syndicate and the Lord's Labyrinth just to name a few. text:
== Legacy variants ==
Like all items, unique items can have legacy variants. This means for some uniques there exist better (or worse) versions that aren't dropping anymore in Standard leagues. The main source of legacy items are nerfs that affect future item drops, but leave the already existing items as they were. The only way to get these legacy items is from players who had them before they were changed.
Rerolling the item's modifier values with a Divine OrbDivine OrbStack Size: 20Randomises the values of the random modifiers on an itemRight click this item then left click a magic, rare or unique item to apply it. may change a mod's values to match the current version of the unique item, but not for all of them. It will not add or remove modifiers that have been adjusted since then as well.
title: Unique item

text:
== Other information ==
A unique item, easily spotted by its orange text and orange banner, as well as a distinct sound affect and animation upon monster drop is one that always spawns with the same mods (sometimes with different values) on the same base item with the same requirements.
Mirrors of KalandraMirror of KalandraStack Size: 10Creates a mirrored copy of an itemRight click this item then left click an equipable non-unique item to apply it. Mirrored copies cannot be modified. and Orbs of ScouringOrb of ScouringStack Size: 30Removes all modifiers from an itemRight click this item then left click on a magic or rare item to apply it. cannot be used on unique items. The only way to downgrade a unique is to use a Vaal OrbVaal OrbStack Size: 20Corrupts an item, modifying it unpredictablyRight click this item then left click an item to corrupt it. Corrupted items cannot be modified again. on it, which can turn it into a corrupted rare item.
Event prize unique items were given out during old race events to select top players and new copies cannot be obtained in-game by any other method.
Unique items with alternate 2D artworks were given out as prizes for races.
Foil uniques are variants with alternate "holographic" 2D artworks. They are obtained using a Reliquary Key, which very rarely drop in-game, some only for a limited time. Certain supporter packs allows the buyer to add a foil unique of their choosing into the game, obtainable through special items.
Foulborn unique items are special variants of unique items which have at least one of its usual modifiers replaced with
title: Unique item

text:
r choosing into the game, obtainable through special items.
Foulborn unique items are special variants of unique items which have at least one of its usual modifiers replaced with a similar Foulborn modifier.
It is possible to get an influenced version of a unique item (for unique items that do not normally drop influenced) by using an Orb of ChanceOrb of ChanceStack Size: 20Upgrades a normal item to a random rarityRight click this item then left click a normal item to apply it. on an influenced version of the base item.
It is impossible to transform a non-unique fractured or synthesised item or an item with an Eldritch implicit modifier into a unique item.
The item level of the unique affects how many sockets can appear on it. While the stats may be the same a unique with a high item level may have a higher selling price when trading with other players.
There are different tiers of unique items. On drop, the rarity roll determines not only if the item will be unique but also from which tier. A random unique will then be pick from the determined tier's pool. When chancing, the probability of obtaining each tier is fixed. If there is no unique of the rolled tier or lower, a rare will be chanced instead.

text:
== Unique items designed by supporters ==

During the Closed Beta phase of Path of Exile's development, supporters of the game that purchased the Diamond supporter pack were given the opportunity to collaborate on the design of a unique item. For a period of time at the start of the Open Beta, Grinding Gear Games offered supporters a unique item design opportunity as a standalone purchase. Once the Open Beta supporter packs were made available, Eternal and Ruler of Wraeclast supporters were likewise also given the opportunity to design a unique item.

Many unique items can have several variants. These variants can be categorized into several categories, which also affect their generation and method of acquisition. Variants are distinctly different items from each other, so rerolling their modifier values with a Divine OrbDivine OrbStack Size: 20Randomises the values of the random modifiers on an itemRight click this item then left click a magic, rare or unique item to apply it. will never transform them into another variant. It is possible for an item to both have basetype variants and modifier variants.

== Basetype variant ==
Basetype variants share the same name but have a different base item type.

Doryani's Delusion, Precursor's Emblem, and Grand Spectrum are both basetype variants and modifier variants.
Synthesised uniques and their fractured or regular (obtained via vendor recipe) versions are also considered basetype variants.

=== Non-unique basetype variant ===

== Modifier variant ==
Modifier variants generate with distinct combinations of modifiers and cannot change between or reroll into other variants.
Lord of Steel and Impresence are distinct in having different art for each variant despite having the same basetype and name. They also have individual slots for each unique item art variant in the Unique Collection Tab; the regular Elder and Uber Uber Elder variants of each damage type variant of Impresence share the same slots, however.

== Pseudo-variant ==
Pseudo-variants are sets of items which are distinct and different in name, but are typically treated as variants of the same item.

== Mechanics ==
Vaal skill gems grant both the base version of the skill and the Vaal version of the skill. Anything supported to the Vaal skill gem will apply to both skills, as long as they're applicable.

text:
=== Souls ===
To use a Vaal skill, its gem must first be charged by collecting souls. Souls can be obtained by killing enemies, granting 1 souls per kill. Souls can also be obtained when damaging Rare or Unique enemies (1 or 6 souls, respectively, per 2% life lost with a 1 second cooldown). Life restored by Unique enemies during phase changes (like Sirus and Catarina) will not grant souls, meaning that if Sirus heals from 25% to 75% during his final phase, all damage from 75% to 25% will grant zero souls. 
Each soul gained will charge a random Vaal skill possessed by the player. Souls will never charge a Vaal skill in the character's secondary weapon set. Souls are also tracked per skill, not per gem. In other words, you cannot store multiple charges of the same skill by equipping multiple copies of the Vaal skill gem.
Collected souls cannot be transferred between zone instances; instead, each instance maintains its own soul counter for each gem. Therefore, entering a new instance will start a new counter for each gem but returning to a previously visited instance will restore each counter to its previous value. However, souls will be retained on death. A vaal gem that collected souls in an instance will keep these souls during a gem swap, a drop on the ground, or putting it in the inventory afterwards.
Once a Vaal skill collects a sufficient number of souls, which varies based on the skill, it is charged with one use. Some skills can store enough souls for multiple uses. While the soul requirement has been referred to as a 'Soul Cost' historically, and still is on Shepherd
title: Vaal skill

text:
charged with one use. Some skills can store enough souls for multiple uses. While the soul requirement has been referred to as a 'Soul Cost' historically, and still is on Shepherd of Souls, it is not a cost in the general sense, and is unaffected by generic cost modifiers such as Fanaticism or Tireless. The number on the skill icon indicates how many times the Vaal skill can be used with its current soul cost; it is not the same as cooldown use.
Once a gem's maximum soul capacity is reached, it can collect no additional souls until they are spent by using the skill. Once used, Soul Gain Prevention will be applied, preventing the player from gaining souls globally; the player will not be able to gain any souls for any vaal skill at all, though skills that already had a charge ready may still be used. Soul gain prevention duration varies between skills. It is not inherently a skill effect duration, though many vaal skills do have a modifier that applies skill effect or buff duration modifiers to soul gain prevention. 
Partying: All players near monsters killed gain the same number of vaal souls as if they had killed it alone. Therefore characters who do not kill can still gain vaal souls in a party. In a party all kills by a player with Soul Eater will not give vaal souls to the party.
Soul Eater will prevent solo characters from gaining any vaal souls during the buff effect.

Unmodifiable: Valdo Maps are not affected by the Atlas passive skill tree and cannot be modified with currency items. Map fragments also cannot be used with them when opening the map.
Valdo Maps cannot be used to unlock an additional Map Device slot.
Upon completing the map a Singular Reliquary spawns on the map, which contains the Celestial foil reward. Map completion requires the fulfilment of all of the following conditions:
Kill at least 90% of all monsters of the map, including all rare and unique enemies. In other words, it is not required to kill all of the magic and normal enemies in the map.
Complete any additional objectives required from the map's modifiers.
The relative rarity of the rewarded unique affects the chance for a specific map to be chosen when opening a Valdo's Puzzle Box. Additionally, each map modifier for that particular outcome grants a more/less multiplier to that chance for that outcome. Each multiplier stacks multiplicatively.

=== Modifiers ===
Valdo Maps have several unique modifiers instead of the typical random modifiers maps can roll. These modifiers can grant a chance to convert maps into Guardian maps or scarabs in addition to pack size and item quantity/rarity. These conversions occur before monster modifier conversions. Gain Instability on Kill; Unstable Players eventually detonate: Each enemy killed grants the player a stack of Instability for 3 seconds. The duration refreshes whenever you gain a stack of Instability. If the stack duration reaches 0, an explosion of physical damage occurs on the player, dealing damage based on the number of Instability stacks before expiry. The explosion can also hurt allies.
Players who Die in area are sent to the Void: On death, the player character is permanently dead and sent to the Void league, even on softcore leagues. Voided characters can no longer be accessed in-game. The player is given a warning before entering these maps.

The vendor recipe system allows the player to sell items to any town vendor in exchange for a multitude of currency items and equipment. Each recipe requires semi-specific items or combinations of items be put into the sell window at the same time, and the outcome will change based on any recipes that have been matched. Unless noted otherwise, each item may only be involved in a single recipe at a time.
Items (and their costs) sold by vendors as part of their normal inventory are covered on the vendor page.

== Equipment ==
Unless otherwise stated, the item level and rarity of the item produced are both equal to the lowest item level and rarity among all items required for the recipe.

title: Vendor recipe system

text:
=== Basic crafting ===
The following vendor recipes involve crafting of existing items (see also: crafting) to add or upgrade a specific modifier. 
Beyond that, these recipes are split into two categories: one the creates a new item with a guaranteed modifier, and one that adds a modifier to the existing item.
Some recipes are specific to a certain rarity of target item: if the ingredients do not match the recipe, consider using a currency orb first such as the Orb of Transmutation to make the item into Magic rarity.

==== Create new item ====
All recipes of this type create a new base item (with randomized base defences).

The following are removed: enchantments, Eldritch implicits, Synthesised implicits, Incubators, Crucible passive trees
The following are retained: quality, sockets, links, item level, influences
Fractured items and corrupted items cannot be used as base items for these recipes.

==== Modify existing item ====
All recipes of this type add a modifier to an existing item or alters the item without affecting its other stats.

The following are retained: enchantments, Eldritch implicits, Synthesised implicits, Incubators, Crucible passive trees, base defences, quality, sockets, links, item level, influences
Fractured items and corrupted items items cannot be used as base items for these recipes.

title: Vendor recipe system

text:
==== Crafting ====
The following vendor recipes are used to craft unique items. A vendor recipe is also the only way to obtain most of the unique items on this list, apart from trading with other players.
Using all same-influenced items as input will create an influenced output.

==== Rerolling ====
A unique item can have its modifiers rerolled by vendoring it along with two more of the same unique item. The result is comparable to using a Divine OrbDivine OrbStack Size: 20Randomises the values of the random modifiers on an itemRight click this item then left click a magic, rare or unique item to apply it. and a Blessed OrbBlessed OrbStack Size: 20Randomises the values of the implicit modifiers of an itemRight click this item then left click another item to apply it..

== Sockets ==
These recipes require single items with certain patterns of sockets. These can sometimes be found at vendors and can be immediately resold for a profit.

== Single Item with Mods ==
These recipes result from selling a single item when no other recipes are valid.

=== Scroll Fragment ===
This is the "default" recipe. If an item does not have a more powerful recipe, it defaults to producing a Scroll FragmentScroll FragmentStack Size: 5A stack of 5 fragments becomes a Scroll of Wisdom.. 5 Scroll Fragments automatically combine to form a Scroll of Wisdom.

=== Transmutation Shard ===
Transmutation ShardTransmutation ShardStack Size: 20A stack of 20 shards becomes an Orb of Transmutation.s come from unidentified items. 20 Transmutation Shards automatically combine to form an Orb of Transmutation.

text:
=== Alteration Shard ===
Alteration ShardAlteration ShardStack Size: 20A stack of 20 shards becomes an Orb of Alteration.s come from identified items depending on their affixes. 20 Alteration Shards automatically combine to form an Orb of Alteration. Most affixes sell for Alteration Shards.

=== Alchemy Shard ===
Certain rarer affixes may yield Alchemy ShardAlchemy ShardStack Size: 20A stack of 20 shards becomes an Orb of Alchemy.s instead of Alteration Shards. 20 Alchemy Shards automatically combine to form an Orb of Alchemy.

=== Orb of Augmentation ===
An identified rare item with six affixes can be traded for an Orb of Augmentation. Note that magic items may only have a maximum of two affixes.

=== Orb of Scouring ===

== Quality Items ==
These recipes produce currency items that improve the quality of their category of items. To produce the currency requires either one of the following:

A single normal item (not magic, rare, etc.) of that category with 20% or higher quality;
Several items (any rarity) of that category with a total of at least 40% quality.
When done for multiple instances of the recipe at once, each individual combination must add up to 40%. For example: 6 items of 19%, 13%, 15%, 9%, 17% and 7% quality would add up to 80%, but would not actually grant 2 of the resulting quality items, only 1. This is because the 2 individual combinations do not add up to 40 each.

== Multiple Rare Items ==
These recipes require multiple items, mostly rares.

=== X of a Kind ===
These recipes require multiple identified rare items with the same name.
title: Vendor recipe system

text:
=== Straight Flush ===
These recipes require multiple items of the same base item type (e.g. Recurve Bow), one from each rarity specified. Items that cannot increase in quality, such as jewellery and belts, will never yield Orbs of Alchemy with this recipe.

=== Full Rare Sets ===
These recipes require a full set of rare items. A full set is capable of filling all item slots in the inventory screen (not including flasks, the alternate weapon set, or a quiver). Specifically, it consists of:

One of the following:
1x Two-Handed Weapon (including bows, quiver not required)
1x One-Handed Weapon and 1x Shield
2x One-Handed Weapon
2x Shield
1x Helmet
1x Body Armour
1x Gloves
1x Boots
1x Belt
1x Amulet
2x Ring
The type of currency produced depends on the item with the lowest item level in the set, and the quantity on whether they are all unidentified and/or 20% or higher quality:

Notes:

If a rare item below item level 60 is added to a Chaos Orb recipe then the recipe will change to an Orb of Chance recipe.
If a rare item below item level 75 is added to a Regal Orb recipe then the recipe will change to a Chaos Orb recipe.
Belts, Amulets, and Rings appear to always be seen as 20% quality for this recipe as they do not have any basic quality. As such, they do not require the use of Catalysts.
In Crucible League (v3.21), advancing a weapon's passive skill tree in a crucible event will make that weapon invalid for use in this recipe.

text: Voidborn Reliquary Key is a vault key that grants access to the Voidborn Reliquary, which drops a Foil version of uniques selected by players who have purchased the Voidborn Supporter Pack. There are currently 8559 potential outcomes for this key. It is possible to have multiple entries that award the same foil coloured unique item. Each submission grants the author the option to add custom flavour text for the drop event of the item, but since there is no restrictions on how many times an item and foil combination can be chosen, there are a substantial number of duplicate entries.
title: Voidborn Reliquary Key

text:
== Mechanics ==
Both the Key and the items that drop within it are weighted based on the rarity of items submitted by supporters. Watcher's Eye is a unique Prismatic JewelPrismatic JewelPlace into an allocated Jewel Socket on the Passive Skill Tree. Right click to remove from the Socket.. 
It is one of the few items in the game that are universally usable in all builds, due to the highly useful and variable modifiers it can drop with. These modifiers are often powerful and in some cases not obtainable on other items. Depending on the modifiers' synergy, a Watcher's Eye has the potential to become one of the most valuable items in the game. Additionally, due to it being a unique item, it cannot be duplicated (e.g. mirrored).
